items.stem: Released from rest at the top of a straight steel loading chute of length 3.5 m inclined at 44° to the horizontal, an instrumented cargo crate of mass 16 kg reaches the bottom with speed 3.59 m s⁻¹. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the coefficient of dynamic friction μ_d between an instrumented cargo crate and a straight steel loading chute?
items.workedSolution: Gravitational potential energy lost ΔE_p = mgL sin 44° = 381 J. Final kinetic energy E_k = ½(16)(3.59)² = 103 J. Frictional energy loss W_f = ΔE_p − E_k = 278 J. Since W_f = μ(mg cos 44°)L, μ = 0.705. Target = 0.705.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔE_p − E_k and normal reaction mg cos 44° accurately to obtain 0.705 (A).

items.stem: Sliding at constant velocity down a straight haulage incline of slope length 25 m and vertical drop 9 m, a mining equipment skid has weight 120 N. What is the magnitude of the resistive force opposing motion along the slope?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed ΔE_k = 0. Potential energy lost = W h = 120 × 9 = 1.08 × 10³ J. Parallel equilibrium gives F_res = W sin θ = W h / L = 43.2 N. Target = 43.2 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ = 9/25 and zero net force to obtain 43.2 N (A).

items.stem: Descending a rough warehouse ramp of length 10 m and vertical drop 4.5 m at a steady speed of 5.5 m s⁻¹, a heavy logistics crate has weight 1500 N. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 1500 × (4.5/10) = 675 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 3.71 × 10³ W. Target = 675 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 675 N (C).

items.stem: Projected from a calibrated ground launcher at 39 m s⁻¹ at an angle of 55° above a flat proving ground, an acoustic ranging dart follows a parabolic arc. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the speed of the projectile at the highest point of its trajectory?
items.workedSolution: At the apex v_y = 0 while horizontal velocity remains constant at v_apex = u cos 55° = 22.4 m s⁻¹. Maximum height h_max = (u sin 55°)² / (2g) = 52.1 m. Target = 22.4 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_y = 0 and constant v_x = u cos 55° at apex to obtain 22.4 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Assumes the projectile is momentarily stationary at its highest point, forgetting its constant horizontal velocity u cos θ.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses u sin θ instead of u cos θ for the speed at the apex.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Assumes speed remains equal to launch speed u throughout the flight.

items.stem: On a horizontal frictionless air track, glider X of mass 2.8 kg moves right at 8 m s⁻¹ and collides with stationary glider Y of mass 0.8 kg. Immediately after impact, glider Y moves right at 9.3 m s⁻¹. What is the speed of glider X immediately after the collision?
items.workedSolution: Momentum conservation: (2.8)(8) = (2.8)v_X + (0.8)(9.3), giving v_X = 5.34 m s⁻¹. K_i = 89.6 J and K_f = 74.6 J, so ΔK_lost = K_i − K_f = 15.0 J. Target = 5.34 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves linear momentum and evaluates kinetic energy budget to obtain 5.34 m s⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: Approaching each other along a horizontal magnetic-bearing guideway, shuttle X (3 kg, 12 m s⁻¹ to the right) collides head-on with shuttle Y (2.4 kg, 3 m s⁻¹ to the left, arrow not shown); afterward shuttle Y travels to the right at 4 m s⁻¹. Determine the final velocity of shuttle X.
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward as positive: p_before = (3)(12) + (2.4)(−3) = 28.8 kg m s⁻¹. From p_before = (3)v_X + (2.4)(4), v_X = 6.40 m s⁻¹, which is 6.40 m s⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: Uses signed head-on momentum p_before = 28.8 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 6.40 m s⁻¹ to the right (B).

items.stem: In a ballistic pendulum rig, a steel pendulum bob of mass 0.8 kg on a light string of length 1.9 m is released from rest with the string horizontal and coalesces at the lowest point with stationary a lump of modelling clay of mass 0.64 kg. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What maximum vertical height above the lowest point do the joined bodies reach?
items.workedSolution: Pre-impact speed u = √(2gL) = 6.11 m s⁻¹. Tangential momentum conservation gives v = mu / (m + M) = 3.39 m s⁻¹. Post-impact rise h = v² / (2g) = (m/(m+M))² L = 0.586 m; energy lost = mgL − (m+M)gh = 6.63 J. Target = 0.586 m.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves energy during swings and momentum during impact to obtain 0.586 m (D).

items.stem: In a vertical circular test rig, a steel sensor sphere of mass 3.1 kg whirls in a vertical circle of radius 1.7 m on a light inextensible wire and passes through the lowest point at speed 7.5 m s⁻¹. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the tension in a light inextensible wire at the lowest point?
items.workedSolution: At the bottom, upward resultant force T − mg = mv²/r. Centripetal force mv²/r = 3.1 × 7.5² / 1.7 = 103 N, so T = 103 + 3.1 × 9.8 = 133 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies T = m(v²/r + g) at the bottom of the circle to obtain 133 N (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts weight mg instead of adding mg, confusing the bottom of a vertical circle with the top.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Equates tension directly to centripetal force mv²/r and forgets the downward weight mg.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Sets tension equal to static weight mg, ignoring centripetal acceleration.

items.stem: In a vertical rotation stand, a telemetry capsule of mass 1.6 kg moves in a vertical circle of radius 2.2 m on a high-tensile cord, which snaps if tension exceeds 70 N. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the maximum speed a telemetry capsule can have at the bottom without breaking a high-tensile cord?
items.workedSolution: Tension is greatest at the bottom where T_max − mg = m v_max² / r. Thus v_max = √[((70/1.6) − 9.81) × 2.2] = 8.64 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves T_max − mg = mv²/r to obtain 8.64 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Adds g instead of subtracting g when rearranging T_max − mg = mv²/r.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Treats vertical circular motion as horizontal, omitting weight mg at the lowest point.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes minimum top-of-loop critical speed √(gr) instead of maximum safe bottom speed.

items.stem: Dropped from rest at the anchor in a cliff-sim drop frame, a mountaineering test mass of mass 10 kg falls freely 2.4 m until a dynamic climbing rope becomes taut at A, then stretches the cord by 0.7 m over 0.15 s to come momentarily to rest at B. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the mean upward force exerted by a dynamic climbing rope between A and B?
items.workedSolution: Speed when taut at A: v_A = √(2 × 9.81 × 2.4) = 6.86 m s⁻¹ downward. Taking upward positive, (F_mean − mg)Δt = 0 − (−mv_A), so F_mean = mv_A / 0.15 + 10(9.81) = 556 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = mv_A with v_A = √(2gL) to obtain 556 N (A).

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, a rail-yard test locomotive of mass 1300 kg accelerates horizontally so a roof-hung indicator sphere hangs at 34° to the vertical, later climbs a 14° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 55 m (static friction coefficient 0.8), and coasts from 15 m s⁻¹ against a 590 N resistive force toward the buffer platform. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.8 m s⁻². During the coasting test from 15 m s⁻¹ against 590 N resistance, what total distance would it travel before coming to rest?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 34° = ma and T cos 34° = mg => a = g tan 34° = 6.61 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.8 × 9.8 × 55) = 20.8 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1300)(15)² / 590 = 248 m. Target = 248 m.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 248 m (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides momentum mv by resistance force (giving stopping time) instead of kinetic energy ½mv².

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of ½ in initial kinetic energy ½mv².

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the semicircular road length πR rather than the coasting stopping distance.

items.stem: In a chute calibration, a timber tool chest of mass 11.5 kg descends 5.5 m from rest down a pitched workshop plank inclined at 34° and exits the base at 5.05 m s⁻¹ under constant friction. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². If the same object is instead released from rest halfway down a pitched workshop plank, what speed does it reach at the bottom?
items.workedSolution: Energy dissipated W_f = mgL sin 34° − ½mv² = 200 J. Constant friction force F_f = W_f / 5.5 = 36.4 N. Released halfway down at unchanged acceleration a, v_half = v / √2 = 3.57 m s⁻¹. Target = 3.57 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Applies work-energy / constant-acceleration scaling on the incline to obtain 3.57 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: While sliding down a braking test slope (22 m long, 5.5 m vertical height) at constant speed 3.5 m s⁻¹, a steel ballast box of weight 1550 N converts lost potential energy into heat. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 1550 × (5.5/22) = 388 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 1.36 × 10³ W. Target = 388 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 388 N (A).

items.stem: During a range trial on a level arena floor, a robotics arena sphere leaves a spring-loaded catapult at 34 m s⁻¹ and 56° above the horizontal. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the total time of flight before returning to a level arena floor?
items.workedSolution: u_y = 34 sin 56° = 28.2 m s⁻¹ and u_x = 34 cos 56° = 19.0 m s⁻¹. Flight time T = 2u_y / 9.8 = 5.75 s; horizontal range R = u_x T = 109 m. Target = 5.75 s.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves orthogonal components accurately to obtain 5.75 s (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes time to reach the apex u sin θ / g rather than full time of flight.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Swaps sin θ and cos θ when resolving vertical launch speed.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses total speed u instead of vertical component u sin θ.

items.stem: During an inelastic collision trial on a horizontal magnetic-bearing guideway, shuttle X (mass 4.4 kg, initial rightward speed 11 m s⁻¹) hits stationary shuttle Y (mass 1.6 kg), which moves off to the right at 9.6 m s⁻¹. What is the speed of shuttle X immediately after the collision?
items.workedSolution: Momentum conservation: (4.4)(11) = (4.4)v_X + (1.6)(9.6), giving v_X = 7.51 m s⁻¹. K_i = 266 J and K_f = 198 J, so ΔK_lost = K_i − K_f = 68.4 J. Target = 7.51 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves linear momentum and evaluates kinetic energy budget to obtain 7.51 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: In a rebound impact on a frictionless optical-bench track, carriage X (mass 2 kg, initial speed 14 m s⁻¹ right) hits stationary carriage Y (mass 6 kg), which moves right at 5.72 m s⁻¹. What is the total kinetic energy of the two bodies immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (2)(14) = (2)v_X + (6)(5.72) gives v_X = -3.16 m s⁻¹ (3.16 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(2)(3.16)² + ½(6)(5.72)² = 108 J. Energy lost = 196 J − K_f = 87.9 J. Target = 108 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 3.16 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 108 J (B).

items.stem: Swinging down from rest with its 0.9 m string initially horizontal in a fracture-toughness pendulum, a hardened striker ball (mass 1.6 kg) embeds into stationary a soft polymer target (mass 1.28 kg) at the bottom. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.8 m s⁻². How much mechanical energy is dissipated during the sticking collision?
items.workedSolution: Pre-impact speed u = √(2gL) = 4.20 m s⁻¹. Tangential momentum conservation gives v = mu / (m + M) = 2.33 m s⁻¹. Post-impact rise h = v² / (2g) = (m/(m+M))² L = 0.278 m; energy lost = mgL − (m+M)gh = 6.27 J. Target = 6.27 J.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves energy during swings and momentum during impact to obtain 6.27 J (C).

items.stem: In a ceiling-mounted swing test, a chrome-steel bob of mass 2.5 kg hangs on a 1.8 m string, is released from rest with the string horizontal, and collides inelastically at the bottom with stationary a resin absorber block of mass 4.5 kg. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the tension in the string immediately before a chrome-steel bob strikes a resin absorber block?
items.workedSolution: Just before collision u² = 2gL => u = 5.94 m s⁻¹. Radial Newton second law T − mg = mu²/L = 2mg gives T = 3mg = 73.6 N. Momentum conservation gives v = mu/(m+M) = 2.12 m s⁻¹. Target = 73.6 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates quarter-swing dynamics and radial/tangential laws to obtain 73.6 N (D).

items.stem: During a tensile limit test in a circular motion demonstrator, a polymer-coated mass of mass 1 kg swings on a light inextensible string of length 0.8 m rated to 59 N maximum tension. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². Calculate the maximum speed at the bottom of the path.
items.workedSolution: Tension is greatest at the bottom where T_max − mg = m v_max² / r. Thus v_max = √[((59/1) − 9.81) × 0.8] = 6.27 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves T_max − mg = mv²/r to obtain 6.27 m s⁻¹ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Adds g instead of subtracting g when rearranging T_max − mg = mv²/r.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats vertical circular motion as horizontal, omitting weight mg at the lowest point.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes minimum top-of-loop critical speed √(gr) instead of maximum safe bottom speed.

items.stem: Attached to a compliant elastomer rope of unstretched length 4.2 m in a vertical deceleration shaft, a payload shock capsule of mass 12 kg falls from rest at the anchor, passes taut point A, and stretches the cord by 0.95 m in 0.14 s to rest at B. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the peak tension in a compliant elastomer rope at the lowest point B?
items.workedSolution: Total vertical drop from release S to lowest point B is L + x = 4.2 + 0.95 = 5.15 m. By energy conservation mg(L + x) = ½kx², giving k = 2mg(L + x)/x² = 1.34 × 10³ N m⁻¹ and peak tension T_B = kx = 1.28 × 10³ N. Target = 1.28 × 10³ N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses full vertical drop (4.2 + 0.95) m in mg(L + x) = ½kx² to obtain 1.28 × 10³ N (B).

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, a proving-ground chassis mule of mass 1700 kg accelerates horizontally so a light-string plumb mass hangs at 30° to the vertical, later climbs a 12° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 65 m (static friction coefficient 0.75), and coasts from 20 m s⁻¹ against a 350 N resistive force toward the recovery marker. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the maximum speed on the flat semicircular curve of radius 65 m without skidding?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 30° = ma and T cos 30° = mg => a = g tan 30° = 5.66 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.75 × 9.81 × 65) = 21.9 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1700)(20)² / 350 = 971 m. Target = 21.9 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 21.9 m s⁻¹ (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the static friction coefficient μ_s in μ_s mg = mv²/R.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Divides by μ_s instead of multiplying by μ_s.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes v² = μ_s g R without taking the square root.

items.stem: The diagram shows a forestry sled carriage of mass 11 kg starting from rest and descending 10.5 m down a hillside guide track angled at 40°, attaining 9.44 m s⁻¹ at the bottom. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the coefficient of kinetic friction μ (defined by F_f = μ R) between a forestry sled carriage and a hillside guide track?
items.workedSolution: Gravitational potential energy lost ΔE_p = mgL sin 40° = 728 J. Final kinetic energy E_k = ½(11)(9.44)² = 490 J. Frictional energy loss W_f = ΔE_p − E_k = 238 J. Since W_f = μ(mg cos 40°)L, μ = 0.274. Target = 0.274.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔE_p − E_k and normal reaction mg cos 40° accurately to obtain 0.274 (C).

items.stem: The diagram depicts a snowcat maintenance sled weighing 1400 N moving at constant speed down a planar ski run of length 28 m and vertical height 11.2 m. What is the magnitude of the resistive force opposing motion along the slope?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed ΔE_k = 0. Potential energy lost = W h = 1400 × 11.2 = 1.57 × 10⁴ J. Parallel equilibrium gives F_res = W sin θ = W h / L = 560 N. Target = 560 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ = 11.2/28 and zero net force to obtain 560 N (B).

items.stem: The diagram shows a shipyard launch block of weight 900 N moving at constant speed 1.5 m s⁻¹ down a greased timber way of slope length 14 m and height 8.4 m. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 900 × (8.4/14) = 540 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 810 W. Target = 540 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 540 N (A).

items.stem: Referring to the launch of an irrigation water packet from a ground-level nozzle at 27 m s⁻¹ and 24° above horizontal farmland: Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². What maximum vertical height above horizontal farmland does it reach?
items.workedSolution: At the apex v_y = 0 while horizontal velocity remains constant at v_apex = u cos 24° = 24.7 m s⁻¹. Maximum height h_max = (u sin 24°)² / (2g) = 6.15 m. Target = 6.15 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_y = 0 and constant v_x = u cos 24° at apex to obtain 6.15 m (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Converts all initial kinetic energy into gravitational potential energy, forgetting non-zero horizontal speed u cos θ at the apex.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses horizontal component u cos θ instead of vertical component u sin θ in h = u_y² / (2g).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of two in the denominator of h_max = u_y² / (2g).

items.stem: The diagram shows cart X of mass 1.4 kg approaching stationary cart Y of mass 4.5 kg at 15 m s⁻¹ on a level low-friction dynamics rail. After impact, cart Y moves right at 6.02 m s⁻¹. How much kinetic energy is dissipated in this rebound collision?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (1.4)(15) = (1.4)v_X + (4.5)(6.02) gives v_X = -4.35 m s⁻¹ (4.35 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(1.4)(4.35)² + ½(4.5)(6.02)² = 94.8 J. Energy lost = 158 J − K_f = 62.7 J. Target = 62.7 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 4.35 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 62.7 J (B).

items.stem: Approaching each other along a level low-friction dynamics rail, cart X (2 kg, 7 m s⁻¹ to the right) collides head-on with cart Y (1.2 kg, 4.5 m s⁻¹ to the left, arrow not shown); afterward cart Y travels to the right at 2 m s⁻¹. Determine the final velocity of cart X.
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward as positive: p_before = (2)(7) + (1.2)(−4.5) = 8.60 kg m s⁻¹. From p_before = (2)v_X + (1.2)(2), v_X = 3.10 m s⁻¹, which is 3.10 m s⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: Uses signed head-on momentum p_before = 8.60 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 3.10 m s⁻¹ to the right (C).

items.stem: The diagram shows a physics lecture bob of mass 2.3 kg released from a horizontal 2 m string in a light-string pendulum toward stationary a stationary putty sphere of mass 4.14 kg at the bottom. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the tension in the string immediately before a physics lecture bob strikes a stationary putty sphere?
items.workedSolution: Just before collision u² = 2gL => u = 6.26 m s⁻¹. Radial Newton second law T − mg = mu²/L = 2mg gives T = 3mg = 67.7 N. Momentum conservation gives v = mu/(m+M) = 2.24 m s⁻¹. Target = 67.7 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates quarter-swing dynamics and radial/tangential laws to obtain 67.7 N (C).

items.stem: The diagram shows a polished alloy bob of mass 1.3 kg moving at 5.5 m s⁻¹ through the bottom of a vertical circle of radius 1.9 m on a light suspension line in a vertical swing circle. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.8 m s⁻². What tension acts in a light suspension line?
items.workedSolution: At the bottom, upward resultant force T − mg = mv²/r. Centripetal force mv²/r = 1.3 × 5.5² / 1.9 = 20.7 N, so T = 20.7 + 1.3 × 9.8 = 33.4 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies T = m(v²/r + g) at the bottom of the circle to obtain 33.4 N (C).

options.label: A

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Sets tension equal to static weight mg, ignoring centripetal acceleration.

items.stem: The three-stage diagram shows a marine mooring weight of mass 11.5 kg dropped from rest at the support of a stretchable nylon hawser (natural length 2.4 m), reaching A taut and extending a further 1.35 m over 0.14 s to rest at lowest point B. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the spring constant of a stretchable nylon hawser?
items.workedSolution: Total vertical drop from release S to lowest point B is L + x = 2.4 + 1.35 = 3.75 m. By energy conservation mg(L + x) = ½kx², giving k = 2mg(L + x)/x² = 464 N m⁻¹ and peak tension T_B = kx = 627 N. Target = 464 N m⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses full vertical drop (2.4 + 1.35) m in mg(L + x) = ½kx² to obtain 464 N m⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: The diagram illustrates an instrumented drop sphere of mass 10 kg released at the support of an elastic bungee tether (natural length 3.2 m), becoming taut at A and decelerating to rest at B (extension 0.8 m) over 0.21 s. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What mean force does an elastic bungee tether exert between A and B?
items.workedSolution: Speed when taut at A: v_A = √(2 × 9.81 × 3.2) = 7.92 m s⁻¹ downward. Taking upward positive, (F_mean − mg)Δt = 0 − (−mv_A), so F_mean = mv_A / 0.21 + 10(9.81) = 475 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = mv_A with v_A = √(2gL) to obtain 475 N (B).

items.stem: Along a planar terminal slide inclined at 24° to the horizontal, a baggage transfer container (mass 10.5 kg) slides 8 m from rest and arrives at the base travelling at 4.39 m s⁻¹. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. How much mechanical energy is dissipated against friction during the descent?
items.workedSolution: Gravitational potential energy lost ΔE_p = mgL sin 24° = 335 J. Final kinetic energy E_k = ½(10.5)(4.39)² = 101 J. Frictional energy loss W_f = ΔE_p − E_k = 234 J. Since W_f = μ(mg cos 24°)L, μ = 0.311. Target = 234 J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔE_p − E_k and normal reaction mg cos 24° accurately to obtain 234 J (C).

items.stem: On a dry-dock slip plank (5.5 m long, angled at 30° to the horizontal), a shipyard keel block of mass 2.5 kg slides from rest and attains 4.77 m s⁻¹ at the base against constant kinetic friction. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. If the same object is instead released from rest halfway down a dry-dock slip plank, what speed does it reach at the bottom?
items.workedSolution: Energy dissipated W_f = mgL sin 30° − ½mv² = 39.0 J. Constant friction force F_f = W_f / 5.5 = 7.09 N. Released halfway down at unchanged acceleration a, v_half = v / √2 = 3.37 m s⁻¹. Target = 3.37 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Applies work-energy / constant-acceleration scaling on the incline to obtain 3.37 m s⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: A civil-engineering gabion (weight 1550 N) slides at constant speed 6.5 m s⁻¹ down a planar test embankment, which is 14 m long and drops 7 m vertically. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 1550 × (7/14) = 775 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 5.04 × 10³ W. Target = 775 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 775 N (B).

items.stem: Fired from a ground discharge tube at 20 m s⁻¹ and 64° above the horizontal, a tracer polymer pellet lands back on a horizontal test paddock. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What is the total time of flight before returning to a horizontal test paddock?
items.workedSolution: u_y = 20 sin 64° = 18.0 m s⁻¹ and u_x = 20 cos 64° = 8.77 m s⁻¹. Flight time T = 2u_y / 9.8 = 3.67 s; horizontal range R = u_x T = 32.2 m. Target = 3.67 s.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves orthogonal components accurately to obtain 3.67 s (B).

options.label: A

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses total speed u instead of vertical component u sin θ.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Takes an erroneous square root of 2u sin θ / g.

items.stem: Travelling at 12 m s⁻¹ to the right along a level docking-simulator rail, module X (2 kg) strikes stationary module Y (0.8 kg), sending module Y rightward at 10.2 m s⁻¹. What is the speed of module X immediately after the collision?
items.workedSolution: Momentum conservation: (2)(12) = (2)v_X + (0.8)(10.2), giving v_X = 7.92 m s⁻¹. K_i = 144 J and K_f = 104 J, so ΔK_lost = K_i − K_f = 39.7 J. Target = 7.92 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves linear momentum and evaluates kinetic energy budget to obtain 7.92 m s⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: Moving rightward at 7 m s⁻¹ on a polished ice test channel, sled X (0.8 kg) collides head-on with stationary sled Y (1.9 kg); immediately afterward sled Y travels right at 3.49 m s⁻¹ and sled X rebounds backward. What is the total kinetic energy of the two bodies immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (0.8)(7) = (0.8)v_X + (1.9)(3.49) gives v_X = -1.29 m s⁻¹ (1.29 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(0.8)(1.29)² + ½(1.9)(3.49)² = 12.2 J. Energy lost = 19.6 J − K_f = 7.36 J. Target = 12.2 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 1.29 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 12.2 J (D).

items.stem: Released from rest from a horizontal string position of length 1.7 m in a fracture-toughness pendulum, a hardened striker ball (2.4 kg) strikes and sticks to stationary a soft polymer target (1.92 kg) at the bottom of its arc. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. How much mechanical energy is dissipated during the sticking collision?
items.workedSolution: Pre-impact speed u = √(2gL) = 5.77 m s⁻¹. Tangential momentum conservation gives v = mu / (m + M) = 3.21 m s⁻¹. Post-impact rise h = v² / (2g) = (m/(m+M))² L = 0.525 m; energy lost = mgL − (m+M)gh = 17.8 J. Target = 17.8 J.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves energy during swings and momentum during impact to obtain 17.8 J (B).

items.stem: Whirled on a light radial tether of length 1.9 m in a vertical-plane spinner, a gyroscope test mass (0.3 kg) has speed 7 m s⁻¹ at the bottom of its vertical circular path. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. Determine the tension in a light radial tether at this instant.
items.workedSolution: At the bottom, upward resultant force T − mg = mv²/r. Centripetal force mv²/r = 0.3 × 7² / 1.9 = 7.74 N, so T = 7.74 + 0.3 × 9.81 = 10.7 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies T = m(v²/r + g) at the bottom of the circle to obtain 10.7 N (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts weight mg instead of adding mg, confusing the bottom of a vertical circle with the top.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Equates tension directly to centripetal force mv²/r and forgets the downward weight mg.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Sets tension equal to static weight mg, ignoring centripetal acceleration.

items.stem: Whirled in a vertical circle of radius 1.4 m on a thin braided string (breaking tension 33 N) in a lecture-hall whirl rig, a calibration ball has mass 1.2 kg. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. Determine the greatest safe speed at the lowest point.
items.workedSolution: Tension is greatest at the bottom where T_max − mg = m v_max² / r. Thus v_max = √[((33/1.2) − 9.81) × 1.4] = 4.98 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves T_max − mg = mv²/r to obtain 4.98 m s⁻¹ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Adds g instead of subtracting g when rearranging T_max − mg = mv²/r.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats vertical circular motion as horizontal, omitting weight mg at the lowest point.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes minimum top-of-loop critical speed √(gr) instead of maximum safe bottom speed.

items.stem: In a vertical deceleration shaft, a payload shock capsule (14 kg) falls from rest at the support through the 1.8 m slack length of a compliant elastomer rope to point A and is brought momentarily to rest after stretching 1.4 m in a time of 0.15 s to B. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. Determine the time-averaged tension in a compliant elastomer rope during this 0.15 s interval.
items.workedSolution: Speed when taut at A: v_A = √(2 × 9.8 × 1.8) = 5.94 m s⁻¹ downward. Taking upward positive, (F_mean − mg)Δt = 0 − (−mv_A), so F_mean = mv_A / 0.15 + 14(9.8) = 692 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = mv_A with v_A = √(2gL) to obtain 692 N (C).

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, an autonomous freight van of mass 1200 kg accelerates horizontally so a cabin pendulum accelerometer hangs at 34° to the vertical, later climbs a 10° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 95 m (static friction coefficient 0.45), and coasts from 18 m s⁻¹ against a 410 N resistive force toward the inspection pad. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.8 m s⁻². During the coasting test from 18 m s⁻¹ against 410 N resistance, what total distance would it travel before coming to rest?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 34° = ma and T cos 34° = mg => a = g tan 34° = 6.61 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.45 × 9.8 × 95) = 20.5 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1200)(18)² / 410 = 474 m. Target = 474 m.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 474 m (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Divides momentum mv by resistance force (giving stopping time) instead of kinetic energy ½mv².

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of ½ in initial kinetic energy ½mv².

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the semicircular road length πR rather than the coasting stopping distance.

items.stem: Released from rest at the top of a brushed concrete incline of length 3 m inclined at 34° to the horizontal, a vulcanized rubber block of mass 15.5 kg reaches the bottom with speed 4.59 m s⁻¹ against a constant friction force. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the magnitude of the constant friction force opposing its motion?
items.workedSolution: Energy dissipated W_f = mgL sin 34° − ½mv² = 91.8 J. Constant friction force F_f = W_f / 3 = 30.6 N. Released halfway down at unchanged acceleration a, v_half = v / √2 = 3.25 m s⁻¹. Target = 30.6 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies work-energy / constant-acceleration scaling on the incline to obtain 30.6 N (B).

items.stem: Sliding at constant velocity down a substation access slope of slope length 17 m and vertical drop 6.1 m, a transformer housing has weight 440 N. What is the magnitude of the resistive force opposing motion along the slope?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed ΔE_k = 0. Potential energy lost = W h = 440 × 6.1 = 2.68 × 10³ J. Parallel equilibrium gives F_res = W sin θ = W h / L = 158 N. Target = 158 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ = 6.1/17 and zero net force to obtain 158 N (C).

items.stem: Across a flat ash plain, a ground-level vent projects a volcanic ballistic clast with initial speed 24 m s⁻¹ at 34° above the horizontal. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What horizontal range does it cover before landing on a flat ash plain?
items.workedSolution: u_y = 24 sin 34° = 13.4 m s⁻¹ and u_x = 24 cos 34° = 19.9 m s⁻¹. Flight time T = 2u_y / 9.81 = 2.74 s; horizontal range R = u_x T = 54.4 m. Target = 54.4 m.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves orthogonal components accurately to obtain 54.4 m (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies horizontal speed by ascent time u sin θ / g instead of full flight time 2u sin θ / g.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes cos θ for sin θ in the flight-time expression.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses the 45° maximum-range formula u²/g without the angle factor sin(2θ).

items.stem: Projected from a deck-level launcher at 18 m s⁻¹ at an angle of 62° above calm water at launch level, a rescue line-throwing bob follows a parabolic arc. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the speed of the projectile at the highest point of its trajectory?
items.workedSolution: At the apex v_y = 0 while horizontal velocity remains constant at v_apex = u cos 62° = 8.45 m s⁻¹. Maximum height h_max = (u sin 62°)² / (2g) = 12.9 m. Target = 8.45 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_y = 0 and constant v_x = u cos 62° at apex to obtain 8.45 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Assumes the projectile is momentarily stationary at its highest point, forgetting its constant horizontal velocity u cos θ.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses u sin θ instead of u cos θ for the speed at the apex.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Assumes speed remains equal to launch speed u throughout the flight.

items.stem: On a smooth glass collision groove, lighter trolley X of mass 0.8 kg moving right at 13 m s⁻¹ strikes stationary heavier trolley Y of mass 2.4 kg, causing trolley Y to move right at 5.96 m s⁻¹ while trolley X rebounds to the left. How much kinetic energy is dissipated in this rebound collision?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (0.8)(13) = (0.8)v_X + (2.4)(5.96) gives v_X = -4.88 m s⁻¹ (4.88 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(0.8)(4.88)² + ½(2.4)(5.96)² = 52.2 J. Energy lost = 67.6 J − K_f = 15.4 J. Target = 15.4 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 4.88 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 15.4 J (B).

items.stem: On a polished ice test channel, sled X of mass 3 kg moves right at 6 m s⁻¹ toward sled Y of mass 3.6 kg approaching head-on to the left at 2 m s⁻¹ (initial arrow on Y omitted). Immediately after collision, sled Y moves right at 1.5 m s⁻¹. What is the velocity of sled X immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward as positive: p_before = (3)(6) + (3.6)(−2) = 10.8 kg m s⁻¹. From p_before = (3)v_X + (3.6)(1.5), v_X = 1.80 m s⁻¹, which is 1.80 m s⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: Uses signed head-on momentum p_before = 10.8 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 1.80 m s⁻¹ to the right (C).

items.stem: In a Charpy-style swing rig, a cast-iron hammer bob of mass 0.3 kg hangs on a 1.6 m string, is released from rest with the string horizontal, and collides inelastically at the bottom with stationary a deformable putty mass of mass 0.42 kg. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the tension in the string immediately before a cast-iron hammer bob strikes a deformable putty mass?
items.workedSolution: Just before collision u² = 2gL => u = 5.60 m s⁻¹. Radial Newton second law T − mg = mu²/L = 2mg gives T = 3mg = 8.83 N. Momentum conservation gives v = mu/(m+M) = 2.33 m s⁻¹. Target = 8.83 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates quarter-swing dynamics and radial/tangential laws to obtain 8.83 N (B).

items.stem: In a centrifuge arm model, an accelerometer test pod of mass 1.9 kg whirls in a vertical circle of radius 0.6 m on a light kevlar tether and passes through the lowest point at speed 3.5 m s⁻¹. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the tension in a light kevlar tether at the lowest point?
items.workedSolution: At the bottom, upward resultant force T − mg = mv²/r. Centripetal force mv²/r = 1.9 × 3.5² / 0.6 = 38.8 N, so T = 38.8 + 1.9 × 9.81 = 57.4 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies T = m(v²/r + g) at the bottom of the circle to obtain 57.4 N (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts weight mg instead of adding mg, confusing the bottom of a vertical circle with the top.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Equates tension directly to centripetal force mv²/r and forgets the downward weight mg.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Sets tension equal to static weight mg, ignoring centripetal acceleration.

items.stem: In a high-platform test rig, a bridge-jump test sandbag of mass 11 kg is released from rest at the anchor of an elastic shock cord of unstretched length 3 m. The cord becomes taut at A and stretches obeying Hooke's law by a maximum extension of 0.45 m over 0.2 s before a bridge-jump test sandbag comes momentarily to rest at B. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the spring constant of an elastic shock cord?
items.workedSolution: Total vertical drop from release S to lowest point B is L + x = 3 + 0.45 = 3.45 m. By energy conservation mg(L + x) = ½kx², giving k = 2mg(L + x)/x² = 3.67 × 10³ N m⁻¹ and peak tension T_B = kx = 1.65 × 10³ N. Target = 3.67 × 10³ N m⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses full vertical drop (3 + 0.45) m in mg(L + x) = ½kx² to obtain 3.67 × 10³ N m⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, a rail-yard test locomotive of mass 1200 kg accelerates horizontally so a roof-hung indicator sphere hangs at 26° to the vertical, later climbs a 14° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 45 m (static friction coefficient 0.5), and coasts from 21 m s⁻¹ against a 530 N resistive force toward the buffer platform. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the horizontal acceleration during the initial straight-line phase when a roof-hung indicator sphere deflects by 26°?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 26° = ma and T cos 26° = mg => a = g tan 26° = 4.78 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.5 × 9.81 × 45) = 14.9 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1200)(21)² / 530 = 499 m. Target = 4.78 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 4.78 m s⁻² (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses g sin θ as if on an inclined plane rather than resolving T sin θ = ma and T cos θ = mg to obtain g tan θ.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the ratio of horizontal to vertical components, evaluating g / tan θ instead of g tan θ.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies g by cos θ instead of tan θ.

items.stem: During a surface-wear test on an anodized calibration incline (8.5 m long, 32° above the horizontal), an avionics shock canister of mass 14.5 kg slides from rest to a bottom speed of 6.3 m s⁻¹. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.8 m s⁻². How much mechanical energy is dissipated against friction during the descent?
items.workedSolution: Gravitational potential energy lost ΔE_p = mgL sin 32° = 640 J. Final kinetic energy E_k = ½(14.5)(6.3)² = 288 J. Frictional energy loss W_f = ΔE_p − E_k = 352 J. Since W_f = μ(mg cos 32°)L, μ = 0.344. Target = 352 J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔE_p − E_k and normal reaction mg cos 32° accurately to obtain 352 J (A).

items.stem: In translational equilibrium at constant speed, a steel cable drum cradle (weight 120 N) travels 9 m down a warehouse ramp, dropping 4.3 m vertically. How much gravitational potential energy is lost over the full length of the slope?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed ΔE_k = 0. Potential energy lost = W h = 120 × 4.3 = 516 J. Parallel equilibrium gives F_res = W sin θ = W h / L = 57.3 N. Target = 516 J.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ = 4.3/9 and zero net force to obtain 516 J (A).

items.stem: Descending a greased timber way of length 22 m and vertical drop 8.8 m at a steady speed of 6.5 m s⁻¹, a shipyard launch block has weight 900 N. At what rate is mechanical energy converted into thermal energy?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 900 × (8.8/22) = 360 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 2.34 × 10³ W. Target = 2.34 × 10³ W.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 2.34 × 10³ W (B).

items.stem: Referring to the launch of a tracer polymer pellet from a ground discharge tube at 30 m s⁻¹ and 24° above a horizontal test paddock: Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.8 m s⁻². What maximum vertical height above a horizontal test paddock does it reach?
items.workedSolution: At the apex v_y = 0 while horizontal velocity remains constant at v_apex = u cos 24° = 27.4 m s⁻¹. Maximum height h_max = (u sin 24°)² / (2g) = 7.60 m. Target = 7.60 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_y = 0 and constant v_x = u cos 24° at apex to obtain 7.60 m (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Converts all initial kinetic energy into gravitational potential energy, forgetting non-zero horizontal speed u cos θ at the apex.

options.label: B

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of two in the denominator of h_max = u_y² / (2g).

items.stem: During an inelastic collision trial on a precision gas-bearing trough, rider X (mass 1.2 kg, initial rightward speed 8 m s⁻¹) hits stationary rider Y (mass 1.6 kg), which moves off to the right at 4.18 m s⁻¹. What is the speed of rider X immediately after the collision?
items.workedSolution: Momentum conservation: (1.2)(8) = (1.2)v_X + (1.6)(4.18), giving v_X = 2.43 m s⁻¹. K_i = 38.4 J and K_f = 17.5 J, so ΔK_lost = K_i − K_f = 20.9 J. Target = 2.43 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves linear momentum and evaluates kinetic energy budget to obtain 2.43 m s⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: During a head-on collision test on a smooth glass collision groove, trolley X (4 kg) moves right at 10 m s⁻¹ while trolley Y (2.4 kg) moves left at 6 m s⁻¹ (arrow omitted), and trolley Y exits right at 5.5 m s⁻¹. Find the velocity of trolley X right after collision.
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward as positive: p_before = (4)(10) + (2.4)(−6) = 25.6 kg m s⁻¹. From p_before = (4)v_X + (2.4)(5.5), v_X = 3.10 m s⁻¹, which is 3.10 m s⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: Uses signed head-on momentum p_before = 25.6 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 3.10 m s⁻¹ to the right (A).

items.stem: Swinging down from rest with its 0.9 m string initially horizontal in a Charpy-style swing rig, a cast-iron hammer bob (mass 2.8 kg) embeds into stationary a deformable putty mass (mass 5.6 kg) at the bottom. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². How much mechanical energy is dissipated during the sticking collision?
items.workedSolution: Pre-impact speed u = √(2gL) = 4.20 m s⁻¹. Tangential momentum conservation gives v = mu / (m + M) = 1.40 m s⁻¹. Post-impact rise h = v² / (2g) = (m/(m+M))² L = 0.100 m; energy lost = mgL − (m+M)gh = 16.5 J. Target = 16.5 J.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves energy during swings and momentum during impact to obtain 16.5 J (B).

items.stem: At the bottom of a vertical circle of radius 1.7 m in a vertical rotation stand, a telemetry capsule of mass 1.7 kg travels at 9.5 m s⁻¹ while attached to a high-tensile cord. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.8 m s⁻². Calculate the tension in a high-tensile cord.
items.workedSolution: At the bottom, upward resultant force T − mg = mv²/r. Centripetal force mv²/r = 1.7 × 9.5² / 1.7 = 90.2 N, so T = 90.2 + 1.7 × 9.8 = 107 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies T = m(v²/r + g) at the bottom of the circle to obtain 107 N (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts weight mg instead of adding mg, confusing the bottom of a vertical circle with the top.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Equates tension directly to centripetal force mv²/r and forgets the downward weight mg.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Sets tension equal to static weight mg, ignoring centripetal acceleration.

items.stem: During a tensile limit test in a vertical circular test rig, a steel sensor sphere of mass 1.2 kg swings on a light inextensible wire of length 1.2 m rated to 29 N maximum tension. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². Calculate the maximum speed at the bottom of the path.
items.workedSolution: Tension is greatest at the bottom where T_max − mg = m v_max² / r. Thus v_max = √[((29/1.2) − 9.81) × 1.2] = 4.15 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves T_max − mg = mv²/r to obtain 4.15 m s⁻¹ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Adds g instead of subtracting g when rearranging T_max − mg = mv²/r.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats vertical circular motion as horizontal, omitting weight mg at the lowest point.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes minimum top-of-loop critical speed √(gr) instead of maximum safe bottom speed.

items.stem: During an impulse-arrest test in a stage gridiron support, a stunt-rig counterweight of mass 2 kg drops freely 4.4 m to taut point A and extends an elastic arrest cable by 1.2 m over 0.24 s until instantaneous rest at B. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². Calculate the mean upward cord force during deceleration.
items.workedSolution: Speed when taut at A: v_A = √(2 × 9.81 × 4.4) = 9.29 m s⁻¹ downward. Taking upward positive, (F_mean − mg)Δt = 0 − (−mv_A), so F_mean = mv_A / 0.24 + 2(9.81) = 97.0 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = mv_A with v_A = √(2gL) to obtain 97.0 N (A).

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, a harbour container carrier of mass 1100 kg accelerates horizontally so a suspended mass indicator hangs at 22° to the vertical, later climbs a 12° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 50 m (static friction coefficient 0.6), and coasts from 16 m s⁻¹ against a 500 N resistive force toward the berth checkpoint. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the maximum speed on the flat semicircular curve of radius 50 m without skidding?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 22° = ma and T cos 22° = mg => a = g tan 22° = 3.96 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.6 × 9.8 × 50) = 17.1 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1100)(16)² / 500 = 282 m. Target = 17.1 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 17.1 m s⁻¹ (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the static friction coefficient μ_s in μ_s mg = mv²/R.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides by μ_s instead of multiplying by μ_s.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes v² = μ_s g R without taking the square root.

items.stem: The diagram illustrates a cleanroom shipping pod (3 kg) released from rest at the top of a coated transfer incline of length 6.5 m and angle 42°, arriving at the bottom at 6 m s⁻¹. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the magnitude of the constant friction force opposing its motion?
items.workedSolution: Energy dissipated W_f = mgL sin 42° − ½mv² = 74.0 J. Constant friction force F_f = W_f / 6.5 = 11.4 N. Released halfway down at unchanged acceleration a, v_half = v / √2 = 4.24 m s⁻¹. Target = 11.4 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies work-energy / constant-acceleration scaling on the incline to obtain 11.4 N (C).

items.stem: The diagram shows a warehouse pallet box of weight 850 N moving at constant speed 4 m s⁻¹ down a gravity-brake ramp of slope length 30 m and height 15 m. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 850 × (15/30) = 425 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 1.70 × 10³ W. Target = 425 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 425 N (B).

items.stem: During a range trial on a horizontal test paddock, a tracer polymer pellet leaves a ground discharge tube at 20 m s⁻¹ and 34° above the horizontal. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the total time of flight before returning to a horizontal test paddock?
items.workedSolution: u_y = 20 sin 34° = 11.2 m s⁻¹ and u_x = 20 cos 34° = 16.6 m s⁻¹. Flight time T = 2u_y / 9.8 = 2.28 s; horizontal range R = u_x T = 37.8 m. Target = 2.28 s.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves orthogonal components accurately to obtain 2.28 s (D).

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Swaps sin θ and cos θ when resolving vertical launch speed.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses total speed u instead of vertical component u sin θ.

items.stem: The diagram shows carriage X of mass 3.6 kg moving right at 14 m s⁻¹ toward stationary carriage Y of mass 0.8 kg on a frictionless optical-bench track; after collision, carriage Y travels right at 14.5 m s⁻¹. What is the speed of carriage X immediately after the collision?
items.workedSolution: Momentum conservation: (3.6)(14) = (3.6)v_X + (0.8)(14.5), giving v_X = 10.8 m s⁻¹. K_i = 353 J and K_f = 293 J, so ΔK_lost = K_i − K_f = 59.6 J. Target = 10.8 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves linear momentum and evaluates kinetic energy budget to obtain 10.8 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: The diagram shows shuttle X of mass 2 kg approaching stationary shuttle Y of mass 6.8 kg at 14 m s⁻¹ on a horizontal magnetic-bearing guideway. After impact, shuttle Y moves right at 5.13 m s⁻¹. How much kinetic energy is dissipated in this rebound collision?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (2)(14) = (2)v_X + (6.8)(5.13) gives v_X = -3.44 m s⁻¹ (3.44 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(2)(3.44)² + ½(6.8)(5.13)² = 101 J. Energy lost = 196 J − K_f = 94.7 J. Target = 94.7 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 3.44 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 94.7 J (A).

items.stem: The diagram shows a calibration swing mass of mass 1.4 kg swinging from a horizontal 1.4 m string in a frictionless pivot stand to couple with stationary a coupling receiver ball of mass 1.12 kg at the lowest point. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.8 m s⁻². What maximum vertical height above the lowest point do the joined bodies reach?
items.workedSolution: Pre-impact speed u = √(2gL) = 5.24 m s⁻¹. Tangential momentum conservation gives v = mu / (m + M) = 2.91 m s⁻¹. Post-impact rise h = v² / (2g) = (m/(m+M))² L = 0.432 m; energy lost = mgL − (m+M)gh = 8.54 J. Target = 0.432 m.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves energy during swings and momentum during impact to obtain 0.432 m (D).

items.stem: The diagram shows a brass impact sphere of mass 0.5 kg released from a horizontal 1.8 m string in a laboratory swing frame toward stationary a wax capture block of mass 0.5 kg at the bottom. items.stem: The diagram shows a compact lead bob (1 kg) at the bottom of a vertical circle of radius 1.4 m in a vertical loop frame; a light steel cable has a maximum safe tension of 40 N. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the maximum allowed speed at this point?
items.workedSolution: Tension is greatest at the bottom where T_max − mg = m v_max² / r. Thus v_max = √[((40/1) − 9.81) × 1.4] = 6.50 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves T_max − mg = mv²/r to obtain 6.50 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Adds g instead of subtracting g when rearranging T_max − mg = mv²/r.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Treats vertical circular motion as horizontal, omitting weight mg at the lowest point.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes minimum top-of-loop critical speed √(gr) instead of maximum safe bottom speed.

items.stem: The three-stage diagram shows a calibration steel ball of mass 2.5 kg dropped from rest at the support of a Hookean rubber cord (natural length 2.6 m), reaching A taut and extending a further 0.95 m over 0.28 s to rest at lowest point B. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the spring constant of a Hookean rubber cord?
items.workedSolution: Total vertical drop from release S to lowest point B is L + x = 2.6 + 0.95 = 3.55 m. By energy conservation mg(L + x) = ½kx², giving k = 2mg(L + x)/x² = 193 N m⁻¹ and peak tension T_B = kx = 183 N. Target = 193 N m⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses full vertical drop (2.6 + 0.95) m in mg(L + x) = ½kx² to obtain 193 N m⁻¹ (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Equates ½kx² to mgL instead of mg(L + x), forgetting the extra vertical drop x while the cord stretches.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of ½ in elastic potential energy E_e = ½kx².

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Sets kx = mg as if the lowest turning point B were a static equilibrium position.

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, an articulated test coach of mass 900 kg accelerates horizontally so a roof-mounted plumb sphere hangs at 34° to the vertical, later climbs a 8° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 90 m (static friction coefficient 0.75), and coasts from 19 m s⁻¹ against a 440 N resistive force toward the timing gate. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the maximum speed on the flat semicircular curve of radius 90 m without skidding?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 34° = ma and T cos 34° = mg => a = g tan 34° = 6.62 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.75 × 9.81 × 90) = 25.7 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(900)(19)² / 440 = 369 m. Target = 25.7 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 25.7 m s⁻¹ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the static friction coefficient μ_s in μ_s mg = mv²/R.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Divides by μ_s instead of multiplying by μ_s.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes v² = μ_s g R without taking the square root.

items.stem: Along a compacted snow test slope inclined at 32° to the horizontal, an alpine supply sled (mass 4.5 kg) slides 4.5 m from rest and arrives at the base travelling at 4.79 m s⁻¹. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. How much mechanical energy is dissipated against friction during the descent?
items.workedSolution: Gravitational potential energy lost ΔE_p = mgL sin 32° = 105 J. Final kinetic energy E_k = ½(4.5)(4.79)² = 51.6 J. Frictional energy loss W_f = ΔE_p − E_k = 53.6 J. Since W_f = μ(mg cos 32°)L, μ = 0.318. Target = 53.6 J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔE_p − E_k and normal reaction mg cos 32° accurately to obtain 53.6 J (C).

options.distractorRationale: Uses L cos θ instead of vertical drop L sin θ when calculating gravitational potential energy lost.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates total gravitational potential energy lost without subtracting final kinetic energy.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the final kinetic energy ½mv² rather than energy dissipated against friction.

items.stem: Of weight 1360 N, a freight container sled descends a dockyard unloading ramp at steady speed over a slope distance of 11 m through a vertical height change of 3.1 m. How much gravitational potential energy is lost over the full length of the slope?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed ΔE_k = 0. Potential energy lost = W h = 1360 × 3.1 = 4.22 × 10³ J. Parallel equilibrium gives F_res = W sin θ = W h / L = 383 N. Target = 4.22 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ = 3.1/11 and zero net force to obtain 4.22 × 10³ J (C).

options.distractorRationale: Multiplies vertical weight W by slope distance L instead of vertical drop h.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies weight W by the horizontal base √(L² − h²) rather than vertical drop h.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the resistive force Wh/L rather than the energy lost Wh.

items.stem: A foundry ingot sled (weight 1150 N) slides at constant speed 6.5 m s⁻¹ down a refractory cooling chute, which is 22 m long and drops 11 m vertically. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 1150 × (11/22) = 575 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 3.74 × 10³ W. Target = 575 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 575 N (D).

options.distractorRationale: Computes perpendicular normal contact force W cos θ instead of parallel friction force W h / L.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies by speed to obtain thermal power rather than friction force.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Equates friction along the incline directly to full weight W.

items.stem: A hail-impact test sphere leaves an angled gas gun at 18 m s⁻¹ inclined at 55° above the horizontal over a horizontal test hall. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What maximum vertical height above a horizontal test hall does it reach?
items.workedSolution: At the apex v_y = 0 while horizontal velocity remains constant at v_apex = u cos 55° = 10.3 m s⁻¹. Maximum height h_max = (u sin 55°)² / (2g) = 11.1 m. Target = 11.1 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_y = 0 and constant v_x = u cos 55° at apex to obtain 11.1 m (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Converts all initial kinetic energy into gravitational potential energy, forgetting non-zero horizontal speed u cos θ at the apex.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses horizontal component u cos θ instead of vertical component u sin θ in h = u_y² / (2g).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of two in the denominator of h_max = u_y² / (2g).

items.stem: The diagram shows trolley X of mass 1 kg approaching stationary trolley Y of mass 2.2 kg at 13 m s⁻¹ on a smooth glass collision groove. After impact, trolley Y moves right at 6.68 m s⁻¹. How much kinetic energy is dissipated in this rebound collision?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (1)(13) = (1)v_X + (2.2)(6.68) gives v_X = -1.70 m s⁻¹ (1.70 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(1)(1.70)² + ½(2.2)(6.68)² = 50.5 J. Energy lost = 84.5 J − K_f = 34.0 J. Target = 34.0 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 1.70 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 34.0 J (A).

options.label: D

items.stem: During a head-on collision test on a precision gas-bearing trough, rider X (2 kg) moves right at 10 m s⁻¹ while rider Y (3 kg) moves left at 3 m s⁻¹ (arrow omitted), and rider Y exits right at 2.5 m s⁻¹. Find the velocity of rider X right after collision.
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward as positive: p_before = (2)(10) + (3)(−3) = 11.0 kg m s⁻¹. From p_before = (2)v_X + (3)(2.5), v_X = 1.75 m s⁻¹, which is 1.75 m s⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: Uses signed head-on momentum p_before = 11.0 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 1.75 m s⁻¹ to the right (B).

items.stem: Held with its 2 m light string horizontal in a suspension test gantry, an instrumented pendulum mass (1.3 kg) swings down from rest and sticks to stationary a magnetic-latch block (2.86 kg) at the lowest point. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What is the speed of the coupled bodies immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Just before collision u² = 2gL => u = 6.26 m s⁻¹. Radial Newton second law T − mg = mu²/L = 2mg gives T = 3mg = 38.3 N. Momentum conservation gives v = mu/(m+M) = 1.96 m s⁻¹. Target = 1.96 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates quarter-swing dynamics and radial/tangential laws to obtain 1.96 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: Whirled on a taut nylon cord of length 0.7 m in a vertical whirl apparatus, a brass pendulum mass (2.7 kg) has speed 6 m s⁻¹ at the bottom of its vertical circular path. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. Determine the tension in a taut nylon cord at this instant.
items.workedSolution: At the bottom, upward resultant force T − mg = mv²/r. Centripetal force mv²/r = 2.7 × 6² / 0.7 = 139 N, so T = 139 + 2.7 × 9.8 = 165 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies T = m(v²/r + g) at the bottom of the circle to obtain 165 N (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts weight mg instead of adding mg, confusing the bottom of a vertical circle with the top.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Equates tension directly to centripetal force mv²/r and forgets the downward weight mg.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Sets tension equal to static weight mg, ignoring centripetal acceleration.

items.stem: Released from rest at the support in a fall-arrest gantry, a rescue arrest dummy (2.5 kg) falls freely through the 3.2 m natural length of a braided dynamic lanyard to point A and then extends the Hookean cord by 0.55 m during 0.16 s to instantaneous rest at B. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What is the peak tension in a braided dynamic lanyard at the lowest point B?
items.workedSolution: Total vertical drop from release S to lowest point B is L + x = 3.2 + 0.55 = 3.75 m. By energy conservation mg(L + x) = ½kx², giving k = 2mg(L + x)/x² = 608 N m⁻¹ and peak tension T_B = kx = 334 N. Target = 334 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses full vertical drop (3.2 + 0.55) m in mg(L + x) = ½kx² to obtain 334 N (D).

options.distractorRationale: Assumes tension equals mg at the lowest point B because instantaneous speed is zero, confusing v = 0 with a = 0.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses gravitational drop L instead of total drop (L + x) when finding elastic energy.

options.label: C

items.stem: In an overhead hoist beam, a crane overload test block (7 kg) falls from rest at the support through the 3.4 m slack length of an elastic snubber line to point A and is brought momentarily to rest after stretching 1.3 m in a time of 0.36 s to B. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. Determine the time-averaged tension in an elastic snubber line during this 0.36 s interval.
items.workedSolution: Speed when taut at A: v_A = √(2 × 9.81 × 3.4) = 8.17 m s⁻¹ downward. Taking upward positive, (F_mean − mg)Δt = 0 − (−mv_A), so F_mean = mv_A / 0.36 + 7(9.81) = 227 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = mv_A with v_A = √(2gL) to obtain 227 N (D).

options.distractorRationale: Calculates mean resultant upward force mv_A/Δt and forgets to add downward weight mg to find mean cord tension.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts mg from mv_A/Δt instead of adding mg in F_mean − mg = Δp/Δt.

items.stem: Released from rest at the top of an inclined launchway of length 11 m inclined at 32° to the horizontal, a marine slipway cradle of mass 9 kg reaches the bottom with speed 7.8 m s⁻¹. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the coefficient of dynamic friction μ_d between a marine slipway cradle and an inclined launchway?
items.workedSolution: Gravitational potential energy lost ΔE_p = mgL sin 32° = 514 J. Final kinetic energy E_k = ½(9)(7.8)² = 274 J. Frictional energy loss W_f = ΔE_p − E_k = 240 J. Since W_f = μ(mg cos 32°)L, μ = 0.292. Target = 0.292.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔE_p − E_k and normal reaction mg cos 32° accurately to obtain 0.292 (A).

options.distractorRationale: Sets μ = tan θ as if the block descended at constant speed, ignoring the kinetic energy gained.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Swaps sin θ and cos θ in the normal reaction force R = mg cos θ.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses R = mg instead of mg cos θ when relating frictional work to normal contact force.

items.stem: Released from rest at the top of a textured service ramp of length 7.5 m inclined at 34° to the horizontal, a battery transport case of mass 13.5 kg reaches the bottom with speed 5.44 m s⁻¹ against a constant friction force. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the magnitude of the constant friction force opposing its motion?
items.workedSolution: Energy dissipated W_f = mgL sin 34° − ½mv² = 356 J. Constant friction force F_f = W_f / 7.5 = 47.4 N. Released halfway down at unchanged acceleration a, v_half = v / √2 = 3.85 m s⁻¹. Target = 47.4 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies work-energy / constant-acceleration scaling on the incline to obtain 47.4 N (A).

items.stem: Descending a crusty glacier slope of length 18 m and vertical drop 5.4 m at a steady speed of 3.5 m s⁻¹, an expedition supply sled has weight 1200 N. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 1200 × (5.4/18) = 360 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 1.26 × 10³ W. Target = 360 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 360 N (C).

items.stem: Across a flat proving ground, a calibrated ground launcher projects an acoustic ranging dart with initial speed 38 m s⁻¹ at 60° above the horizontal. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What horizontal range does it cover before landing on a flat proving ground?
items.workedSolution: u_y = 38 sin 60° = 32.9 m s⁻¹ and u_x = 38 cos 60° = 19.0 m s⁻¹. Flight time T = 2u_y / 9.8 = 6.72 s; horizontal range R = u_x T = 128 m. Target = 128 m.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves orthogonal components accurately to obtain 128 m (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies horizontal speed by ascent time u sin θ / g instead of full flight time 2u sin θ / g.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes cos θ for sin θ in the flight-time expression.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses the 45° maximum-range formula u²/g without the angle factor sin(2θ).

items.stem: On a polished ice test channel, sled X of mass 2.8 kg moves right at 7 m s⁻¹ and collides with stationary sled Y of mass 3.6 kg. Immediately after impact, sled Y moves right at 4.08 m s⁻¹. What is the speed of sled X immediately after the collision?
items.workedSolution: Momentum conservation: (2.8)(7) = (2.8)v_X + (3.6)(4.08), giving v_X = 1.75 m s⁻¹. K_i = 68.6 J and K_f = 34.3 J, so ΔK_lost = K_i − K_f = 34.3 J. Target = 1.75 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves linear momentum and evaluates kinetic energy budget to obtain 1.75 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: On a level docking-simulator rail, lighter module X of mass 0.8 kg moving right at 14 m s⁻¹ strikes stationary heavier module Y of mass 2.9 kg, causing module Y to move right at 5.07 m s⁻¹ while module X rebounds to the left. How much kinetic energy is dissipated in this rebound collision?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (0.8)(14) = (0.8)v_X + (2.9)(5.07) gives v_X = -4.38 m s⁻¹ (4.38 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(0.8)(4.38)² + ½(2.9)(5.07)² = 44.9 J. Energy lost = 78.4 J − K_f = 33.5 J. Target = 33.5 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 4.38 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 33.5 J (C).

items.stem: In a suspension test gantry, an instrumented pendulum mass of mass 1 kg on a light string of length 2.4 m is released from rest with the string horizontal and coalesces at the lowest point with stationary a magnetic-latch block of mass 1.2 kg. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What maximum vertical height above the lowest point do the joined bodies reach?
items.workedSolution: Pre-impact speed u = √(2gL) = 6.86 m s⁻¹. Tangential momentum conservation gives v = mu / (m + M) = 3.12 m s⁻¹. Post-impact rise h = v² / (2g) = (m/(m+M))² L = 0.496 m; energy lost = mgL − (m+M)gh = 12.8 J. Target = 0.496 m.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves energy during swings and momentum during impact to obtain 0.496 m (B).

items.stem: In a lecture-hall whirl rig, a calibration ball of mass 1.3 kg whirls in a vertical circle of radius 0.5 m on a thin braided string and passes through the lowest point at speed 4.5 m s⁻¹. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the tension in a thin braided string at the lowest point?
items.workedSolution: At the bottom, upward resultant force T − mg = mv²/r. Centripetal force mv²/r = 1.3 × 4.5² / 0.5 = 52.6 N, so T = 52.6 + 1.3 × 9.81 = 65.4 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies T = m(v²/r + g) at the bottom of the circle to obtain 65.4 N (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts weight mg instead of adding mg, confusing the bottom of a vertical circle with the top.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Equates tension directly to centripetal force mv²/r and forgets the downward weight mg.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Sets tension equal to static weight mg, ignoring centripetal acceleration.

items.stem: In a vertical-plane spinner, a gyroscope test mass of mass 3 kg moves in a vertical circle of radius 2 m on a light radial tether, which snaps if tension exceeds 106 N. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the maximum speed a gyroscope test mass can have at the bottom without breaking a light radial tether?
items.workedSolution: Tension is greatest at the bottom where T_max − mg = m v_max² / r. Thus v_max = √[((106/3) − 9.81) × 2] = 7.14 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves T_max − mg = mv²/r to obtain 7.14 m s⁻¹ (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Adds g instead of subtracting g when rearranging T_max − mg = mv²/r.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Treats vertical circular motion as horizontal, omitting weight mg at the lowest point.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes minimum top-of-loop critical speed √(gr) instead of maximum safe bottom speed.

items.stem: Dropped from rest at the anchor in a laboratory ceiling mount, a calibration steel ball of mass 10 kg falls freely 3.6 m until a Hookean rubber cord becomes taut at A, then stretches the cord by 0.7 m over 0.18 s to come momentarily to rest at B. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the mean upward force exerted by a Hookean rubber cord between A and B?
items.workedSolution: Speed when taut at A: v_A = √(2 × 9.8 × 3.6) = 8.40 m s⁻¹ downward. Taking upward positive, (F_mean − mg)Δt = 0 − (−mv_A), so F_mean = mv_A / 0.18 + 10(9.8) = 565 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = mv_A with v_A = √(2gL) to obtain 565 N (A).

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, a proving-ground chassis mule of mass 1400 kg accelerates horizontally so a light-string plumb mass hangs at 18° to the vertical, later climbs a 14° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 50 m (static friction coefficient 0.7), and coasts from 16 m s⁻¹ against a 500 N resistive force toward the recovery marker. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the horizontal acceleration during the initial straight-line phase when a light-string plumb mass deflects by 18°?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 18° = ma and T cos 18° = mg => a = g tan 18° = 3.18 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.7 × 9.8 × 50) = 18.5 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1400)(16)² / 500 = 358 m. Target = 3.18 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 3.18 m s⁻² (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses g sin θ as if on an inclined plane rather than resolving T sin θ = ma and T cos θ = mg to obtain g tan θ.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the ratio of horizontal to vertical components, evaluating g / tan θ instead of g tan θ.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies g by cos θ instead of tan θ.

items.stem: In a chute calibration, a stage ballast crate of mass 3.5 kg descends 10 m from rest down an angled loading board inclined at 30° and exits the base at 5.45 m s⁻¹ under constant friction. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². If the same object is instead released from rest halfway down an angled loading board, what speed does it reach at the bottom?
items.workedSolution: Energy dissipated W_f = mgL sin 30° − ½mv² = 120 J. Constant friction force F_f = W_f / 10 = 12.0 N. Released halfway down at unchanged acceleration a, v_half = v / √2 = 3.85 m s⁻¹. Target = 3.85 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Applies work-energy / constant-acceleration scaling on the incline to obtain 3.85 m s⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: In translational equilibrium at constant speed, a turbine casing pallet (weight 1080 N) travels 29 m down a powerhouse access incline, dropping 7 m vertically. How much gravitational potential energy is lost over the full length of the slope?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed ΔE_k = 0. Potential energy lost = W h = 1080 × 7 = 7.56 × 10³ J. Parallel equilibrium gives F_res = W sin θ = W h / L = 261 N. Target = 7.56 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ = 7/29 and zero net force to obtain 7.56 × 10³ J (B).

items.stem: During a range trial on a level demonstration track, a lecture-hall steel ball leaves a floor-mounted spring cannon at 32 m s⁻¹ and 60° above the horizontal. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the total time of flight before returning to a level demonstration track?
items.workedSolution: u_y = 32 sin 60° = 27.7 m s⁻¹ and u_x = 32 cos 60° = 16.0 m s⁻¹. Flight time T = 2u_y / 9.81 = 5.65 s; horizontal range R = u_x T = 90.4 m. Target = 5.65 s.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves orthogonal components accurately to obtain 5.65 s (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes time to reach the apex u sin θ / g rather than full time of flight.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Swaps sin θ and cos θ when resolving vertical launch speed.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses total speed u instead of vertical component u sin θ.

items.stem: Referring to the launch of an irrigation water packet from a ground-level nozzle at 45 m s⁻¹ and 62° above horizontal farmland: Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². What maximum vertical height above horizontal farmland does it reach?
items.workedSolution: At the apex v_y = 0 while horizontal velocity remains constant at v_apex = u cos 62° = 21.1 m s⁻¹. Maximum height h_max = (u sin 62°)² / (2g) = 80.5 m. Target = 80.5 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_y = 0 and constant v_x = u cos 62° at apex to obtain 80.5 m (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Converts all initial kinetic energy into gravitational potential energy, forgetting non-zero horizontal speed u cos θ at the apex.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses horizontal component u cos θ instead of vertical component u sin θ in h = u_y² / (2g).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of two in the denominator of h_max = u_y² / (2g).

items.stem: In a rebound impact on a smooth marshalling test track, wagon X (mass 2 kg, initial speed 7 m s⁻¹ right) hits stationary wagon Y (mass 5.6 kg), which moves right at 3.27 m s⁻¹. What is the total kinetic energy of the two bodies immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (2)(7) = (2)v_X + (5.6)(3.27) gives v_X = -2.16 m s⁻¹ (2.16 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(2)(2.16)² + ½(5.6)(3.27)² = 34.6 J. Energy lost = 49.0 J − K_f = 14.4 J. Target = 34.6 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 2.16 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 34.6 J (B).

items.stem: On a horizontal frictionless air track, glider X of mass 3.5 kg moves right at 11 m s⁻¹ toward glider Y of mass 2.4 kg approaching head-on to the left at 2.5 m s⁻¹ (initial arrow on Y omitted). Immediately after collision, glider Y moves right at 4 m s⁻¹. What is the velocity of glider X immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward as positive: p_before = (3.5)(11) + (2.4)(−2.5) = 32.5 kg m s⁻¹. From p_before = (3.5)v_X + (2.4)(4), v_X = 6.54 m s⁻¹, which is 6.54 m s⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: Uses signed head-on momentum p_before = 32.5 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 6.54 m s⁻¹ to the right (C).

items.stem: In a laboratory swing frame, a brass impact sphere of mass 1.3 kg hangs on a 2 m string, is released from rest with the string horizontal, and collides inelastically at the bottom with stationary a wax capture block of mass 2.34 kg. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the tension in the string immediately before a brass impact sphere strikes a wax capture block?
items.workedSolution: Just before collision u² = 2gL => u = 6.26 m s⁻¹. Radial Newton second law T − mg = mu²/L = 2mg gives T = 3mg = 38.3 N. Momentum conservation gives v = mu/(m+M) = 2.24 m s⁻¹. Target = 38.3 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates quarter-swing dynamics and radial/tangential laws to obtain 38.3 N (C).

items.stem: At the bottom of a vertical circle of radius 0.6 m in a dynamic tension rig, a forged test weight of mass 0.9 kg travels at 8 m s⁻¹ while attached to a taut braided wire. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². Calculate the tension in a taut braided wire.
items.workedSolution: At the bottom, upward resultant force T − mg = mv²/r. Centripetal force mv²/r = 0.9 × 8² / 0.6 = 96.0 N, so T = 96.0 + 0.9 × 9.81 = 105 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies T = m(v²/r + g) at the bottom of the circle to obtain 105 N (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts weight mg instead of adding mg, confusing the bottom of a vertical circle with the top.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Equates tension directly to centripetal force mv²/r and forgets the downward weight mg.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Sets tension equal to static weight mg, ignoring centripetal acceleration.

items.stem: In a laboratory ceiling mount, a calibration steel ball of mass 10 kg is released from rest at the anchor of a Hookean rubber cord of unstretched length 3.2 m. The cord becomes taut at A and stretches obeying Hooke's law by a maximum extension of 0.95 m over 0.2 s before a calibration steel ball comes momentarily to rest at B. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the spring constant of a Hookean rubber cord?
items.workedSolution: Total vertical drop from release S to lowest point B is L + x = 3.2 + 0.95 = 4.15 m. By energy conservation mg(L + x) = ½kx², giving k = 2mg(L + x)/x² = 901 N m⁻¹ and peak tension T_B = kx = 856 N. Target = 901 N m⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses full vertical drop (3.2 + 0.95) m in mg(L + x) = ½kx² to obtain 901 N m⁻¹ (A).
