items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, a mine-tunnel shuttle vehicle of mass 1700 kg accelerates horizontally so a ceiling pendulum sensor hangs at 22° to the vertical, later climbs a 12° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 50 m (static friction coefficient 0.85), and coasts from 22 m s⁻¹ against a 530 N resistive force toward the shaft station. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the horizontal acceleration during the initial straight-line phase when a ceiling pendulum sensor deflects by 22°?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 22° = ma and T cos 22° = mg => a = g tan 22° = 3.96 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.85 × 9.81 × 50) = 20.4 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1700)(22)² / 530 = 776 m. Target = 3.96 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 3.96 m s⁻² (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses g sin θ as if on an inclined plane rather than resolving T sin θ = ma and T cos θ = mg to obtain g tan θ.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the ratio of horizontal to vertical components, evaluating g / tan θ instead of g tan θ.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies g by cos θ instead of tan θ.

items.stem: The diagram shows an instrumented cargo crate of mass 4.5 kg starting from rest and descending 5 m down a straight steel loading chute angled at 28°, attaining 4.54 m s⁻¹ at the bottom. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the coefficient of dynamic friction μ_d between an instrumented cargo crate and a straight steel loading chute?
items.workedSolution: Gravitational potential energy lost ΔE_p = mgL sin 28° = 104 J. Final kinetic energy E_k = ½(4.5)(4.54)² = 46.4 J. Frictional energy loss W_f = ΔE_p − E_k = 57.1 J. Since W_f = μ(mg cos 28°)L, μ = 0.294. Target = 0.294.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔE_p − E_k and normal reaction mg cos 28° accurately to obtain 0.294 (B).

items.stem: The diagram depicts a mining equipment skid weighing 840 N moving at constant speed down a straight haulage incline of length 11 m and vertical height 5.7 m. What is the magnitude of the resistive force opposing motion along the slope?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed ΔE_k = 0. Potential energy lost = W h = 840 × 5.7 = 4.79 × 10³ J. Parallel equilibrium gives F_res = W sin θ = W h / L = 435 N. Target = 435 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ = 5.7/11 and zero net force to obtain 435 N (C).

items.stem: The diagram shows a heavy logistics crate of weight 1350 N moving at constant speed 4 m s⁻¹ down a rough warehouse ramp of slope length 14 m and height 6.3 m. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 1350 × (6.3/14) = 608 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 2.43 × 10³ W. Target = 608 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 608 N (C).

items.stem: Referring to the launch of a hail-impact test sphere from an angled gas gun at 42 m s⁻¹ and 28° above a horizontal test hall: Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.8 m s⁻². What maximum vertical height above a horizontal test hall does it reach?
items.workedSolution: At the apex v_y = 0 while horizontal velocity remains constant at v_apex = u cos 28° = 37.1 m s⁻¹. Maximum height h_max = (u sin 28°)² / (2g) = 19.8 m. Target = 19.8 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_y = 0 and constant v_x = u cos 28° at apex to obtain 19.8 m (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Converts all initial kinetic energy into gravitational potential energy, forgetting non-zero horizontal speed u cos θ at the apex.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses horizontal component u cos θ instead of vertical component u sin θ in h = u_y² / (2g).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of two in the denominator of h_max = u_y² / (2g).

items.stem: The diagram shows glider X of mass 1.6 kg moving right at 6 m s⁻¹ toward stationary glider Y of mass 0.8 kg on a horizontal frictionless air track; after collision, glider Y travels right at 5.06 m s⁻¹. What is the speed of glider X immediately after the collision?
items.workedSolution: Momentum conservation: (1.6)(6) = (1.6)v_X + (0.8)(5.06), giving v_X = 3.47 m s⁻¹. K_i = 28.8 J and K_f = 19.9 J, so ΔK_lost = K_i − K_f = 8.93 J. Target = 3.47 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves linear momentum and evaluates kinetic energy budget to obtain 3.47 m s⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: Along a smooth marshalling test track, wagon X of mass 2 kg travelling right at 13 m s⁻¹ meets wagon Y of mass 3.6 kg travelling left at 6 m s⁻¹ (not drawn). After impact wagon Y rebounds right at 4 m s⁻¹. What is the post-collision velocity of wagon X?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward as positive: p_before = (2)(13) + (3.6)(−6) = 4.40 kg m s⁻¹. From p_before = (2)v_X + (3.6)(4), v_X = -5.00 m s⁻¹, which is 5.00 m s⁻¹ to the left.

markScheme.criterion: Uses signed head-on momentum p_before = 4.40 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 5.00 m s⁻¹ to the left (C).

items.stem: The diagram shows a steel pendulum bob of mass 0.8 kg swinging from a horizontal 1.5 m string in a ballistic pendulum rig to couple with stationary a lump of modelling clay of mass 2 kg at the lowest point. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What maximum vertical height above the lowest point do the joined bodies reach?
items.workedSolution: Pre-impact speed u = √(2gL) = 5.42 m s⁻¹. Tangential momentum conservation gives v = mu / (m + M) = 1.55 m s⁻¹. Post-impact rise h = v² / (2g) = (m/(m+M))² L = 0.122 m; energy lost = mgL − (m+M)gh = 8.41 J. Target = 0.122 m.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves energy during swings and momentum during impact to obtain 0.122 m (B).

items.stem: The diagram shows a steel sensor sphere of mass 0.7 kg moving at 6.5 m s⁻¹ through the bottom of a vertical circle of radius 1.7 m on a light inextensible wire in a vertical circular test rig. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.8 m s⁻². What tension acts in a light inextensible wire?
items.workedSolution: At the bottom, upward resultant force T − mg = mv²/r. Centripetal force mv²/r = 0.7 × 6.5² / 1.7 = 17.4 N, so T = 17.4 + 0.7 × 9.8 = 24.3 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies T = m(v²/r + g) at the bottom of the circle to obtain 24.3 N (A).

items.stem: The diagram shows a telemetry capsule (2.2 kg) at the bottom of a vertical circle of radius 2 m in a vertical rotation stand; a high-tensile cord has a maximum safe tension of 95 N. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the maximum allowed speed at this point?
items.workedSolution: Tension is greatest at the bottom where T_max − mg = m v_max² / r. Thus v_max = √[((95/2.2) − 9.81) × 2] = 8.17 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves T_max − mg = mv²/r to obtain 8.17 m s⁻¹ (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds g instead of subtracting g when rearranging T_max − mg = mv²/r.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats vertical circular motion as horizontal, omitting weight mg at the lowest point.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes minimum top-of-loop critical speed √(gr) instead of maximum safe bottom speed.

items.stem: The diagram illustrates a mountaineering test mass of mass 2 kg released at the support of a dynamic climbing rope (natural length 2.6 m), becoming taut at A and decelerating to rest at B (extension 1.2 m) over 0.33 s. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What mean force does a dynamic climbing rope exert between A and B?
items.workedSolution: Speed when taut at A: v_A = √(2 × 9.81 × 2.6) = 7.14 m s⁻¹ downward. Taking upward positive, (F_mean − mg)Δt = 0 − (−mv_A), so F_mean = mv_A / 0.33 + 2(9.81) = 62.9 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = mv_A with v_A = √(2gL) to obtain 62.9 N (D).

options.distractorRationale: Calculates mean resultant upward force mv_A/Δt and forgets to add downward weight mg to find mean cord tension.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts mg from mv_A/Δt instead of adding mg in F_mean − mg = Δp/Δt.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies momentum change mv_A by Δt instead of dividing by Δt.

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, an instrumented test truck of mass 1800 kg accelerates horizontally so a ceiling-suspended plumb bob hangs at 18° to the vertical, later climbs a 14° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 45 m (static friction coefficient 0.55), and coasts from 15 m s⁻¹ against a 410 N resistive force toward the terminal bay. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the horizontal acceleration during the initial straight-line phase when a ceiling-suspended plumb bob deflects by 18°?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 18° = ma and T cos 18° = mg => a = g tan 18° = 3.18 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.55 × 9.8 × 45) = 15.6 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1800)(15)² / 410 = 494 m. Target = 3.18 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 3.18 m s⁻² (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses g sin θ as if on an inclined plane rather than resolving T sin θ = ma and T cos θ = mg to obtain g tan θ.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the ratio of horizontal to vertical components, evaluating g / tan θ instead of g tan θ.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies g by cos θ instead of tan θ.

items.stem: On a pitched workshop plank (7.5 m long, angled at 22° to the horizontal), a timber tool chest of mass 5.5 kg slides from rest and attains 4.45 m s⁻¹ at the base against constant kinetic friction. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. If the same object is instead released from rest halfway down a pitched workshop plank, what speed does it reach at the bottom?
items.workedSolution: Energy dissipated W_f = mgL sin 22° − ½mv² = 97.1 J. Constant friction force F_f = W_f / 7.5 = 13.0 N. Released halfway down at unchanged acceleration a, v_half = v / √2 = 3.15 m s⁻¹. Target = 3.15 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Applies work-energy / constant-acceleration scaling on the incline to obtain 3.15 m s⁻¹ (B).

options.distractorRationale: Assumes final speed scales linearly with distance (v/2) instead of with √s (v/√2) under constant acceleration.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Divides speed by four instead of √2 when halving the release distance.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes frictionless half-ramp speed and ignores the constant friction force.

items.stem: The diagram shows an expedition supply sled of weight 350 N moving at constant speed 3.5 m s⁻¹ down a crusty glacier slope of slope length 16 m and height 4.8 m. At what rate is mechanical energy converted into thermal energy?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 350 × (4.8/16) = 105 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 368 W. Target = 368 W.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 368 W (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies full vertical weight W by speed v, omitting sin θ = h/L.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates total gravitational energy Wh in joules instead of rate of thermal dissipation in watts.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies normal reaction W cos θ by speed v despite normal force being perpendicular to velocity.

items.stem: The diagram shows an acoustic ranging dart launched at 26 m s⁻¹ inclined at 38° to a flat proving ground. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.8 m s⁻². What horizontal range does it cover before landing on a flat proving ground?
items.workedSolution: u_y = 26 sin 38° = 16.0 m s⁻¹ and u_x = 26 cos 38° = 20.5 m s⁻¹. Flight time T = 2u_y / 9.8 = 3.27 s; horizontal range R = u_x T = 66.9 m. Target = 66.9 m.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves orthogonal components accurately to obtain 66.9 m (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies horizontal speed by ascent time u sin θ / g instead of full flight time 2u sin θ / g.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes cos θ for sin θ in the flight-time expression.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses the 45° maximum-range formula u²/g without the angle factor sin(2θ).

items.stem: Travelling at 6 m s⁻¹ to the right along a horizontal magnetic-bearing guideway, shuttle X (5.2 kg) strikes stationary shuttle Y (3.2 kg), sending shuttle Y rightward at 4.42 m s⁻¹. What is the speed of shuttle X immediately after the collision?
items.workedSolution: Momentum conservation: (5.2)(6) = (5.2)v_X + (3.2)(4.42), giving v_X = 3.28 m s⁻¹. K_i = 93.6 J and K_f = 59.2 J, so ΔK_lost = K_i − K_f = 34.4 J. Target = 3.28 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves linear momentum and evaluates kinetic energy budget to obtain 3.28 m s⁻¹ (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Assumes both bodies stick together instead of using the measured post-collision speed of Y.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds m_Y v_Y instead of subtracting m_Y v_Y when solving momentum conservation.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Assumes kinetic energy is conserved in an inelastic collision.

items.stem: Moving rightward at 16 m s⁻¹ on a frictionless optical-bench track, carriage X (1.8 kg) collides head-on with stationary carriage Y (5.4 kg); immediately afterward carriage Y travels right at 6.53 m s⁻¹ and carriage X rebounds backward. What is the total kinetic energy of the two bodies immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (1.8)(16) = (1.8)v_X + (5.4)(6.53) gives v_X = -3.59 m s⁻¹ (3.59 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(1.8)(3.59)² + ½(5.4)(6.53)² = 127 J. Energy lost = 230 J − K_f = 104 J. Target = 127 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 3.59 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 127 J (B).

options.distractorRationale: Subtracts the kinetic energy of rebounding X from Y as if kinetic energy were a signed vector.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Includes only the kinetic energy of Y and forgets the kinetic energy of rebounding X.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Assumes the collision is perfectly elastic and equates K_f to K_i.

items.stem: Released from rest from a horizontal string position of length 1.4 m in a fracture-toughness pendulum, a hardened striker ball (0.8 kg) strikes and sticks to stationary a soft polymer target (0.96 kg) at the bottom of its arc. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. How much mechanical energy is dissipated during the sticking collision?
items.workedSolution: Pre-impact speed u = √(2gL) = 5.24 m s⁻¹. Tangential momentum conservation gives v = mu / (m + M) = 2.38 m s⁻¹. Post-impact rise h = v² / (2g) = (m/(m+M))² L = 0.289 m; energy lost = mgL − (m+M)gh = 5.99 J. Target = 5.99 J.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves energy during swings and momentum during impact to obtain 5.99 J (A).

items.stem: The diagram shows a chrome-steel bob of mass 2.3 kg released from a horizontal 1.4 m string in a ceiling-mounted swing test toward stationary a resin absorber block of mass 3.22 kg at the bottom. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the tension in the string immediately before a chrome-steel bob strikes a resin absorber block?
items.workedSolution: Just before collision u² = 2gL => u = 5.24 m s⁻¹. Radial Newton second law T − mg = mu²/L = 2mg gives T = 3mg = 67.7 N. Momentum conservation gives v = mu/(m+M) = 2.18 m s⁻¹. Target = 67.7 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates quarter-swing dynamics and radial/tangential laws to obtain 67.7 N (B).

items.stem: Whirled in a vertical circle of radius 2.2 m on a light inextensible string (breaking tension 63 N) in a circular motion demonstrator, a polymer-coated mass has mass 1.6 kg. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. Determine the greatest safe speed at the lowest point.
items.workedSolution: Tension is greatest at the bottom where T_max − mg = m v_max² / r. Thus v_max = √[((63/1.6) − 9.81) × 2.2] = 8.06 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves T_max − mg = mv²/r to obtain 8.06 m s⁻¹ (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds g instead of subtracting g when rearranging T_max − mg = mv²/r.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats vertical circular motion as horizontal, omitting weight mg at the lowest point.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes minimum top-of-loop critical speed √(gr) instead of maximum safe bottom speed.

items.stem: Released from rest at the support in a vertical deceleration shaft, a payload shock capsule (5.5 kg) falls freely through the 3 m natural length of a compliant elastomer rope to point A and then extends the Hookean cord by 1.15 m during 0.14 s to instantaneous rest at B. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What is the peak tension in a compliant elastomer rope at the lowest point B?
items.workedSolution: Total vertical drop from release S to lowest point B is L + x = 3 + 1.15 = 4.15 m. By energy conservation mg(L + x) = ½kx², giving k = 2mg(L + x)/x² = 338 N m⁻¹ and peak tension T_B = kx = 389 N. Target = 389 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses full vertical drop (3 + 1.15) m in mg(L + x) = ½kx² to obtain 389 N (A).

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, an electric quarry haulage rig of mass 1800 kg accelerates horizontally so a suspended brass bob hangs at 18° to the vertical, later climbs a 10° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 75 m (static friction coefficient 0.5), and coasts from 18 m s⁻¹ against a 470 N resistive force toward the weighbridge. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What is the horizontal acceleration during the initial straight-line phase when a suspended brass bob deflects by 18°?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 18° = ma and T cos 18° = mg => a = g tan 18° = 3.19 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.5 × 9.81 × 75) = 19.2 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1800)(18)² / 470 = 620 m. Target = 3.19 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 3.19 m s⁻² (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses g sin θ as if on an inclined plane rather than resolving T sin θ = ma and T cos θ = mg to obtain g tan θ.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the ratio of horizontal to vertical components, evaluating g / tan θ instead of g tan θ.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies g by cos θ instead of tan θ.

items.stem: Released from rest at the top of a hillside guide track of length 11.5 m inclined at 28° to the horizontal, a forestry sled carriage of mass 14 kg reaches the bottom with speed 8.44 m s⁻¹. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the coefficient of kinetic friction μ (defined by F_f = μ R) between a forestry sled carriage and a hillside guide track?
items.workedSolution: Gravitational potential energy lost ΔE_p = mgL sin 28° = 741 J. Final kinetic energy E_k = ½(14)(8.44)² = 499 J. Frictional energy loss W_f = ΔE_p − E_k = 243 J. Since W_f = μ(mg cos 28°)L, μ = 0.174. Target = 0.174.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔE_p − E_k and normal reaction mg cos 28° accurately to obtain 0.174 (C).

items.stem: Sliding at constant velocity down a planar ski run of slope length 25 m and vertical drop 8 m, a snowcat maintenance sled has weight 1680 N. What is the magnitude of the resistive force opposing motion along the slope?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed ΔE_k = 0. Potential energy lost = W h = 1680 × 8 = 1.34 × 10⁴ J. Parallel equilibrium gives F_res = W sin θ = W h / L = 538 N. Target = 538 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ = 8/25 and zero net force to obtain 538 N (D).

items.stem: Descending a greased timber way of length 20 m and vertical drop 12 m at a steady speed of 1.5 m s⁻¹, a shipyard launch block has weight 300 N. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 300 × (12/20) = 180 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 270 W. Target = 180 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 180 N (D).

items.stem: Projected from a pneumatic pitching machine at 30 m s⁻¹ at an angle of 28° above a level turf pitch, a sports-science test ball follows a parabolic arc. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the speed of the projectile at the highest point of its trajectory?
items.workedSolution: At the apex v_y = 0 while horizontal velocity remains constant at v_apex = u cos 28° = 26.5 m s⁻¹. Maximum height h_max = (u sin 28°)² / (2g) = 10.1 m. Target = 26.5 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_y = 0 and constant v_x = u cos 28° at apex to obtain 26.5 m s⁻¹ (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Assumes the projectile is momentarily stationary at its highest point, forgetting its constant horizontal velocity u cos θ.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses u sin θ instead of u cos θ for the speed at the apex.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Assumes speed remains equal to launch speed u throughout the flight.

items.stem: On a level low-friction dynamics rail, lighter cart X of mass 0.8 kg moving right at 16 m s⁻¹ strikes stationary heavier cart Y of mass 2.2 kg, causing cart Y to move right at 7.31 m s⁻¹ while cart X rebounds to the left. How much kinetic energy is dissipated in this rebound collision?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (0.8)(16) = (0.8)v_X + (2.2)(7.31) gives v_X = -4.10 m s⁻¹ (4.10 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(0.8)(4.10)² + ½(2.2)(7.31)² = 65.5 J. Energy lost = 102 J − K_f = 36.9 J. Target = 36.9 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 4.10 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 36.9 J (B).

items.stem: Approaching each other along a level docking-simulator rail, module X (1 kg, 12 m s⁻¹ to the right) collides head-on with module Y (1.8 kg, 3.5 m s⁻¹ to the left, arrow not shown); afterward module Y travels to the right at 4.5 m s⁻¹. Determine the final velocity of module X.
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward as positive: p_before = (1)(12) + (1.8)(−3.5) = 5.70 kg m s⁻¹. From p_before = (1)v_X + (1.8)(4.5), v_X = -2.40 m s⁻¹, which is 2.40 m s⁻¹ to the left.

markScheme.criterion: Uses signed head-on momentum p_before = 5.70 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 2.40 m s⁻¹ to the left (D).

items.stem: In a light-string pendulum, a physics lecture bob of mass 0.3 kg hangs on a 1.8 m string, is released from rest with the string horizontal, and collides inelastically at the bottom with stationary a stationary putty sphere of mass 0.66 kg. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the tension in the string immediately before a physics lecture bob strikes a stationary putty sphere?
items.workedSolution: Just before collision u² = 2gL => u = 5.94 m s⁻¹. Radial Newton second law T − mg = mu²/L = 2mg gives T = 3mg = 8.83 N. Momentum conservation gives v = mu/(m+M) = 1.86 m s⁻¹. Target = 8.83 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates quarter-swing dynamics and radial/tangential laws to obtain 8.83 N (D).

options.label: B

items.stem: In a vertical swing circle, a polished alloy bob of mass 0.9 kg whirls in a vertical circle of radius 0.7 m on a light suspension line and passes through the lowest point at speed 5 m s⁻¹. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the tension in a light suspension line at the lowest point?
items.workedSolution: At the bottom, upward resultant force T − mg = mv²/r. Centripetal force mv²/r = 0.9 × 5² / 0.7 = 32.1 N, so T = 32.1 + 0.9 × 9.8 = 41.0 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies T = m(v²/r + g) at the bottom of the circle to obtain 41.0 N (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts weight mg instead of adding mg, confusing the bottom of a vertical circle with the top.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Equates tension directly to centripetal force mv²/r and forgets the downward weight mg.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Sets tension equal to static weight mg, ignoring centripetal acceleration.

items.stem: In a dry-test tower, a marine mooring weight of mass 6.5 kg is released from rest at the anchor of a stretchable nylon hawser of unstretched length 4 m. The cord becomes taut at A and stretches obeying Hooke's law by a maximum extension of 0.55 m over 0.32 s before a marine mooring weight comes momentarily to rest at B. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the spring constant of a stretchable nylon hawser?
items.workedSolution: Total vertical drop from release S to lowest point B is L + x = 4 + 0.55 = 4.55 m. By energy conservation mg(L + x) = ½kx², giving k = 2mg(L + x)/x² = 1.92 × 10³ N m⁻¹ and peak tension T_B = kx = 1.06 × 10³ N. Target = 1.92 × 10³ N m⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses full vertical drop (4 + 0.55) m in mg(L + x) = ½kx² to obtain 1.92 × 10³ N m⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: Dropped from rest at the anchor in a drop-test tower, an instrumented drop sphere of mass 8 kg falls freely 2.4 m until an elastic bungee tether becomes taut at A, then stretches the cord by 1 m over 0.24 s to come momentarily to rest at B. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the mean upward force exerted by an elastic bungee tether between A and B?
items.workedSolution: Speed when taut at A: v_A = √(2 × 9.81 × 2.4) = 6.86 m s⁻¹ downward. Taking upward positive, (F_mean − mg)Δt = 0 − (−mv_A), so F_mean = mv_A / 0.24 + 8(9.81) = 307 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = mv_A with v_A = √(2gL) to obtain 307 N (A).

items.stem: During a surface-wear test on a planar terminal slide (10.5 m long, 28° above the horizontal), a baggage transfer container of mass 5.5 kg slides from rest to a bottom speed of 7.77 m s⁻¹. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.8 m s⁻². How much mechanical energy is dissipated against friction during the descent?
items.workedSolution: Gravitational potential energy lost ΔE_p = mgL sin 28° = 266 J. Final kinetic energy E_k = ½(5.5)(7.77)² = 166 J. Frictional energy loss W_f = ΔE_p − E_k = 99.7 J. Since W_f = μ(mg cos 28°)L, μ = 0.199. Target = 99.7 J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔE_p − E_k and normal reaction mg cos 28° accurately to obtain 99.7 J (C).

items.stem: In a chute calibration, a shipyard keel block of mass 11.5 kg descends 4.5 m from rest down a dry-dock slip plank inclined at 38° and exits the base at 4.79 m s⁻¹ under constant friction. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². If the same object is instead released from rest halfway down a dry-dock slip plank, what speed does it reach at the bottom?
items.workedSolution: Energy dissipated W_f = mgL sin 38° − ½mv² = 181 J. Constant friction force F_f = W_f / 4.5 = 40.1 N. Released halfway down at unchanged acceleration a, v_half = v / √2 = 3.39 m s⁻¹. Target = 3.39 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Applies work-energy / constant-acceleration scaling on the incline to obtain 3.39 m s⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: While sliding down a planar test embankment (22 m long, 7.7 m vertical height) at constant speed 2.5 m s⁻¹, a civil-engineering gabion of weight 1350 N converts lost potential energy into heat. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 1350 × (7.7/22) = 473 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 1.18 × 10³ W. Target = 473 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 473 N (C).

items.stem: Across a level turf pitch, a pneumatic pitching machine projects a sports-science test ball with initial speed 14 m s⁻¹ at 34° above the horizontal. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What horizontal range does it cover before landing on a level turf pitch?
items.workedSolution: u_y = 14 sin 34° = 7.83 m s⁻¹ and u_x = 14 cos 34° = 11.6 m s⁻¹. Flight time T = 2u_y / 9.8 = 1.60 s; horizontal range R = u_x T = 18.5 m. Target = 18.5 m.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves orthogonal components accurately to obtain 18.5 m (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies horizontal speed by ascent time u sin θ / g instead of full flight time 2u sin θ / g.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes cos θ for sin θ in the flight-time expression.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses the 45° maximum-range formula u²/g without the angle factor sin(2θ).

items.stem: During an inelastic collision trial on a level docking-simulator rail, module X (mass 4.4 kg, initial rightward speed 4 m s⁻¹) hits stationary module Y (mass 0.8 kg), which moves off to the right at 4.28 m s⁻¹. What is the speed of module X immediately after the collision?
items.workedSolution: Momentum conservation: (4.4)(4) = (4.4)v_X + (0.8)(4.28), giving v_X = 3.22 m s⁻¹. K_i = 35.2 J and K_f = 30.2 J, so ΔK_lost = K_i − K_f = 5.04 J. Target = 3.22 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves linear momentum and evaluates kinetic energy budget to obtain 3.22 m s⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: On a precision gas-bearing trough, lighter rider X of mass 1 kg moving right at 7 m s⁻¹ strikes stationary heavier rider Y of mass 3.2 kg, causing rider Y to move right at 2.82 m s⁻¹ while rider X rebounds to the left. How much kinetic energy is dissipated in this rebound collision?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (1)(7) = (1)v_X + (3.2)(2.82) gives v_X = -2.02 m s⁻¹ (2.02 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(1)(2.02)² + ½(3.2)(2.82)² = 14.8 J. Energy lost = 24.5 J − K_f = 9.73 J. Target = 9.73 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 2.02 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 9.73 J (B).

items.stem: In a ballistic pendulum rig, a steel pendulum bob of mass 0.4 kg on a light string of length 1.1 m is released from rest with the string horizontal and coalesces at the lowest point with stationary a lump of modelling clay of mass 0.32 kg. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What maximum vertical height above the lowest point do the joined bodies reach?
items.workedSolution: Pre-impact speed u = √(2gL) = 4.64 m s⁻¹. Tangential momentum conservation gives v = mu / (m + M) = 2.58 m s⁻¹. Post-impact rise h = v² / (2g) = (m/(m+M))² L = 0.340 m; energy lost = mgL − (m+M)gh = 1.92 J. Target = 0.340 m.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves energy during swings and momentum during impact to obtain 0.340 m (C).

items.stem: At the bottom of a vertical circle of radius 1 m in a vertical-plane spinner, a gyroscope test mass of mass 1.5 kg travels at 6.5 m s⁻¹ while attached to a light radial tether. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². Calculate the tension in a light radial tether.
items.workedSolution: At the bottom, upward resultant force T − mg = mv²/r. Centripetal force mv²/r = 1.5 × 6.5² / 1 = 63.4 N, so T = 63.4 + 1.5 × 9.81 = 78.1 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies T = m(v²/r + g) at the bottom of the circle to obtain 78.1 N (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts weight mg instead of adding mg, confusing the bottom of a vertical circle with the top.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Equates tension directly to centripetal force mv²/r and forgets the downward weight mg.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Sets tension equal to static weight mg, ignoring centripetal acceleration.

items.stem: During a tensile limit test in a lecture-hall whirl rig, a calibration ball of mass 2.4 kg swings on a thin braided string of length 0.8 m rated to 76 N maximum tension. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². Calculate the maximum speed at the bottom of the path.
items.workedSolution: Tension is greatest at the bottom where T_max − mg = m v_max² / r. Thus v_max = √[((76/2.4) − 9.81) × 0.8] = 4.18 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves T_max − mg = mv²/r to obtain 4.18 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Adds g instead of subtracting g when rearranging T_max − mg = mv²/r.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Treats vertical circular motion as horizontal, omitting weight mg at the lowest point.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes minimum top-of-loop critical speed √(gr) instead of maximum safe bottom speed.

items.stem: During an impulse-arrest test in a vertical deceleration shaft, a payload shock capsule of mass 12 kg drops freely 4.6 m to taut point A and extends a compliant elastomer rope by 1.3 m over 0.3 s until instantaneous rest at B. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.8 m s⁻². Calculate the mean upward cord force during deceleration.
items.workedSolution: Speed when taut at A: v_A = √(2 × 9.8 × 4.6) = 9.50 m s⁻¹ downward. Taking upward positive, (F_mean − mg)Δt = 0 − (−mv_A), so F_mean = mv_A / 0.3 + 12(9.8) = 497 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = mv_A with v_A = √(2gL) to obtain 497 N (A).

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, an articulated test coach of mass 1600 kg accelerates horizontally so a roof-mounted plumb sphere hangs at 30° to the vertical, later climbs a 14° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 85 m (static friction coefficient 0.45), and coasts from 15 m s⁻¹ against a 410 N resistive force toward the timing gate. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the horizontal acceleration during the initial straight-line phase when a roof-mounted plumb sphere deflects by 30°?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 30° = ma and T cos 30° = mg => a = g tan 30° = 5.66 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.45 × 9.8 × 85) = 19.4 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1600)(15)² / 410 = 439 m. Target = 5.66 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 5.66 m s⁻² (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses g sin θ as if on an inclined plane rather than resolving T sin θ = ma and T cos θ = mg to obtain g tan θ.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the ratio of horizontal to vertical components, evaluating g / tan θ instead of g tan θ.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies g by cos θ instead of tan θ.

items.stem: The diagram illustrates a vulcanized rubber block (13 kg) released from rest at the top of a brushed concrete incline of length 4 m and angle 30°, arriving at the bottom at 3.76 m s⁻¹. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the magnitude of the constant friction force opposing its motion?
items.workedSolution: Energy dissipated W_f = mgL sin 30° − ½mv² = 163 J. Constant friction force F_f = W_f / 4 = 40.8 N. Released halfway down at unchanged acceleration a, v_half = v / √2 = 2.66 m s⁻¹. Target = 40.8 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies work-energy / constant-acceleration scaling on the incline to obtain 40.8 N (C).

items.stem: The diagram depicts a transformer housing weighing 560 N moving at constant speed down a substation access slope of length 14 m and vertical height 3.9 m. What is the magnitude of the resistive force opposing motion along the slope?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed ΔE_k = 0. Potential energy lost = W h = 560 × 3.9 = 2.18 × 10³ J. Parallel equilibrium gives F_res = W sin θ = W h / L = 156 N. Target = 156 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ = 3.9/14 and zero net force to obtain 156 N (B).

items.stem: The diagram shows a volcanic ballistic clast launched at 30 m s⁻¹ inclined at 64° to a flat ash plain. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What horizontal range does it cover before landing on a flat ash plain?
items.workedSolution: u_y = 30 sin 64° = 27.0 m s⁻¹ and u_x = 30 cos 64° = 13.2 m s⁻¹. Flight time T = 2u_y / 9.81 = 5.50 s; horizontal range R = u_x T = 72.3 m. Target = 72.3 m.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves orthogonal components accurately to obtain 72.3 m (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies horizontal speed by ascent time u sin θ / g instead of full flight time 2u sin θ / g.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes cos θ for sin θ in the flight-time expression.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses the 45° maximum-range formula u²/g without the angle factor sin(2θ).

items.stem: In a kinematics experiment over calm water at launch level, a rescue line-throwing bob is launched at 30 m s⁻¹ and 55° above the horizontal. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the speed of the projectile at the highest point of its trajectory?
items.workedSolution: At the apex v_y = 0 while horizontal velocity remains constant at v_apex = u cos 55° = 17.2 m s⁻¹. Maximum height h_max = (u sin 55°)² / (2g) = 30.8 m. Target = 17.2 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_y = 0 and constant v_x = u cos 55° at apex to obtain 17.2 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Assumes the projectile is momentarily stationary at its highest point, forgetting its constant horizontal velocity u cos θ.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses u sin θ instead of u cos θ for the speed at the apex.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Assumes speed remains equal to launch speed u throughout the flight.

items.stem: The diagram shows trolley X of mass 1.8 kg approaching stationary trolley Y of mass 5.8 kg at 16 m s⁻¹ on a smooth glass collision groove. After impact, trolley Y moves right at 6.66 m s⁻¹. How much kinetic energy is dissipated in this rebound collision?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (1.8)(16) = (1.8)v_X + (5.8)(6.66) gives v_X = -5.46 m s⁻¹ (5.46 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(1.8)(5.46)² + ½(5.8)(6.66)² = 155 J. Energy lost = 230 J − K_f = 74.9 J. Target = 74.9 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 5.46 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 74.9 J (C).

items.stem: On a level cleanroom linear rail, carrier X of mass 4 kg moves right at 5 m s⁻¹ toward carrier Y of mass 1.2 kg approaching head-on to the left at 4.5 m s⁻¹ (initial arrow on Y omitted). Immediately after collision, carrier Y moves right at 4 m s⁻¹. What is the velocity of carrier X immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward as positive: p_before = (4)(5) + (1.2)(−4.5) = 14.6 kg m s⁻¹. From p_before = (4)v_X + (1.2)(4), v_X = 2.45 m s⁻¹, which is 2.45 m s⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: Uses signed head-on momentum p_before = 14.6 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 2.45 m s⁻¹ to the right (D).

items.stem: The diagram shows a cast-iron hammer bob of mass 0.7 kg released from a horizontal 0.8 m string in a Charpy-style swing rig toward stationary a deformable putty mass of mass 0.98 kg at the bottom. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the tension in the string immediately before a cast-iron hammer bob strikes a deformable putty mass?
items.workedSolution: Just before collision u² = 2gL => u = 3.96 m s⁻¹. Radial Newton second law T − mg = mu²/L = 2mg gives T = 3mg = 20.6 N. Momentum conservation gives v = mu/(m+M) = 1.65 m s⁻¹. Target = 20.6 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates quarter-swing dynamics and radial/tangential laws to obtain 20.6 N (D).

items.stem: The diagram shows an accelerometer test pod of mass 0.9 kg moving at 9 m s⁻¹ through the bottom of a vertical circle of radius 1.3 m on a light kevlar tether in a centrifuge arm model. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What tension acts in a light kevlar tether?
items.workedSolution: At the bottom, upward resultant force T − mg = mv²/r. Centripetal force mv²/r = 0.9 × 9² / 1.3 = 56.1 N, so T = 56.1 + 0.9 × 9.81 = 64.9 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies T = m(v²/r + g) at the bottom of the circle to obtain 64.9 N (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts weight mg instead of adding mg, confusing the bottom of a vertical circle with the top.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Equates tension directly to centripetal force mv²/r and forgets the downward weight mg.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Sets tension equal to static weight mg, ignoring centripetal acceleration.

items.stem: The three-stage diagram shows a bridge-jump test sandbag of mass 9 kg dropped from rest at the support of an elastic shock cord (natural length 2 m), reaching A taut and extending a further 0.45 m over 0.22 s to rest at lowest point B. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the spring constant of an elastic shock cord?
items.workedSolution: Total vertical drop from release S to lowest point B is L + x = 2 + 0.45 = 2.45 m. By energy conservation mg(L + x) = ½kx², giving k = 2mg(L + x)/x² = 2.13 × 10³ N m⁻¹ and peak tension T_B = kx = 960 N. Target = 2.13 × 10³ N m⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses full vertical drop (2 + 0.45) m in mg(L + x) = ½kx² to obtain 2.13 × 10³ N m⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, an electric quarry haulage rig of mass 1300 kg accelerates horizontally so a suspended brass bob hangs at 22° to the vertical, later climbs a 10° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 75 m (static friction coefficient 0.75), and coasts from 15 m s⁻¹ against a 530 N resistive force toward the weighbridge. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the maximum speed on the flat semicircular curve of radius 75 m without skidding?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 22° = ma and T cos 22° = mg => a = g tan 22° = 3.96 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.75 × 9.81 × 75) = 23.5 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1300)(15)² / 530 = 276 m. Target = 23.5 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 23.5 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the static friction coefficient μ_s in μ_s mg = mv²/R.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides by μ_s instead of multiplying by μ_s.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes v² = μ_s g R without taking the square root.

items.stem: Along an anodized calibration incline inclined at 40° to the horizontal, an avionics shock canister (mass 4.5 kg) slides 5 m from rest and arrives at the base travelling at 4.37 m s⁻¹. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. How much mechanical energy is dissipated against friction during the descent?
items.workedSolution: Gravitational potential energy lost ΔE_p = mgL sin 40° = 142 J. Final kinetic energy E_k = ½(4.5)(4.37)² = 43.0 J. Frictional energy loss W_f = ΔE_p − E_k = 98.8 J. Since W_f = μ(mg cos 40°)L, μ = 0.585. Target = 98.8 J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔE_p − E_k and normal reaction mg cos 40° accurately to obtain 98.8 J (C).

items.stem: Of weight 920 N, a steel cable drum cradle descends a warehouse ramp at steady speed over a slope distance of 33 m through a vertical height change of 10.6 m. How much gravitational potential energy is lost over the full length of the slope?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed ΔE_k = 0. Potential energy lost = W h = 920 × 10.6 = 9.75 × 10³ J. Parallel equilibrium gives F_res = W sin θ = W h / L = 296 N. Target = 9.75 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ = 10.6/33 and zero net force to obtain 9.75 × 10³ J (A).

items.stem: A quarry stone skip (weight 1100 N) slides at constant speed 6.5 m s⁻¹ down a planar service incline, which is 12 m long and drops 5.4 m vertically. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 1100 × (5.4/12) = 495 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 3.22 × 10³ W. Target = 495 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 495 N (B).

items.stem: A tracer polymer pellet leaves a ground discharge tube at 21 m s⁻¹ inclined at 55° above the horizontal over a horizontal test paddock. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What maximum vertical height above a horizontal test paddock does it reach?
items.workedSolution: At the apex v_y = 0 while horizontal velocity remains constant at v_apex = u cos 55° = 12.0 m s⁻¹. Maximum height h_max = (u sin 55°)² / (2g) = 15.1 m. Target = 15.1 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_y = 0 and constant v_x = u cos 55° at apex to obtain 15.1 m (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Converts all initial kinetic energy into gravitational potential energy, forgetting non-zero horizontal speed u cos θ at the apex.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses horizontal component u cos θ instead of vertical component u sin θ in h = u_y² / (2g).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of two in the denominator of h_max = u_y² / (2g).

items.stem: Travelling at 9 m s⁻¹ to the right along a precision gas-bearing trough, rider X (1.6 kg) strikes stationary rider Y (1.2 kg), sending rider Y rightward at 6.12 m s⁻¹. What is the speed of rider X immediately after the collision?
items.workedSolution: Momentum conservation: (1.6)(9) = (1.6)v_X + (1.2)(6.12), giving v_X = 4.41 m s⁻¹. K_i = 64.8 J and K_f = 38.0 J, so ΔK_lost = K_i − K_f = 26.8 J. Target = 4.41 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves linear momentum and evaluates kinetic energy budget to obtain 4.41 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: Along a frictionless optical-bench track, carriage X of mass 2.5 kg travelling right at 8 m s⁻¹ meets carriage Y of mass 4.2 kg travelling left at 5 m s⁻¹ (not drawn). After impact carriage Y rebounds right at 3.5 m s⁻¹. What is the post-collision velocity of carriage X?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward as positive: p_before = (2.5)(8) + (4.2)(−5) = -1.00 kg m s⁻¹. From p_before = (2.5)v_X + (4.2)(3.5), v_X = -6.28 m s⁻¹, which is 6.28 m s⁻¹ to the left.

markScheme.criterion: Uses signed head-on momentum p_before = -1.00 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 6.28 m s⁻¹ to the left (A).

items.stem: Released from rest from a horizontal string position of length 1.5 m in a Charpy-style swing rig, a cast-iron hammer bob (1 kg) strikes and sticks to stationary a deformable putty mass (1.2 kg) at the bottom of its arc. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. How much mechanical energy is dissipated during the sticking collision?
items.workedSolution: Pre-impact speed u = √(2gL) = 5.42 m s⁻¹. Tangential momentum conservation gives v = mu / (m + M) = 2.47 m s⁻¹. Post-impact rise h = v² / (2g) = (m/(m+M))² L = 0.310 m; energy lost = mgL − (m+M)gh = 8.03 J. Target = 8.03 J.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves energy during swings and momentum during impact to obtain 8.03 J (C).

items.stem: Whirled on a high-tensile cord of length 1.3 m in a vertical rotation stand, a telemetry capsule (1.7 kg) has speed 9.5 m s⁻¹ at the bottom of its vertical circular path. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. Determine the tension in a high-tensile cord at this instant.
items.workedSolution: At the bottom, upward resultant force T − mg = mv²/r. Centripetal force mv²/r = 1.7 × 9.5² / 1.3 = 118 N, so T = 118 + 1.7 × 9.8 = 135 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies T = m(v²/r + g) at the bottom of the circle to obtain 135 N (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts weight mg instead of adding mg, confusing the bottom of a vertical circle with the top.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Equates tension directly to centripetal force mv²/r and forgets the downward weight mg.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Sets tension equal to static weight mg, ignoring centripetal acceleration.

items.stem: Whirled in a vertical circle of radius 2 m on a light inextensible wire (breaking tension 95 N) in a vertical circular test rig, a steel sensor sphere has mass 2.2 kg. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. Determine the greatest safe speed at the lowest point.
items.workedSolution: Tension is greatest at the bottom where T_max − mg = m v_max² / r. Thus v_max = √[((95/2.2) − 9.81) × 2] = 8.17 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves T_max − mg = mv²/r to obtain 8.17 m s⁻¹ (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds g instead of subtracting g when rearranging T_max − mg = mv²/r.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats vertical circular motion as horizontal, omitting weight mg at the lowest point.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes minimum top-of-loop critical speed √(gr) instead of maximum safe bottom speed.

items.stem: In a stage gridiron support, a stunt-rig counterweight (9 kg) falls from rest at the support through the 3.2 m slack length of an elastic arrest cable to point A and is brought momentarily to rest after stretching 1.2 m in a time of 0.3 s to B. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. Determine the time-averaged tension in an elastic arrest cable during this 0.3 s interval.
items.workedSolution: Speed when taut at A: v_A = √(2 × 9.81 × 3.2) = 7.92 m s⁻¹ downward. Taking upward positive, (F_mean − mg)Δt = 0 − (−mv_A), so F_mean = mv_A / 0.3 + 9(9.81) = 326 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = mv_A with v_A = √(2gL) to obtain 326 N (D).

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, an airport baggage tractor of mass 1800 kg accelerates horizontally so a cab-mounted pendulum bob hangs at 34° to the vertical, later climbs a 10° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 55 m (static friction coefficient 0.6), and coasts from 22 m s⁻¹ against a 620 N resistive force toward the concourse stop. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What is the horizontal acceleration during the initial straight-line phase when a cab-mounted pendulum bob deflects by 34°?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 34° = ma and T cos 34° = mg => a = g tan 34° = 6.61 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.6 × 9.8 × 55) = 18.0 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1800)(22)² / 620 = 703 m. Target = 6.61 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 6.61 m s⁻² (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses g sin θ as if on an inclined plane rather than resolving T sin θ = ma and T cos θ = mg to obtain g tan θ.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the ratio of horizontal to vertical components, evaluating g / tan θ instead of g tan θ.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies g by cos θ instead of tan θ.

items.stem: On a dry-dock slip plank (8.5 m long, angled at 34° to the horizontal), a shipyard keel block of mass 6.5 kg slides from rest and attains 5.31 m s⁻¹ at the base against constant kinetic friction. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. If the same object is instead released from rest halfway down a dry-dock slip plank, what speed does it reach at the bottom?
items.workedSolution: Energy dissipated W_f = mgL sin 34° − ½mv² = 211 J. Constant friction force F_f = W_f / 8.5 = 24.9 N. Released halfway down at unchanged acceleration a, v_half = v / √2 = 3.75 m s⁻¹. Target = 3.75 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Applies work-energy / constant-acceleration scaling on the incline to obtain 3.75 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: Descending a gravity-brake ramp of length 18 m and vertical drop 8.1 m at a steady speed of 2 m s⁻¹, a warehouse pallet box has weight 1400 N. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 1400 × (8.1/18) = 630 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 1.26 × 10³ W. Target = 630 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 630 N (B).

items.stem: Across a level driving range, a tee on flat ground projects a golf launch-monitor ball with initial speed 38 m s⁻¹ at 52° above the horizontal. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What horizontal range does it cover before landing on a level driving range?
items.workedSolution: u_y = 38 sin 52° = 29.9 m s⁻¹ and u_x = 38 cos 52° = 23.4 m s⁻¹. Flight time T = 2u_y / 9.8 = 6.11 s; horizontal range R = u_x T = 143 m. Target = 143 m.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves orthogonal components accurately to obtain 143 m (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies horizontal speed by ascent time u sin θ / g instead of full flight time 2u sin θ / g.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes cos θ for sin θ in the flight-time expression.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses the 45° maximum-range formula u²/g without the angle factor sin(2θ).

items.stem: On a frictionless optical-bench track, carriage X of mass 1.6 kg moves right at 10 m s⁻¹ and collides with stationary carriage Y of mass 1.2 kg. Immediately after impact, carriage Y moves right at 7.23 m s⁻¹. What is the speed of carriage X immediately after the collision?
items.workedSolution: Momentum conservation: (1.6)(10) = (1.6)v_X + (1.2)(7.23), giving v_X = 4.58 m s⁻¹. K_i = 80.0 J and K_f = 48.1 J, so ΔK_lost = K_i − K_f = 31.9 J. Target = 4.58 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves linear momentum and evaluates kinetic energy budget to obtain 4.58 m s⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: On a horizontal magnetic-bearing guideway, lighter shuttle X of mass 1.4 kg moving right at 15 m s⁻¹ strikes stationary heavier shuttle Y of mass 5 kg, causing shuttle Y to move right at 5.03 m s⁻¹ while shuttle X rebounds to the left. How much kinetic energy is dissipated in this rebound collision?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (1.4)(15) = (1.4)v_X + (5)(5.03) gives v_X = -2.96 m s⁻¹ (2.96 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(1.4)(2.96)² + ½(5)(5.03)² = 69.4 J. Energy lost = 158 J − K_f = 88.1 J. Target = 88.1 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 2.96 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 88.1 J (A).

items.stem: In a frictionless pivot stand, a calibration swing mass of mass 2.4 kg on a light string of length 2.3 m is released from rest with the string horizontal and coalesces at the lowest point with stationary a coupling receiver ball of mass 6 kg. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What maximum vertical height above the lowest point do the joined bodies reach?
items.workedSolution: Pre-impact speed u = √(2gL) = 6.71 m s⁻¹. Tangential momentum conservation gives v = mu / (m + M) = 1.92 m s⁻¹. Post-impact rise h = v² / (2g) = (m/(m+M))² L = 0.188 m; energy lost = mgL − (m+M)gh = 38.6 J. Target = 0.188 m.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves energy during swings and momentum during impact to obtain 0.188 m (A).

items.stem: In a laboratory swing frame, a brass impact sphere of mass 0.9 kg hangs on a 1.6 m string, is released from rest with the string horizontal, and collides inelastically at the bottom with stationary a wax capture block of mass 1.62 kg. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the tension in the string immediately before a brass impact sphere strikes a wax capture block?
items.workedSolution: Just before collision u² = 2gL => u = 5.60 m s⁻¹. Radial Newton second law T − mg = mu²/L = 2mg gives T = 3mg = 26.5 N. Momentum conservation gives v = mu/(m+M) = 2.00 m s⁻¹. Target = 26.5 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates quarter-swing dynamics and radial/tangential laws to obtain 26.5 N (C).

items.stem: In a vertical loop frame, a compact lead bob of mass 0.8 kg moves in a vertical circle of radius 1.4 m on a light steel cable, which snaps if tension exceeds 38 N. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the maximum speed a compact lead bob can have at the bottom without breaking a light steel cable?
items.workedSolution: Tension is greatest at the bottom where T_max − mg = m v_max² / r. Thus v_max = √[((38/0.8) − 9.81) × 1.4] = 7.26 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves T_max − mg = mv²/r to obtain 7.26 m s⁻¹ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Adds g instead of subtracting g when rearranging T_max − mg = mv²/r.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats vertical circular motion as horizontal, omitting weight mg at the lowest point.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes minimum top-of-loop critical speed √(gr) instead of maximum safe bottom speed.

items.stem: In a laboratory ceiling mount, a calibration steel ball of mass 5.5 kg is released from rest at the anchor of a Hookean rubber cord of unstretched length 3 m. The cord becomes taut at A and stretches obeying Hooke's law by a maximum extension of 0.45 m over 0.26 s before a calibration steel ball comes momentarily to rest at B. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the spring constant of a Hookean rubber cord?
items.workedSolution: Total vertical drop from release S to lowest point B is L + x = 3 + 0.45 = 3.45 m. By energy conservation mg(L + x) = ½kx², giving k = 2mg(L + x)/x² = 1.84 × 10³ N m⁻¹ and peak tension T_B = kx = 826 N. Target = 1.84 × 10³ N m⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses full vertical drop (3 + 0.45) m in mg(L + x) = ½kx² to obtain 1.84 × 10³ N m⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, an articulated test coach of mass 1800 kg accelerates horizontally so a roof-mounted plumb sphere hangs at 30° to the vertical, later climbs a 12° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 45 m (static friction coefficient 0.55), and coasts from 16 m s⁻¹ against a 380 N resistive force toward the timing gate. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What is the maximum speed on the flat semicircular curve of radius 45 m without skidding?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 30° = ma and T cos 30° = mg => a = g tan 30° = 5.66 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.55 × 9.81 × 45) = 15.6 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1800)(16)² / 380 = 606 m. Target = 15.6 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 15.6 m s⁻¹ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the static friction coefficient μ_s in μ_s mg = mv²/R.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Divides by μ_s instead of multiplying by μ_s.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes v² = μ_s g R without taking the square root.

items.stem: During a surface-wear test on a compacted snow test slope (11.5 m long, 44° above the horizontal), an alpine supply sled of mass 13.5 kg slides from rest to a bottom speed of 6.51 m s⁻¹. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². How much mechanical energy is dissipated against friction during the descent?
items.workedSolution: Gravitational potential energy lost ΔE_p = mgL sin 44° = 1.06 × 10³ J. Final kinetic energy E_k = ½(13.5)(6.51)² = 286 J. Frictional energy loss W_f = ΔE_p − E_k = 772 J. Since W_f = μ(mg cos 44°)L, μ = 0.705. Target = 772 J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔE_p − E_k and normal reaction mg cos 44° accurately to obtain 772 J (D).

items.stem: In translational equilibrium at constant speed, a freight container sled (weight 1000 N) travels 12 m down a dockyard unloading ramp, dropping 6.2 m vertically. How much gravitational potential energy is lost over the full length of the slope?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed ΔE_k = 0. Potential energy lost = W h = 1000 × 6.2 = 6.20 × 10³ J. Parallel equilibrium gives F_res = W sin θ = W h / L = 517 N. Target = 6.20 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ = 6.2/12 and zero net force to obtain 6.20 × 10³ J (C).

items.stem: While sliding down a refractory cooling chute (26 m long, 10.4 m vertical height) at constant speed 5.5 m s⁻¹, a foundry ingot sled of weight 1450 N converts lost potential energy into heat. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 1450 × (10.4/26) = 580 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 3.19 × 10³ W. Target = 580 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 580 N (D).

items.stem: Referring to the launch of a hail-impact test sphere from an angled gas gun at 36 m s⁻¹ and 33° above a horizontal test hall: Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². What maximum vertical height above a horizontal test hall does it reach?
items.workedSolution: At the apex v_y = 0 while horizontal velocity remains constant at v_apex = u cos 33° = 30.2 m s⁻¹. Maximum height h_max = (u sin 33°)² / (2g) = 19.6 m. Target = 19.6 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_y = 0 and constant v_x = u cos 33° at apex to obtain 19.6 m (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Converts all initial kinetic energy into gravitational potential energy, forgetting non-zero horizontal speed u cos θ at the apex.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses horizontal component u cos θ instead of vertical component u sin θ in h = u_y² / (2g).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of two in the denominator of h_max = u_y² / (2g).

items.stem: On a smooth glass collision groove, lighter trolley X of mass 1.2 kg moving right at 15 m s⁻¹ strikes stationary heavier trolley Y of mass 3.8 kg, causing trolley Y to move right at 5.6 m s⁻¹ while trolley X rebounds to the left. How much kinetic energy is dissipated in this rebound collision?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (1.2)(15) = (1.2)v_X + (3.8)(5.6) gives v_X = -2.73 m s⁻¹ (2.73 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(1.2)(2.73)² + ½(3.8)(5.6)² = 64.1 J. Energy lost = 135 J − K_f = 70.9 J. Target = 70.9 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 2.73 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 70.9 J (D).

items.stem: During a head-on collision test on a horizontal magnetic-bearing guideway, shuttle X (2.5 kg) moves right at 5 m s⁻¹ while shuttle Y (2.4 kg) moves left at 6 m s⁻¹ (arrow omitted), and shuttle Y exits right at 4 m s⁻¹. Find the velocity of shuttle X right after collision.
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward as positive: p_before = (2.5)(5) + (2.4)(−6) = -1.90 kg m s⁻¹. From p_before = (2.5)v_X + (2.4)(4), v_X = -4.60 m s⁻¹, which is 4.60 m s⁻¹ to the left.

markScheme.criterion: Uses signed head-on momentum p_before = -1.90 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 4.60 m s⁻¹ to the left (A).

items.stem: In a Charpy-style swing rig, a cast-iron hammer bob of mass 1.7 kg hangs on a 2.2 m string, is released from rest with the string horizontal, and collides inelastically at the bottom with stationary a deformable putty mass of mass 1.7 kg. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the tension in the string immediately before a cast-iron hammer bob strikes a deformable putty mass?
items.workedSolution: Just before collision u² = 2gL => u = 6.57 m s⁻¹. Radial Newton second law T − mg = mu²/L = 2mg gives T = 3mg = 50.0 N. Momentum conservation gives v = mu/(m+M) = 3.28 m s⁻¹. Target = 50.0 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates quarter-swing dynamics and radial/tangential laws to obtain 50.0 N (A).

items.stem: At the bottom of a vertical circle of radius 1.9 m in a vertical whirl apparatus, a brass pendulum mass of mass 1.3 kg travels at 9.5 m s⁻¹ while attached to a taut nylon cord. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.8 m s⁻². Calculate the tension in a taut nylon cord.
items.workedSolution: At the bottom, upward resultant force T − mg = mv²/r. Centripetal force mv²/r = 1.3 × 9.5² / 1.9 = 61.8 N, so T = 61.8 + 1.3 × 9.8 = 74.5 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies T = m(v²/r + g) at the bottom of the circle to obtain 74.5 N (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts weight mg instead of adding mg, confusing the bottom of a vertical circle with the top.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Equates tension directly to centripetal force mv²/r and forgets the downward weight mg.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Sets tension equal to static weight mg, ignoring centripetal acceleration.

items.stem: Attached to a braided dynamic lanyard of unstretched length 4 m in a fall-arrest gantry, a rescue arrest dummy of mass 2.5 kg falls from rest at the anchor, passes taut point A, and stretches the cord by 0.45 m in 0.34 s to rest at B. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the peak tension in a braided dynamic lanyard at the lowest point B?
items.workedSolution: Total vertical drop from release S to lowest point B is L + x = 4 + 0.45 = 4.45 m. By energy conservation mg(L + x) = ½kx², giving k = 2mg(L + x)/x² = 1.08 × 10³ N m⁻¹ and peak tension T_B = kx = 485 N. Target = 485 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses full vertical drop (4 + 0.45) m in mg(L + x) = ½kx² to obtain 485 N (C).

items.stem: During an impulse-arrest test in an overhead hoist beam, a crane overload test block of mass 14 kg drops freely 2.8 m to taut point A and extends an elastic snubber line by 1.4 m over 0.12 s until instantaneous rest at B. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². Calculate the mean upward cord force during deceleration.
items.workedSolution: Speed when taut at A: v_A = √(2 × 9.81 × 2.8) = 7.41 m s⁻¹ downward. Taking upward positive, (F_mean − mg)Δt = 0 − (−mv_A), so F_mean = mv_A / 0.12 + 14(9.81) = 1.00 × 10³ N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = mv_A with v_A = √(2gL) to obtain 1.00 × 10³ N (C).

items.stem: The diagram shows a marine slipway cradle of mass 8 kg starting from rest and descending 11 m down an inclined launchway angled at 24°, attaining 7.68 m s⁻¹ at the bottom. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the coefficient of dynamic friction μ_d between a marine slipway cradle and an inclined launchway?
items.workedSolution: Gravitational potential energy lost ΔE_p = mgL sin 24° = 351 J. Final kinetic energy E_k = ½(8)(7.68)² = 236 J. Frictional energy loss W_f = ΔE_p − E_k = 115 J. Since W_f = μ(mg cos 24°)L, μ = 0.146. Target = 0.146.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔE_p − E_k and normal reaction mg cos 24° accurately to obtain 0.146 (D).

items.stem: The diagram illustrates a battery transport case (9.5 kg) released from rest at the top of a textured service ramp of length 5 m and angle 30°, arriving at the bottom at 4.55 m s⁻¹. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the magnitude of the constant friction force opposing its motion?
items.workedSolution: Energy dissipated W_f = mgL sin 30° − ½mv² = 135 J. Constant friction force F_f = W_f / 5 = 26.9 N. Released halfway down at unchanged acceleration a, v_half = v / √2 = 3.22 m s⁻¹. Target = 26.9 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies work-energy / constant-acceleration scaling on the incline to obtain 26.9 N (A).

items.stem: The diagram shows an expedition supply sled of weight 1150 N moving at constant speed 4.5 m s⁻¹ down a crusty glacier slope of slope length 12 m and height 3.6 m. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 1150 × (3.6/12) = 345 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 1.55 × 10³ W. Target = 345 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 345 N (A).

items.stem: The diagram shows an acoustic ranging dart launched at 22 m s⁻¹ inclined at 60° to a flat proving ground. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.8 m s⁻². What horizontal range does it cover before landing on a flat proving ground?
items.workedSolution: u_y = 22 sin 60° = 19.1 m s⁻¹ and u_x = 22 cos 60° = 11.0 m s⁻¹. Flight time T = 2u_y / 9.8 = 3.89 s; horizontal range R = u_x T = 42.8 m. Target = 42.8 m.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves orthogonal components accurately to obtain 42.8 m (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies horizontal speed by ascent time u sin θ / g instead of full flight time 2u sin θ / g.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes cos θ for sin θ in the flight-time expression.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses the 45° maximum-range formula u²/g without the angle factor sin(2θ).

items.stem: The diagram shows sled X of mass 2.8 kg moving right at 11 m s⁻¹ toward stationary sled Y of mass 2.8 kg on a polished ice test channel; after collision, sled Y travels right at 8.39 m s⁻¹. What is the speed of sled X immediately after the collision?
items.workedSolution: Momentum conservation: (2.8)(11) = (2.8)v_X + (2.8)(8.39), giving v_X = 2.61 m s⁻¹. K_i = 169 J and K_f = 108 J, so ΔK_lost = K_i − K_f = 61.3 J. Target = 2.61 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves linear momentum and evaluates kinetic energy budget to obtain 2.61 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: The diagram shows module X of mass 1.8 kg approaching stationary module Y of mass 6.5 kg at 8 m s⁻¹ on a level docking-simulator rail. After impact, module Y moves right at 2.65 m s⁻¹. How much kinetic energy is dissipated in this rebound collision?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (1.8)(8) = (1.8)v_X + (6.5)(2.65) gives v_X = -1.57 m s⁻¹ (1.57 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(1.8)(1.57)² + ½(6.5)(2.65)² = 25.0 J. Energy lost = 57.6 J − K_f = 32.6 J. Target = 32.6 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 1.57 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 32.6 J (A).

items.stem: The diagram shows an instrumented pendulum mass of mass 2.2 kg swinging from a horizontal 1.5 m string in a suspension test gantry to couple with stationary a magnetic-latch block of mass 1.76 kg at the lowest point. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.8 m s⁻². What maximum vertical height above the lowest point do the joined bodies reach?
items.workedSolution: Pre-impact speed u = √(2gL) = 5.42 m s⁻¹. Tangential momentum conservation gives v = mu / (m + M) = 3.01 m s⁻¹. Post-impact rise h = v² / (2g) = (m/(m+M))² L = 0.463 m; energy lost = mgL − (m+M)gh = 14.4 J. Target = 0.463 m.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves energy during swings and momentum during impact to obtain 0.463 m (C).

items.stem: The diagram shows a calibration ball of mass 0.7 kg moving at 8.5 m s⁻¹ through the bottom of a vertical circle of radius 0.5 m on a thin braided string in a lecture-hall whirl rig. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What tension acts in a thin braided string?
items.workedSolution: At the bottom, upward resultant force T − mg = mv²/r. Centripetal force mv²/r = 0.7 × 8.5² / 0.5 = 101 N, so T = 101 + 0.7 × 9.81 = 108 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies T = m(v²/r + g) at the bottom of the circle to obtain 108 N (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts weight mg instead of adding mg, confusing the bottom of a vertical circle with the top.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Equates tension directly to centripetal force mv²/r and forgets the downward weight mg.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Sets tension equal to static weight mg, ignoring centripetal acceleration.

items.stem: The diagram shows a gyroscope test mass (2 kg) at the bottom of a vertical circle of radius 1.6 m in a vertical-plane spinner; a light radial tether has a maximum safe tension of 87 N. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the maximum allowed speed at this point?
items.workedSolution: Tension is greatest at the bottom where T_max − mg = m v_max² / r. Thus v_max = √[((87/2) − 9.81) × 1.6] = 7.34 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves T_max − mg = mv²/r to obtain 7.34 m s⁻¹ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Adds g instead of subtracting g when rearranging T_max − mg = mv²/r.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats vertical circular motion as horizontal, omitting weight mg at the lowest point.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes minimum top-of-loop critical speed √(gr) instead of maximum safe bottom speed.

items.stem: The diagram illustrates a calibration steel ball of mass 12 kg released at the support of a Hookean rubber cord (natural length 2 m), becoming taut at A and decelerating to rest at B (extension 0.8 m) over 0.36 s. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.8 m s⁻². What mean force does a Hookean rubber cord exert between A and B?
items.workedSolution: Speed when taut at A: v_A = √(2 × 9.8 × 2) = 6.26 m s⁻¹ downward. Taking upward positive, (F_mean − mg)Δt = 0 − (−mv_A), so F_mean = mv_A / 0.36 + 12(9.8) = 326 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = mv_A with v_A = √(2gL) to obtain 326 N (C).

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, a proving-ground chassis mule of mass 1700 kg accelerates horizontally so a light-string plumb mass hangs at 30° to the vertical, later climbs a 14° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 45 m (static friction coefficient 0.55), and coasts from 17 m s⁻¹ against a 410 N resistive force toward the recovery marker. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the horizontal acceleration during the initial straight-line phase when a light-string plumb mass deflects by 30°?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 30° = ma and T cos 30° = mg => a = g tan 30° = 5.66 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.55 × 9.8 × 45) = 15.6 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1700)(17)² / 410 = 599 m. Target = 5.66 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 5.66 m s⁻² (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses g sin θ as if on an inclined plane rather than resolving T sin θ = ma and T cos θ = mg to obtain g tan θ.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the ratio of horizontal to vertical components, evaluating g / tan θ instead of g tan θ.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies g by cos θ instead of tan θ.

items.stem: On an angled loading board (5.5 m long, angled at 22° to the horizontal), a stage ballast crate of mass 13 kg slides from rest and attains 5.09 m s⁻¹ at the base against constant kinetic friction. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. If the same object is instead released from rest halfway down an angled loading board, what speed does it reach at the bottom?
items.workedSolution: Energy dissipated W_f = mgL sin 22° − ½mv² = 94.4 J. Constant friction force F_f = W_f / 5.5 = 17.2 N. Released halfway down at unchanged acceleration a, v_half = v / √2 = 3.60 m s⁻¹. Target = 3.60 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Applies work-energy / constant-acceleration scaling on the incline to obtain 3.60 m s⁻¹ (B).

options.label: C

items.stem: Of weight 400 N, a turbine casing pallet descends a powerhouse access incline at steady speed over a slope distance of 13 m through a vertical height change of 4.2 m. How much gravitational potential energy is lost over the full length of the slope?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed ΔE_k = 0. Potential energy lost = W h = 400 × 4.2 = 1.68 × 10³ J. Parallel equilibrium gives F_res = W sin θ = W h / L = 129 N. Target = 1.68 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ = 4.2/13 and zero net force to obtain 1.68 × 10³ J (A).

items.stem: Fired from a floor-mounted spring cannon at 32 m s⁻¹ and 56° above the horizontal, a lecture-hall steel ball lands back on a level demonstration track. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What is the total time of flight before returning to a level demonstration track?
items.workedSolution: u_y = 32 sin 56° = 26.5 m s⁻¹ and u_x = 32 cos 56° = 17.9 m s⁻¹. Flight time T = 2u_y / 9.81 = 5.41 s; horizontal range R = u_x T = 96.8 m. Target = 5.41 s.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves orthogonal components accurately to obtain 5.41 s (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes time to reach the apex u sin θ / g rather than full time of flight.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Swaps sin θ and cos θ when resolving vertical launch speed.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses total speed u instead of vertical component u sin θ.

items.stem: An irrigation water packet leaves a ground-level nozzle at 42 m s⁻¹ inclined at 51° above the horizontal over horizontal farmland. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What maximum vertical height above horizontal farmland does it reach?
items.workedSolution: At the apex v_y = 0 while horizontal velocity remains constant at v_apex = u cos 51° = 26.4 m s⁻¹. Maximum height h_max = (u sin 51°)² / (2g) = 54.3 m. Target = 54.3 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_y = 0 and constant v_x = u cos 51° at apex to obtain 54.3 m (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Converts all initial kinetic energy into gravitational potential energy, forgetting non-zero horizontal speed u cos θ at the apex.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses horizontal component u cos θ instead of vertical component u sin θ in h = u_y² / (2g).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of two in the denominator of h_max = u_y² / (2g).

items.stem: Moving rightward at 13 m s⁻¹ on a smooth marshalling test track, wagon X (1.4 kg) collides head-on with stationary wagon Y (3.9 kg); immediately afterward wagon Y travels right at 5.44 m s⁻¹ and wagon X rebounds backward. What is the total kinetic energy of the two bodies immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (1.4)(13) = (1.4)v_X + (3.9)(5.44) gives v_X = -2.15 m s⁻¹ (2.15 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(1.4)(2.15)² + ½(3.9)(5.44)² = 61.0 J. Energy lost = 118 J − K_f = 57.3 J. Target = 61.0 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 2.15 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 61.0 J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts the kinetic energy of rebounding X from Y as if kinetic energy were a signed vector.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Includes only the kinetic energy of Y and forgets the kinetic energy of rebounding X.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Assumes the collision is perfectly elastic and equates K_f to K_i.

items.stem: Along a horizontal frictionless air track, glider X of mass 4 kg travelling right at 13 m s⁻¹ meets glider Y of mass 3.6 kg travelling left at 4 m s⁻¹ (not drawn). After impact glider Y rebounds right at 5 m s⁻¹. What is the post-collision velocity of glider X?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward as positive: p_before = (4)(13) + (3.6)(−4) = 37.6 kg m s⁻¹. From p_before = (4)v_X + (3.6)(5), v_X = 4.90 m s⁻¹, which is 4.90 m s⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: Uses signed head-on momentum p_before = 37.6 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 4.90 m s⁻¹ to the right (C).

items.stem: Held with its 2 m light string horizontal in a ballistic pendulum rig, a steel pendulum bob (2.3 kg) swings down from rest and sticks to stationary a lump of modelling clay (5.06 kg) at the lowest point. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What is the speed of the coupled bodies immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Just before collision u² = 2gL => u = 6.26 m s⁻¹. Radial Newton second law T − mg = mu²/L = 2mg gives T = 3mg = 67.7 N. Momentum conservation gives v = mu/(m+M) = 1.96 m s⁻¹. Target = 1.96 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates quarter-swing dynamics and radial/tangential laws to obtain 1.96 m s⁻¹ (C).
