items.stem: Whirled on a taut braided wire of length 1.6 m in a dynamic tension rig, a forged test weight (1.1 kg) has speed 7 m s⁻¹ at the bottom of its vertical circular path. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. Determine the tension in a taut braided wire at this instant.
items.workedSolution: At the bottom, upward resultant force T − mg = mv²/r. Centripetal force mv²/r = 1.1 × 7² / 1.6 = 33.7 N, so T = 33.7 + 1.1 × 9.81 = 44.5 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies T = m(v²/r + g) at the bottom of the circle to obtain 44.5 N (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts weight mg instead of adding mg, confusing the bottom of a vertical circle with the top.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Equates tension directly to centripetal force mv²/r and forgets the downward weight mg.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Sets tension equal to static weight mg, ignoring centripetal acceleration.

items.stem: Released from rest at the support in a vertical test bay, an aerospace drop canister (1.5 kg) falls freely through the 2.2 m natural length of an elastic recovery cord to point A and then extends the Hookean cord by 0.55 m during 0.2 s to instantaneous rest at B. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What is the peak tension in an elastic recovery cord at the lowest point B?
items.workedSolution: Total vertical drop from release S to lowest point B is L + x = 2.2 + 0.55 = 2.75 m. By energy conservation mg(L + x) = ½kx², giving k = 2mg(L + x)/x² = 267 N m⁻¹ and peak tension T_B = kx = 147 N. Target = 147 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses full vertical drop (2.2 + 0.55) m in mg(L + x) = ½kx² to obtain 147 N (A).

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, a mine-tunnel shuttle vehicle of mass 1600 kg accelerates horizontally so a ceiling pendulum sensor hangs at 34° to the vertical, later climbs a 8° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 80 m (static friction coefficient 0.8), and coasts from 18 m s⁻¹ against a 350 N resistive force toward the shaft station. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What is the horizontal acceleration during the initial straight-line phase when a ceiling pendulum sensor deflects by 34°?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 34° = ma and T cos 34° = mg => a = g tan 34° = 6.62 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.8 × 9.81 × 80) = 25.1 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1600)(18)² / 350 = 741 m. Target = 6.62 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 6.62 m s⁻² (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses g sin θ as if on an inclined plane rather than resolving T sin θ = ma and T cos θ = mg to obtain g tan θ.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the ratio of horizontal to vertical components, evaluating g / tan θ instead of g tan θ.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies g by cos θ instead of tan θ.

items.stem: Released from rest at the top of a straight steel loading chute of length 10 m inclined at 32° to the horizontal, an instrumented cargo crate of mass 6.5 kg reaches the bottom with speed 6.22 m s⁻¹. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the coefficient of dynamic friction μ_d between an instrumented cargo crate and a straight steel loading chute?
items.workedSolution: Gravitational potential energy lost ΔE_p = mgL sin 32° = 338 J. Final kinetic energy E_k = ½(6.5)(6.22)² = 126 J. Frictional energy loss W_f = ΔE_p − E_k = 212 J. Since W_f = μ(mg cos 32°)L, μ = 0.392. Target = 0.392.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔE_p − E_k and normal reaction mg cos 32° accurately to obtain 0.392 (D).

items.stem: Sliding at constant velocity down a straight haulage incline of slope length 30 m and vertical drop 7.2 m, a mining equipment skid has weight 360 N. What is the magnitude of the resistive force opposing motion along the slope?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed ΔE_k = 0. Potential energy lost = W h = 360 × 7.2 = 2.59 × 10³ J. Parallel equilibrium gives F_res = W sin θ = W h / L = 86.4 N. Target = 86.4 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ = 7.2/30 and zero net force to obtain 86.4 N (B).

items.stem: Descending a rough warehouse ramp of length 32 m and vertical drop 17.6 m at a steady speed of 2 m s⁻¹, a heavy logistics crate has weight 400 N. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 400 × (17.6/32) = 220 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 440 W. Target = 220 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 220 N (D).

items.stem: Projected from a calibrated ground launcher at 30 m s⁻¹ at an angle of 24° above a flat proving ground, an acoustic ranging dart follows a parabolic arc. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the speed of the projectile at the highest point of its trajectory?
items.workedSolution: At the apex v_y = 0 while horizontal velocity remains constant at v_apex = u cos 24° = 27.4 m s⁻¹. Maximum height h_max = (u sin 24°)² / (2g) = 7.60 m. Target = 27.4 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_y = 0 and constant v_x = u cos 24° at apex to obtain 27.4 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Assumes the projectile is momentarily stationary at its highest point, forgetting its constant horizontal velocity u cos θ.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses u sin θ instead of u cos θ for the speed at the apex.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Assumes speed remains equal to launch speed u throughout the flight.

items.stem: On a horizontal frictionless air track, glider X of mass 2.4 kg moves right at 9 m s⁻¹ and collides with stationary glider Y of mass 1.6 kg. Immediately after impact, glider Y moves right at 7.66 m s⁻¹. What is the speed of glider X immediately after the collision?
items.workedSolution: Momentum conservation: (2.4)(9) = (2.4)v_X + (1.6)(7.66), giving v_X = 3.89 m s⁻¹. K_i = 97.2 J and K_f = 65.1 J, so ΔK_lost = K_i − K_f = 32.1 J. Target = 3.89 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves linear momentum and evaluates kinetic energy budget to obtain 3.89 m s⁻¹ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Assumes both bodies stick together instead of using the measured post-collision speed of Y.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Adds m_Y v_Y instead of subtracting m_Y v_Y when solving momentum conservation.

options.label: D

items.stem: Along a polished ice test channel, sled X of mass 2 kg travelling right at 8 m s⁻¹ meets sled Y of mass 3 kg travelling left at 3 m s⁻¹ (not drawn). After impact sled Y rebounds right at 4 m s⁻¹. What is the post-collision velocity of sled X?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward as positive: p_before = (2)(8) + (3)(−3) = 7.00 kg m s⁻¹. From p_before = (2)v_X + (3)(4), v_X = -2.50 m s⁻¹, which is 2.50 m s⁻¹ to the left.

markScheme.criterion: Uses signed head-on momentum p_before = 7.00 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 2.50 m s⁻¹ to the left (D).

items.stem: In a ballistic pendulum rig, a steel pendulum bob of mass 2 kg on a light string of length 1.6 m is released from rest with the string horizontal and coalesces at the lowest point with stationary a lump of modelling clay of mass 2.4 kg. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What maximum vertical height above the lowest point do the joined bodies reach?
items.workedSolution: Pre-impact speed u = √(2gL) = 5.60 m s⁻¹. Tangential momentum conservation gives v = mu / (m + M) = 2.55 m s⁻¹. Post-impact rise h = v² / (2g) = (m/(m+M))² L = 0.331 m; energy lost = mgL − (m+M)gh = 17.1 J. Target = 0.331 m.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves energy during swings and momentum during impact to obtain 0.331 m (D).

items.stem: In a vertical circular test rig, a steel sensor sphere of mass 1.7 kg whirls in a vertical circle of radius 0.9 m on a light inextensible wire and passes through the lowest point at speed 4.5 m s⁻¹. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the tension in a light inextensible wire at the lowest point?
items.workedSolution: At the bottom, upward resultant force T − mg = mv²/r. Centripetal force mv²/r = 1.7 × 4.5² / 0.9 = 38.2 N, so T = 38.2 + 1.7 × 9.8 = 54.9 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies T = m(v²/r + g) at the bottom of the circle to obtain 54.9 N (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts weight mg instead of adding mg, confusing the bottom of a vertical circle with the top.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Equates tension directly to centripetal force mv²/r and forgets the downward weight mg.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Sets tension equal to static weight mg, ignoring centripetal acceleration.

items.stem: Whirled in a vertical circle of radius 0.6 m on a light suspension line (breaking tension 130 N) in a vertical swing circle, a polished alloy bob has mass 2.2 kg. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. Determine the greatest safe speed at the lowest point.
items.workedSolution: Tension is greatest at the bottom where T_max − mg = m v_max² / r. Thus v_max = √[((130/2.2) − 9.81) × 0.6] = 5.44 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves T_max − mg = mv²/r to obtain 5.44 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Adds g instead of subtracting g when rearranging T_max − mg = mv²/r.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Treats vertical circular motion as horizontal, omitting weight mg at the lowest point.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes minimum top-of-loop critical speed √(gr) instead of maximum safe bottom speed.

items.stem: Dropped from rest at the anchor in a cliff-sim drop frame, a mountaineering test mass of mass 11 kg falls freely 2.6 m until a dynamic climbing rope becomes taut at A, then stretches the cord by 0.8 m over 0.21 s to come momentarily to rest at B. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the mean upward force exerted by a dynamic climbing rope between A and B?
items.workedSolution: Speed when taut at A: v_A = √(2 × 9.81 × 2.6) = 7.14 m s⁻¹ downward. Taking upward positive, (F_mean − mg)Δt = 0 − (−mv_A), so F_mean = mv_A / 0.21 + 11(9.81) = 482 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = mv_A with v_A = √(2gL) to obtain 482 N (B).

items.stem: Launched from a floor-mounted spring cannon across a level demonstration track, a lecture-hall steel ball has an initial speed of 39 m s⁻¹ at 37° above the horizontal. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) v_apex = 39 × cos 37°. Answer: 31.1 m s⁻¹. (b) u_y = 39 × sin 37° = 23.5 m s⁻¹. h_max = u_y² / (2 × 9.81). Answer: 28.1 m. (c) T = 2u_y / 9.81 = 4.79 s. R = 31.1 × T. Answer: 149 m.

markScheme.criterion: Recognizes v_y = 0 at apex so v_apex = u cos θ.

items.stem: On a precision gas-bearing trough, rider X of mass 4 kg moves to the right at 11 m s⁻¹ and collides head-on with rider Y of mass 4.2 kg moving to the left at 3.5 m s⁻¹ (arrow on Y not shown). Immediately after impact, rider Y moves to the right at 4.5 m s⁻¹. Take motion to the right as positive.
items.workedSolution: (a) p_before = 4 × 11 + 4.2 × (−3.5) = 29.3 kg m s⁻¹. Answer: 29.3 kg m s⁻¹ to the right. (b) v_X = (29.3 − 4.2 × 4.5) / 4 = 2.60 m s⁻¹. Answer: 2.60 m s⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates m_X u_X − m_Y |u_Y| with correct signs.
Obtains 29.3 kg m s⁻¹ to the right.
Solves p_before = m_X v_X + m_Y v_Y for v_X.
Obtains 2.60 m s⁻¹ to the right.

items.stem: During proving-ground tests, a harbour container carrier of mass 1800 kg accelerates along a level straight so a suspended mass indicator deflects by 34° from the vertical, climbs a straight 14° incline at constant speed, negotiates a flat semicircular curve of radius 95 m (coefficient of static friction 0.7), and finally coasts along the semicircle from 18 m s⁻¹ against a constant 470 N resistance toward the berth checkpoint. items.stem: Launched from a spring-loaded catapult across a level arena floor, a robotics arena sphere has an initial speed of 42 m s⁻¹ at 28° above the horizontal. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance.
items.workedSolution: (a) v_apex = 42 × cos 28°. Answer: 37.1 m s⁻¹. (b) u_y = 42 × sin 28° = 19.7 m s⁻¹. h_max = u_y² / (2 × 9.8). Answer: 19.8 m. (c) T = 2u_y / 9.8 = 4.02 s. R = 37.1 × T. Answer: 149 m.

markScheme.criterion: Recognizes v_y = 0 at apex so v_apex = u cos θ.

items.stem: On a level low-friction dynamics rail, cart X of mass 3 kg moves to the right at 9 m s⁻¹ and collides head-on with cart Y of mass 1.2 kg moving to the left at 5.5 m s⁻¹ (arrow on Y not shown). Immediately after impact, cart Y moves to the right at 1.5 m s⁻¹. Take motion to the right as positive.
items.workedSolution: (a) p_before = 3 × 9 + 1.2 × (−5.5) = 20.4 kg m s⁻¹. Answer: 20.4 kg m s⁻¹ to the right. (b) v_X = (20.4 − 1.2 × 1.5) / 3 = 6.20 m s⁻¹. Answer: 6.20 m s⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates m_X u_X − m_Y |u_Y| with correct signs.
Obtains 20.4 kg m s⁻¹ to the right.
Solves p_before = m_X v_X + m_Y v_Y for v_X.
Obtains 6.20 m s⁻¹ to the right.

items.stem: Released from rest at the anchor of an elastic shock cord (natural length 4 m) in a high-platform test rig, a bridge-jump test sandbag of mass 7 kg falls freely to point A where the cord becomes taut, then stretches the cord by 1.1 m over 0.27 s before reaching instantaneous rest at B. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.8 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) v_A = √(2 × 9.8 × 4). Answer: 8.85 m s⁻¹. (b) Mean resultant upward force = (7 × 8.85) / 0.27 = 230 N. F_mean = 230 + 7 × 9.8. Answer: 298 N. (c) T_B = 2 × 7 × 9.8 × (4 + 1.1) / 1.1. Answer: 636 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = m v_A, including weight mg.
Uses mg(L + x) = ½kx² and T_B = kx.

items.stem: Released from rest at the anchor of an elastic shock cord (natural length 2.6 m) in a high-platform test rig, a bridge-jump test sandbag of mass 10 kg falls freely to point A where the cord becomes taut, then stretches the cord by 0.6 m over 0.33 s before reaching instantaneous rest at B. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = m v_A, including weight mg.
Uses mg(L + x) = ½kx² and T_B = kx.

items.stem: Along a precision gas-bearing trough, rider X of mass 1.4 kg moves to the right at 15 m s⁻¹ and strikes stationary rider Y of mass 3.6 kg. Immediately after the collision, rider Y moves to the right at 6.73 m s⁻¹. Take rightward as positive.

items.stem: Launched from a spring-loaded catapult across a level arena floor, a robotics arena sphere has an initial speed of 21 m s⁻¹ at 24° above the horizontal. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.8 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) v_apex = 21 × cos 24°. Answer: 19.2 m s⁻¹. (b) u_y = 21 × sin 24° = 8.54 m s⁻¹. h_max = u_y² / (2 × 9.8). Answer: 3.72 m. (c) T = 2u_y / 9.8 = 1.74 s. R = 19.2 × T. Answer: 33.4 m.

markScheme.criterion: Recognizes v_y = 0 at apex so v_apex = u cos θ.

items.stem: On a level low-friction dynamics rail, cart X of mass 3.5 kg moves to the right at 12 m s⁻¹ and collides head-on with cart Y of mass 3.6 kg moving to the left at 3 m s⁻¹ (arrow on Y not shown). Immediately after impact, cart Y moves to the right at 2 m s⁻¹. Take motion to the right as positive.
items.workedSolution: (a) p_before = 3.5 × 12 + 3.6 × (−3) = 31.2 kg m s⁻¹. Answer: 31.2 kg m s⁻¹ to the right. (b) v_X = (31.2 − 3.6 × 2) / 3.5 = 6.86 m s⁻¹. Answer: 6.86 m s⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates m_X u_X − m_Y |u_Y| with correct signs.
Obtains 31.2 kg m s⁻¹ to the right.
Solves p_before = m_X v_X + m_Y v_Y for v_X.
Obtains 6.86 m s⁻¹ to the right.

items.stem: During proving-ground tests, a harbour container carrier of mass 1300 kg accelerates along a level straight so a suspended mass indicator deflects by 26° from the vertical, climbs a straight 14° incline at constant speed, negotiates a flat semicircular curve of radius 45 m (coefficient of static friction 0.5), and finally coasts along the semicircle from 20 m s⁻¹ against a constant 560 N resistance toward the berth checkpoint. markScheme.criterion: Uses T sin θ = ma and T cos θ = mg => a = g tan θ.
Applies μ_s mg = m v_max² / R.
Subtracts resistive work F_res(πR) from initial kinetic energy ½mu².

items.stem: Sliding at constant velocity down a straight haulage incline of slope length 25 m and vertical drop 7 m, a mining equipment skid has weight 1360 N. What is the magnitude of the resistive force opposing motion along the slope?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed ΔE_k = 0. Potential energy lost = W h = 1360 × 7 = 9.52 × 10³ J. Parallel equilibrium gives F_res = W sin θ = W h / L = 381 N. Target = 381 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ = 7/25 and zero net force to obtain 381 N (D).

items.stem: Descending a rough warehouse ramp of length 10 m and vertical drop 2.5 m at a steady speed of 2.5 m s⁻¹, a heavy logistics crate has weight 450 N. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 450 × (2.5/10) = 113 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 281 W. Target = 113 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 113 N (B).

items.stem: Projected from a calibrated ground launcher at 45 m s⁻¹ at an angle of 33° above a flat proving ground, an acoustic ranging dart follows a parabolic arc. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the speed of the projectile at the highest point of its trajectory?
items.workedSolution: At the apex v_y = 0 while horizontal velocity remains constant at v_apex = u cos 33° = 37.7 m s⁻¹. Maximum height h_max = (u sin 33°)² / (2g) = 30.6 m. Target = 37.7 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_y = 0 and constant v_x = u cos 33° at apex to obtain 37.7 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Assumes the projectile is momentarily stationary at its highest point, forgetting its constant horizontal velocity u cos θ.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses u sin θ instead of u cos θ for the speed at the apex.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Assumes speed remains equal to launch speed u throughout the flight.

items.stem: On a horizontal frictionless air track, glider X of mass 5.2 kg moves right at 12 m s⁻¹ and collides with stationary glider Y of mass 1.6 kg. Immediately after impact, glider Y moves right at 10.92 m s⁻¹. What is the speed of glider X immediately after the collision?
items.workedSolution: Momentum conservation: (5.2)(12) = (5.2)v_X + (1.6)(10.92), giving v_X = 8.64 m s⁻¹. K_i = 374 J and K_f = 289 J, so ΔK_lost = K_i − K_f = 84.9 J. Target = 8.64 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves linear momentum and evaluates kinetic energy budget to obtain 8.64 m s⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: On a smooth marshalling test track, wagon X of mass 3 kg moves right at 9 m s⁻¹ toward wagon Y of mass 4.2 kg approaching head-on to the left at 5.5 m s⁻¹ (initial arrow on Y omitted). Immediately after collision, wagon Y moves right at 4 m s⁻¹. What is the velocity of wagon X immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward as positive: p_before = (3)(9) + (4.2)(−5.5) = 3.90 kg m s⁻¹. From p_before = (3)v_X + (4.2)(4), v_X = -4.30 m s⁻¹, which is 4.30 m s⁻¹ to the left.

markScheme.criterion: Uses signed head-on momentum p_before = 3.90 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 4.30 m s⁻¹ to the left (B).

items.stem: In a vertical rotation stand, a telemetry capsule of mass 1.2 kg moves in a vertical circle of radius 0.8 m on a high-tensile cord, which snaps if tension exceeds 33 N. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the maximum speed a telemetry capsule can have at the bottom without breaking a high-tensile cord?
items.workedSolution: Tension is greatest at the bottom where T_max − mg = m v_max² / r. Thus v_max = √[((33/1.2) − 9.81) × 0.8] = 3.76 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves T_max − mg = mv²/r to obtain 3.76 m s⁻¹ (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Adds g instead of subtracting g when rearranging T_max − mg = mv²/r.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Treats vertical circular motion as horizontal, omitting weight mg at the lowest point.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes minimum top-of-loop critical speed √(gr) instead of maximum safe bottom speed.

items.stem: Dropped from rest at the anchor in a cliff-sim drop frame, a mountaineering test mass of mass 6 kg falls freely 4.6 m until a dynamic climbing rope becomes taut at A, then stretches the cord by 1.3 m over 0.3 s to come momentarily to rest at B. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the mean upward force exerted by a dynamic climbing rope between A and B?
items.workedSolution: Speed when taut at A: v_A = √(2 × 9.81 × 4.6) = 9.50 m s⁻¹ downward. Taking upward positive, (F_mean − mg)Δt = 0 − (−mv_A), so F_mean = mv_A / 0.3 + 6(9.81) = 249 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = mv_A with v_A = √(2gL) to obtain 249 N (D).

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, an instrumented test truck of mass 1800 kg accelerates horizontally so a ceiling-suspended plumb bob hangs at 18° to the vertical, later climbs a 14° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 60 m (static friction coefficient 0.7), and coasts from 15 m s⁻¹ against a 590 N resistive force toward the terminal bay. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the horizontal acceleration during the initial straight-line phase when a ceiling-suspended plumb bob deflects by 18°?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 18° = ma and T cos 18° = mg => a = g tan 18° = 3.18 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.7 × 9.8 × 60) = 20.3 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1800)(15)² / 590 = 343 m. Target = 3.18 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 3.18 m s⁻² (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses g sin θ as if on an inclined plane rather than resolving T sin θ = ma and T cos θ = mg to obtain g tan θ.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the ratio of horizontal to vertical components, evaluating g / tan θ instead of g tan θ.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies g by cos θ instead of tan θ.

items.stem: While sliding down a braking test slope (10 m long, 4 m vertical height) at constant speed 6.5 m s⁻¹, a steel ballast box of weight 200 N converts lost potential energy into heat. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 200 × (4/10) = 80.0 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 520 W. Target = 80.0 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 80.0 N (C).

items.stem: During a range trial on a level arena floor, a robotics arena sphere leaves a spring-loaded catapult at 42 m s⁻¹ and 64° above the horizontal. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the total time of flight before returning to a level arena floor?
items.workedSolution: u_y = 42 sin 64° = 37.7 m s⁻¹ and u_x = 42 cos 64° = 18.4 m s⁻¹. Flight time T = 2u_y / 9.8 = 7.70 s; horizontal range R = u_x T = 142 m. Target = 7.70 s.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves orthogonal components accurately to obtain 7.70 s (B).

options.label: C

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Takes an erroneous square root of 2u sin θ / g.

items.stem: During an inelastic collision trial on a horizontal magnetic-bearing guideway, shuttle X (mass 2.4 kg, initial rightward speed 7 m s⁻¹) hits stationary shuttle Y (mass 2.8 kg), which moves off to the right at 3.89 m s⁻¹. What is the speed of shuttle X immediately after the collision?
items.workedSolution: Momentum conservation: (2.4)(7) = (2.4)v_X + (2.8)(3.89), giving v_X = 2.46 m s⁻¹. K_i = 58.8 J and K_f = 28.5 J, so ΔK_lost = K_i − K_f = 30.3 J. Target = 2.46 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves linear momentum and evaluates kinetic energy budget to obtain 2.46 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: On a level docking-simulator rail, lighter module X of mass 1 kg moving right at 8 m s⁻¹ strikes stationary heavier module Y of mass 2.6 kg, causing module Y to move right at 4.24 m s⁻¹ while module X rebounds to the left. How much kinetic energy is dissipated in this rebound collision?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (1)(8) = (1)v_X + (2.6)(4.24) gives v_X = -3.02 m s⁻¹ (3.02 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(1)(3.02)² + ½(2.6)(4.24)² = 27.9 J. Energy lost = 32.0 J − K_f = 4.06 J. Target = 4.06 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 3.02 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 4.06 J (C).

items.stem: In a ceiling-mounted swing test, a chrome-steel bob of mass 0.3 kg hangs on a 2 m string, is released from rest with the string horizontal, and collides inelastically at the bottom with stationary a resin absorber block of mass 0.3 kg. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the tension in the string immediately before a chrome-steel bob strikes a resin absorber block?
items.workedSolution: Just before collision u² = 2gL => u = 6.26 m s⁻¹. Radial Newton second law T − mg = mu²/L = 2mg gives T = 3mg = 8.83 N. Momentum conservation gives v = mu/(m+M) = 3.13 m s⁻¹. Target = 8.83 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates quarter-swing dynamics and radial/tangential laws to obtain 8.83 N (D).

items.stem: Attached to a compliant elastomer rope of unstretched length 2.4 m in a vertical deceleration shaft, a payload shock capsule of mass 8 kg falls from rest at the anchor, passes taut point A, and stretches the cord by 1.05 m in 0.24 s to rest at B. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the peak tension in a compliant elastomer rope at the lowest point B?
items.workedSolution: Total vertical drop from release S to lowest point B is L + x = 2.4 + 1.05 = 3.45 m. By energy conservation mg(L + x) = ½kx², giving k = 2mg(L + x)/x² = 491 N m⁻¹ and peak tension T_B = kx = 515 N. Target = 515 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses full vertical drop (2.4 + 1.05) m in mg(L + x) = ½kx² to obtain 515 N (C).

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, a proving-ground chassis mule of mass 1800 kg accelerates horizontally so a light-string plumb mass hangs at 30° to the vertical, later climbs a 10° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 60 m (static friction coefficient 0.45), and coasts from 22 m s⁻¹ against a 350 N resistive force toward the recovery marker. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the maximum speed on the flat semicircular curve of radius 60 m without skidding?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 30° = ma and T cos 30° = mg => a = g tan 30° = 5.66 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.45 × 9.81 × 60) = 16.3 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1800)(22)² / 350 = 1.24 × 10³ m. Target = 16.3 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 16.3 m s⁻¹ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the static friction coefficient μ_s in μ_s mg = mv²/R.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Divides by μ_s instead of multiplying by μ_s.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes v² = μ_s g R without taking the square root.

items.stem: The diagram depicts a snowcat maintenance sled weighing 1040 N moving at constant speed down a planar ski run of length 20 m and vertical height 10.4 m. What is the magnitude of the resistive force opposing motion along the slope?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed ΔE_k = 0. Potential energy lost = W h = 1040 × 10.4 = 1.08 × 10⁴ J. Parallel equilibrium gives F_res = W sin θ = W h / L = 541 N. Target = 541 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ = 10.4/20 and zero net force to obtain 541 N (D).

items.stem: The diagram shows a shipyard launch block of weight 1350 N moving at constant speed 4.5 m s⁻¹ down a greased timber way of slope length 24 m and height 13.2 m. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 1350 × (13.2/24) = 743 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 3.34 × 10³ W. Target = 743 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 743 N (D).

items.stem: In a kinematics experiment over a level turf pitch, a sports-science test ball is launched at 45 m s⁻¹ and 62° above the horizontal. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the speed of the projectile at the highest point of its trajectory?
items.workedSolution: At the apex v_y = 0 while horizontal velocity remains constant at v_apex = u cos 62° = 21.1 m s⁻¹. Maximum height h_max = (u sin 62°)² / (2g) = 80.5 m. Target = 21.1 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_y = 0 and constant v_x = u cos 62° at apex to obtain 21.1 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Assumes the projectile is momentarily stationary at its highest point, forgetting its constant horizontal velocity u cos θ.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses u sin θ instead of u cos θ for the speed at the apex.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Assumes speed remains equal to launch speed u throughout the flight.

items.stem: The diagram shows cart X of mass 1.6 kg approaching stationary cart Y of mass 3.8 kg at 11 m s⁻¹ on a level low-friction dynamics rail. After impact, cart Y moves right at 5.86 m s⁻¹. How much kinetic energy is dissipated in this rebound collision?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (1.6)(11) = (1.6)v_X + (3.8)(5.86) gives v_X = -2.92 m s⁻¹ (2.92 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(1.6)(2.92)² + ½(3.8)(5.86)² = 72.1 J. Energy lost = 96.8 J − K_f = 24.7 J. Target = 24.7 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 2.92 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 24.7 J (B).

items.stem: On a horizontal frictionless air track, glider X of mass 3.5 kg moves right at 9 m s⁻¹ toward glider Y of mass 2.4 kg approaching head-on to the left at 3 m s⁻¹ (initial arrow on Y omitted). Immediately after collision, glider Y moves right at 4.5 m s⁻¹. What is the velocity of glider X immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward as positive: p_before = (3.5)(9) + (2.4)(−3) = 24.3 kg m s⁻¹. From p_before = (3.5)v_X + (2.4)(4.5), v_X = 3.86 m s⁻¹, which is 3.86 m s⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: Uses signed head-on momentum p_before = 24.3 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 3.86 m s⁻¹ to the right (B).

items.stem: The diagram shows a physics lecture bob of mass 1.3 kg released from a horizontal 0.8 m string in a light-string pendulum toward stationary a stationary putty sphere of mass 1.3 kg at the bottom. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the tension in the string immediately before a physics lecture bob strikes a stationary putty sphere?
items.workedSolution: Just before collision u² = 2gL => u = 3.96 m s⁻¹. Radial Newton second law T − mg = mu²/L = 2mg gives T = 3mg = 38.3 N. Momentum conservation gives v = mu/(m+M) = 1.98 m s⁻¹. Target = 38.3 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates quarter-swing dynamics and radial/tangential laws to obtain 38.3 N (D).

items.stem: The three-stage diagram shows a marine mooring weight of mass 6 kg dropped from rest at the support of a stretchable nylon hawser (natural length 3.2 m), reaching A taut and extending a further 0.85 m over 0.26 s to rest at lowest point B. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the spring constant of a stretchable nylon hawser?
items.workedSolution: Total vertical drop from release S to lowest point B is L + x = 3.2 + 0.85 = 4.05 m. By energy conservation mg(L + x) = ½kx², giving k = 2mg(L + x)/x² = 660 N m⁻¹ and peak tension T_B = kx = 561 N. Target = 660 N m⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses full vertical drop (3.2 + 0.85) m in mg(L + x) = ½kx² to obtain 660 N m⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: The diagram illustrates an instrumented drop sphere of mass 14 kg released at the support of an elastic bungee tether (natural length 3.2 m), becoming taut at A and decelerating to rest at B (extension 1.4 m) over 0.15 s. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What mean force does an elastic bungee tether exert between A and B?
items.workedSolution: Speed when taut at A: v_A = √(2 × 9.81 × 3.2) = 7.92 m s⁻¹ downward. Taking upward positive, (F_mean − mg)Δt = 0 − (−mv_A), so F_mean = mv_A / 0.15 + 14(9.81) = 877 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = mv_A with v_A = √(2gL) to obtain 877 N (C).

items.stem: A civil-engineering gabion (weight 300 N) slides at constant speed 4 m s⁻¹ down a planar test embankment, which is 20 m long and drops 12 m vertically. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 300 × (12/20) = 180 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 720 W. Target = 180 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 180 N (D).

items.stem: Fired from a ground discharge tube at 32 m s⁻¹ and 64° above the horizontal, a tracer polymer pellet lands back on a horizontal test paddock. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What is the total time of flight before returning to a horizontal test paddock?
items.workedSolution: u_y = 32 sin 64° = 28.8 m s⁻¹ and u_x = 32 cos 64° = 14.0 m s⁻¹. Flight time T = 2u_y / 9.8 = 5.87 s; horizontal range R = u_x T = 82.3 m. Target = 5.87 s.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves orthogonal components accurately to obtain 5.87 s (D).

options.label: C

items.stem: Travelling at 7 m s⁻¹ to the right along a level docking-simulator rail, module X (4 kg) strikes stationary module Y (1.6 kg), sending module Y rightward at 5.95 m s⁻¹. What is the speed of module X immediately after the collision?
items.workedSolution: Momentum conservation: (4)(7) = (4)v_X + (1.6)(5.95), giving v_X = 4.62 m s⁻¹. K_i = 98.0 J and K_f = 71.0 J, so ΔK_lost = K_i − K_f = 27.0 J. Target = 4.62 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves linear momentum and evaluates kinetic energy budget to obtain 4.62 m s⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: The diagram shows rider X of mass 0.6 kg approaching stationary rider Y of mass 2.2 kg at 14 m s⁻¹ on a precision gas-bearing trough. After impact, rider Y moves right at 5.67 m s⁻¹. How much kinetic energy is dissipated in this rebound collision?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (0.6)(14) = (0.6)v_X + (2.2)(5.67) gives v_X = -6.79 m s⁻¹ (6.79 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(0.6)(6.79)² + ½(2.2)(5.67)² = 49.2 J. Energy lost = 58.8 J − K_f = 9.60 J. Target = 9.60 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 6.79 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 9.60 J (D).

items.stem: The diagram shows a telemetry capsule (1.2 kg) at the bottom of a vertical circle of radius 1.6 m in a vertical rotation stand; a high-tensile cord has a maximum safe tension of 38 N. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the maximum allowed speed at this point?
items.workedSolution: Tension is greatest at the bottom where T_max − mg = m v_max² / r. Thus v_max = √[((38/1.2) − 9.81) × 1.6] = 5.91 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves T_max − mg = mv²/r to obtain 5.91 m s⁻¹ (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds g instead of subtracting g when rearranging T_max − mg = mv²/r.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats vertical circular motion as horizontal, omitting weight mg at the lowest point.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes minimum top-of-loop critical speed √(gr) instead of maximum safe bottom speed.

items.stem: In a vertical deceleration shaft, a payload shock capsule (3 kg) falls from rest at the support through the 2.6 m slack length of a compliant elastomer rope to point A and is brought momentarily to rest after stretching 1.1 m in a time of 0.15 s to B. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. Determine the time-averaged tension in a compliant elastomer rope during this 0.15 s interval.
items.workedSolution: Speed when taut at A: v_A = √(2 × 9.8 × 2.6) = 7.14 m s⁻¹ downward. Taking upward positive, (F_mean − mg)Δt = 0 − (−mv_A), so F_mean = mv_A / 0.15 + 3(9.8) = 172 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = mv_A with v_A = √(2gL) to obtain 172 N (D).

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, an articulated test coach of mass 1600 kg accelerates horizontally so a roof-mounted plumb sphere hangs at 34° to the vertical, later climbs a 10° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 85 m (static friction coefficient 0.5), and coasts from 22 m s⁻¹ against a 560 N resistive force toward the timing gate. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What is the horizontal acceleration during the initial straight-line phase when a roof-mounted plumb sphere deflects by 34°?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 34° = ma and T cos 34° = mg => a = g tan 34° = 6.61 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.5 × 9.8 × 85) = 20.4 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1600)(22)² / 560 = 691 m. Target = 6.61 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 6.61 m s⁻² (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses g sin θ as if on an inclined plane rather than resolving T sin θ = ma and T cos θ = mg to obtain g tan θ.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the ratio of horizontal to vertical components, evaluating g / tan θ instead of g tan θ.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies g by cos θ instead of tan θ.

items.stem: Sliding at constant velocity down a substation access slope of slope length 14 m and vertical drop 3.4 m, a transformer housing has weight 960 N. What is the magnitude of the resistive force opposing motion along the slope?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed ΔE_k = 0. Potential energy lost = W h = 960 × 3.4 = 3.26 × 10³ J. Parallel equilibrium gives F_res = W sin θ = W h / L = 233 N. Target = 233 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ = 3.4/14 and zero net force to obtain 233 N (B).

items.stem: Across a flat ash plain, a ground-level vent projects a volcanic ballistic clast with initial speed 30 m s⁻¹ at 56° above the horizontal. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What horizontal range does it cover before landing on a flat ash plain?
items.workedSolution: u_y = 30 sin 56° = 24.9 m s⁻¹ and u_x = 30 cos 56° = 16.8 m s⁻¹. Flight time T = 2u_y / 9.81 = 5.07 s; horizontal range R = u_x T = 85.1 m. Target = 85.1 m.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves orthogonal components accurately to obtain 85.1 m (B).

items.stem: Projected from a deck-level launcher at 39 m s⁻¹ at an angle of 28° above calm water at launch level, a rescue line-throwing bob follows a parabolic arc. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the speed of the projectile at the highest point of its trajectory?
items.workedSolution: At the apex v_y = 0 while horizontal velocity remains constant at v_apex = u cos 28° = 34.4 m s⁻¹. Maximum height h_max = (u sin 28°)² / (2g) = 17.1 m. Target = 34.4 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_y = 0 and constant v_x = u cos 28° at apex to obtain 34.4 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses u sin θ instead of u cos θ for the speed at the apex.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Assumes speed remains equal to launch speed u throughout the flight.

items.stem: On a smooth glass collision groove, lighter trolley X of mass 1.6 kg moving right at 14 m s⁻¹ strikes stationary heavier trolley Y of mass 5.4 kg, causing trolley Y to move right at 6.06 m s⁻¹ while trolley X rebounds to the left. How much kinetic energy is dissipated in this rebound collision?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (1.6)(14) = (1.6)v_X + (5.4)(6.06) gives v_X = -6.45 m s⁻¹ (6.45 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(1.6)(6.45)² + ½(5.4)(6.06)² = 132 J. Energy lost = 157 J − K_f = 24.3 J. Target = 24.3 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 6.45 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 24.3 J (B).

items.stem: On a polished ice test channel, sled X of mass 2 kg moves right at 10 m s⁻¹ toward sled Y of mass 3 kg approaching head-on to the left at 5.5 m s⁻¹ (initial arrow on Y omitted). Immediately after collision, sled Y moves right at 4 m s⁻¹. What is the velocity of sled X immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward as positive: p_before = (2)(10) + (3)(−5.5) = 3.50 kg m s⁻¹. From p_before = (2)v_X + (3)(4), v_X = -4.25 m s⁻¹, which is 4.25 m s⁻¹ to the left.

markScheme.criterion: Uses signed head-on momentum p_before = 3.50 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 4.25 m s⁻¹ to the left (D).

items.stem: In a Charpy-style swing rig, a cast-iron hammer bob of mass 2.5 kg hangs on a 2.2 m string, is released from rest with the string horizontal, and collides inelastically at the bottom with stationary a deformable putty mass of mass 4.5 kg. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the tension in the string immediately before a cast-iron hammer bob strikes a deformable putty mass?
items.workedSolution: Just before collision u² = 2gL => u = 6.57 m s⁻¹. Radial Newton second law T − mg = mu²/L = 2mg gives T = 3mg = 73.6 N. Momentum conservation gives v = mu/(m+M) = 2.35 m s⁻¹. Target = 73.6 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates quarter-swing dynamics and radial/tangential laws to obtain 73.6 N (D).

items.stem: In a high-platform test rig, a bridge-jump test sandbag of mass 11 kg is released from rest at the anchor of an elastic shock cord of unstretched length 3.2 m. The cord becomes taut at A and stretches obeying Hooke's law by a maximum extension of 0.75 m over 0.3 s before a bridge-jump test sandbag comes momentarily to rest at B. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the spring constant of an elastic shock cord?
items.workedSolution: Total vertical drop from release S to lowest point B is L + x = 3.2 + 0.75 = 3.95 m. By energy conservation mg(L + x) = ½kx², giving k = 2mg(L + x)/x² = 1.51 × 10³ N m⁻¹ and peak tension T_B = kx = 1.14 × 10³ N. Target = 1.51 × 10³ N m⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses full vertical drop (3.2 + 0.75) m in mg(L + x) = ½kx² to obtain 1.51 × 10³ N m⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, a rail-yard test locomotive of mass 1000 kg accelerates horizontally so a roof-hung indicator sphere hangs at 26° to the vertical, later climbs a 12° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 45 m (static friction coefficient 0.55), and coasts from 19 m s⁻¹ against a 620 N resistive force toward the buffer platform. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the horizontal acceleration during the initial straight-line phase when a roof-hung indicator sphere deflects by 26°?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 26° = ma and T cos 26° = mg => a = g tan 26° = 4.78 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.55 × 9.81 × 45) = 15.6 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1000)(19)² / 620 = 291 m. Target = 4.78 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 4.78 m s⁻² (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses g sin θ as if on an inclined plane rather than resolving T sin θ = ma and T cos θ = mg to obtain g tan θ.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the ratio of horizontal to vertical components, evaluating g / tan θ instead of g tan θ.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies g by cos θ instead of tan θ.

items.stem: In translational equilibrium at constant speed, a steel cable drum cradle (weight 440 N) travels 21 m down a warehouse ramp, dropping 7.6 m vertically. How much gravitational potential energy is lost over the full length of the slope?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed ΔE_k = 0. Potential energy lost = W h = 440 × 7.6 = 3.34 × 10³ J. Parallel equilibrium gives F_res = W sin θ = W h / L = 159 N. Target = 3.34 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ = 7.6/21 and zero net force to obtain 3.34 × 10³ J (C).

items.stem: While sliding down a planar service incline (24 m long, 6 m vertical height) at constant speed 4.5 m s⁻¹, a quarry stone skip of weight 400 N converts lost potential energy into heat. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 400 × (6/24) = 100 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 450 W. Target = 100 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 100 N (A).

items.stem: Referring to the launch of a tracer polymer pellet from a ground discharge tube at 42 m s⁻¹ and 33° above a horizontal test paddock: Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.8 m s⁻². What maximum vertical height above a horizontal test paddock does it reach?
items.workedSolution: At the apex v_y = 0 while horizontal velocity remains constant at v_apex = u cos 33° = 35.2 m s⁻¹. Maximum height h_max = (u sin 33°)² / (2g) = 26.7 m. Target = 26.7 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_y = 0 and constant v_x = u cos 33° at apex to obtain 26.7 m (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Converts all initial kinetic energy into gravitational potential energy, forgetting non-zero horizontal speed u cos θ at the apex.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses horizontal component u cos θ instead of vertical component u sin θ in h = u_y² / (2g).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of two in the denominator of h_max = u_y² / (2g).

items.stem: During an inelastic collision trial on a precision gas-bearing trough, rider X (mass 3.2 kg, initial rightward speed 6 m s⁻¹) hits stationary rider Y (mass 2.8 kg), which moves off to the right at 4.54 m s⁻¹. What is the speed of rider X immediately after the collision?
items.workedSolution: Momentum conservation: (3.2)(6) = (3.2)v_X + (2.8)(4.54), giving v_X = 2.03 m s⁻¹. K_i = 57.6 J and K_f = 35.4 J, so ΔK_lost = K_i − K_f = 22.2 J. Target = 2.03 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves linear momentum and evaluates kinetic energy budget to obtain 2.03 m s⁻¹ (A).

options.label: C

options.label: D

items.stem: During a head-on collision test on a smooth glass collision groove, trolley X (3 kg) moves right at 11 m s⁻¹ while trolley Y (4.2 kg) moves left at 3.5 m s⁻¹ (arrow omitted), and trolley Y exits right at 3 m s⁻¹. Find the velocity of trolley X right after collision.
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward as positive: p_before = (3)(11) + (4.2)(−3.5) = 18.3 kg m s⁻¹. From p_before = (3)v_X + (4.2)(3), v_X = 1.90 m s⁻¹, which is 1.90 m s⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: Uses signed head-on momentum p_before = 18.3 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 1.90 m s⁻¹ to the right (C).

options.label: B

options.label: D

items.stem: In a vertical whirl apparatus, a brass pendulum mass of mass 1.6 kg moves in a vertical circle of radius 1 m on a taut nylon cord, which snaps if tension exceeds 51 N. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the maximum speed a brass pendulum mass can have at the bottom without breaking a taut nylon cord?
items.workedSolution: Tension is greatest at the bottom where T_max − mg = m v_max² / r. Thus v_max = √[((51/1.6) − 9.81) × 1] = 4.70 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves T_max − mg = mv²/r to obtain 4.70 m s⁻¹ (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Adds g instead of subtracting g when rearranging T_max − mg = mv²/r.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Treats vertical circular motion as horizontal, omitting weight mg at the lowest point.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes minimum top-of-loop critical speed √(gr) instead of maximum safe bottom speed.

items.stem: During an impulse-arrest test in a stage gridiron support, a stunt-rig counterweight of mass 8 kg drops freely 2 m to taut point A and extends an elastic arrest cable by 0.5 m over 0.33 s until instantaneous rest at B. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². Calculate the mean upward cord force during deceleration.
items.workedSolution: Speed when taut at A: v_A = √(2 × 9.81 × 2) = 6.26 m s⁻¹ downward. Taking upward positive, (F_mean − mg)Δt = 0 − (−mv_A), so F_mean = mv_A / 0.33 + 8(9.81) = 230 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = mv_A with v_A = √(2gL) to obtain 230 N (A).

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, a heavy-duty rescue tender of mass 1500 kg accelerates horizontally so a suspended steel bob hangs at 22° to the vertical, later climbs a 10° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 60 m (static friction coefficient 0.55), and coasts from 20 m s⁻¹ against a 470 N resistive force toward the depot line. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the horizontal acceleration during the initial straight-line phase when a suspended steel bob deflects by 22°?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 22° = ma and T cos 22° = mg => a = g tan 22° = 3.96 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.55 × 9.8 × 60) = 18.0 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1500)(20)² / 470 = 638 m. Target = 3.96 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 3.96 m s⁻² (B).

options.label: C

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies g by cos θ instead of tan θ.

items.stem: The diagram shows a warehouse pallet box of weight 850 N moving at constant speed 6 m s⁻¹ down a gravity-brake ramp of slope length 22 m and height 13.2 m. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 850 × (13.2/22) = 510 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 3.06 × 10³ W. Target = 510 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 510 N (B).

items.stem: The diagram shows a golf launch-monitor ball launched at 26 m s⁻¹ inclined at 56° to a level driving range. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.8 m s⁻². What horizontal range does it cover before landing on a level driving range?
items.workedSolution: u_y = 26 sin 56° = 21.6 m s⁻¹ and u_x = 26 cos 56° = 14.5 m s⁻¹. Flight time T = 2u_y / 9.8 = 4.40 s; horizontal range R = u_x T = 64.0 m. Target = 64.0 m.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves orthogonal components accurately to obtain 64.0 m (C).

items.stem: The diagram shows carriage X of mass 5.2 kg moving right at 5 m s⁻¹ toward stationary carriage Y of mass 1.2 kg on a frictionless optical-bench track; after collision, carriage Y travels right at 6.07 m s⁻¹. What is the speed of carriage X immediately after the collision?
items.workedSolution: Momentum conservation: (5.2)(5) = (5.2)v_X + (1.2)(6.07), giving v_X = 3.60 m s⁻¹. K_i = 65.0 J and K_f = 55.8 J, so ΔK_lost = K_i − K_f = 9.21 J. Target = 3.60 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves linear momentum and evaluates kinetic energy budget to obtain 3.60 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: The diagram shows shuttle X of mass 2 kg approaching stationary shuttle Y of mass 6.4 kg at 9 m s⁻¹ on a horizontal magnetic-bearing guideway. After impact, shuttle Y moves right at 3.62 m s⁻¹. How much kinetic energy is dissipated in this rebound collision?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (2)(9) = (2)v_X + (6.4)(3.62) gives v_X = -2.58 m s⁻¹ (2.58 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(2)(2.58)² + ½(6.4)(3.62)² = 48.6 J. Energy lost = 81.0 J − K_f = 32.4 J. Target = 32.4 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 2.58 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 32.4 J (D).

items.stem: The diagram shows a brass impact sphere of mass 0.3 kg released from a horizontal 1.4 m string in a laboratory swing frame toward stationary a wax capture block of mass 0.3 kg at the bottom. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the tension in the string immediately before a brass impact sphere strikes a wax capture block?
items.workedSolution: Just before collision u² = 2gL => u = 5.24 m s⁻¹. Radial Newton second law T − mg = mu²/L = 2mg gives T = 3mg = 8.83 N. Momentum conservation gives v = mu/(m+M) = 2.62 m s⁻¹. Target = 8.83 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates quarter-swing dynamics and radial/tangential laws to obtain 8.83 N (C).

items.stem: The diagram shows a compact lead bob (1.4 kg) at the bottom of a vertical circle of radius 1.4 m in a vertical loop frame; a light steel cable has a maximum safe tension of 66 N. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the maximum allowed speed at this point?
items.workedSolution: Tension is greatest at the bottom where T_max − mg = m v_max² / r. Thus v_max = √[((66/1.4) − 9.81) × 1.4] = 7.23 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves T_max − mg = mv²/r to obtain 7.23 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: The three-stage diagram shows a calibration steel ball of mass 10.5 kg dropped from rest at the support of a Hookean rubber cord (natural length 1.8 m), reaching A taut and extending a further 0.55 m over 0.38 s to rest at lowest point B. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the spring constant of a Hookean rubber cord?
items.workedSolution: Total vertical drop from release S to lowest point B is L + x = 1.8 + 0.55 = 2.35 m. By energy conservation mg(L + x) = ½kx², giving k = 2mg(L + x)/x² = 1.60 × 10³ N m⁻¹ and peak tension T_B = kx = 879 N. Target = 1.60 × 10³ N m⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses full vertical drop (1.8 + 0.55) m in mg(L + x) = ½kx² to obtain 1.60 × 10³ N m⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: Of weight 280 N, a freight container sled descends a dockyard unloading ramp at steady speed over a slope distance of 11 m through a vertical height change of 6.2 m. How much gravitational potential energy is lost over the full length of the slope?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed ΔE_k = 0. Potential energy lost = W h = 280 × 6.2 = 1.74 × 10³ J. Parallel equilibrium gives F_res = W sin θ = W h / L = 158 N. Target = 1.74 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ = 6.2/11 and zero net force to obtain 1.74 × 10³ J (D).

items.stem: A foundry ingot sled (weight 900 N) slides at constant speed 5.5 m s⁻¹ down a refractory cooling chute, which is 16 m long and drops 7.2 m vertically. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 900 × (7.2/16) = 405 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 2.23 × 10³ W. Target = 405 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 405 N (B).

items.stem: A hail-impact test sphere leaves an angled gas gun at 15 m s⁻¹ inclined at 28° above the horizontal over a horizontal test hall. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What maximum vertical height above a horizontal test hall does it reach?
items.workedSolution: At the apex v_y = 0 while horizontal velocity remains constant at v_apex = u cos 28° = 13.2 m s⁻¹. Maximum height h_max = (u sin 28°)² / (2g) = 2.53 m. Target = 2.53 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_y = 0 and constant v_x = u cos 28° at apex to obtain 2.53 m (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Converts all initial kinetic energy into gravitational potential energy, forgetting non-zero horizontal speed u cos θ at the apex.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses horizontal component u cos θ instead of vertical component u sin θ in h = u_y² / (2g).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of two in the denominator of h_max = u_y² / (2g).

items.stem: Moving rightward at 9 m s⁻¹ on a level cleanroom linear rail, carrier X (2 kg) collides head-on with stationary carrier Y (6.8 kg); immediately afterward carrier Y travels right at 3.87 m s⁻¹ and carrier X rebounds backward. What is the total kinetic energy of the two bodies immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (2)(9) = (2)v_X + (6.8)(3.87) gives v_X = -4.16 m s⁻¹ (4.16 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(2)(4.16)² + ½(6.8)(3.87)² = 68.2 J. Energy lost = 81.0 J − K_f = 12.8 J. Target = 68.2 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 4.16 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 68.2 J (D).

items.stem: Along a polished ice test channel, sled X of mass 4 kg travelling right at 11 m s⁻¹ meets sled Y of mass 2.4 kg travelling left at 5 m s⁻¹ (not drawn). After impact sled Y rebounds right at 3 m s⁻¹. What is the post-collision velocity of sled X?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward as positive: p_before = (4)(11) + (2.4)(−5) = 32.0 kg m s⁻¹. From p_before = (4)v_X + (2.4)(3), v_X = 6.20 m s⁻¹, which is 6.20 m s⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: Uses signed head-on momentum p_before = 32.0 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 6.20 m s⁻¹ to the right (B).

items.stem: Held with its 1.4 m light string horizontal in a suspension test gantry, an instrumented pendulum mass (2.5 kg) swings down from rest and sticks to stationary a magnetic-latch block (5.5 kg) at the lowest point. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What is the speed of the coupled bodies immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Just before collision u² = 2gL => u = 5.24 m s⁻¹. Radial Newton second law T − mg = mu²/L = 2mg gives T = 3mg = 73.6 N. Momentum conservation gives v = mu/(m+M) = 1.64 m s⁻¹. Target = 1.64 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates quarter-swing dynamics and radial/tangential laws to obtain 1.64 m s⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: Released from rest at the support in a fall-arrest gantry, a rescue arrest dummy (8.5 kg) falls freely through the 1.8 m natural length of a braided dynamic lanyard to point A and then extends the Hookean cord by 1.35 m during 0.32 s to instantaneous rest at B. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What is the peak tension in a braided dynamic lanyard at the lowest point B?
items.workedSolution: Total vertical drop from release S to lowest point B is L + x = 1.8 + 1.35 = 3.15 m. By energy conservation mg(L + x) = ½kx², giving k = 2mg(L + x)/x² = 288 N m⁻¹ and peak tension T_B = kx = 389 N. Target = 389 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses full vertical drop (1.8 + 1.35) m in mg(L + x) = ½kx² to obtain 389 N (B).

items.stem: In an overhead hoist beam, a crane overload test block (12 kg) falls from rest at the support through the 2 m slack length of an elastic snubber line to point A and is brought momentarily to rest after stretching 1.2 m in a time of 0.21 s to B. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. Determine the time-averaged tension in an elastic snubber line during this 0.21 s interval.
items.workedSolution: Speed when taut at A: v_A = √(2 × 9.81 × 2) = 6.26 m s⁻¹ downward. Taking upward positive, (F_mean − mg)Δt = 0 − (−mv_A), so F_mean = mv_A / 0.21 + 12(9.81) = 476 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = mv_A with v_A = √(2gL) to obtain 476 N (C).

items.stem: Descending a crusty glacier slope of length 10 m and vertical drop 4 m at a steady speed of 3.5 m s⁻¹, an expedition supply sled has weight 1050 N. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 1050 × (4/10) = 420 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 1.47 × 10³ W. Target = 420 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 420 N (D).

items.stem: Across a flat proving ground, a calibrated ground launcher projects an acoustic ranging dart with initial speed 44 m s⁻¹ at 52° above the horizontal. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What horizontal range does it cover before landing on a flat proving ground?
items.workedSolution: u_y = 44 sin 52° = 34.7 m s⁻¹ and u_x = 44 cos 52° = 27.1 m s⁻¹. Flight time T = 2u_y / 9.8 = 7.08 s; horizontal range R = u_x T = 192 m. Target = 192 m.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves orthogonal components accurately to obtain 192 m (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies horizontal speed by ascent time u sin θ / g instead of full flight time 2u sin θ / g.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes cos θ for sin θ in the flight-time expression.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses the 45° maximum-range formula u²/g without the angle factor sin(2θ).

items.stem: On a polished ice test channel, sled X of mass 1.2 kg moves right at 5 m s⁻¹ and collides with stationary sled Y of mass 2 kg. Immediately after impact, sled Y moves right at 2.31 m s⁻¹. What is the speed of sled X immediately after the collision?
items.workedSolution: Momentum conservation: (1.2)(5) = (1.2)v_X + (2)(2.31), giving v_X = 1.15 m s⁻¹. K_i = 15.0 J and K_f = 6.13 J, so ΔK_lost = K_i − K_f = 8.87 J. Target = 1.15 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves linear momentum and evaluates kinetic energy budget to obtain 1.15 m s⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: On a level docking-simulator rail, lighter module X of mass 2 kg moving right at 8 m s⁻¹ strikes stationary heavier module Y of mass 6.8 kg, causing module Y to move right at 2.8 m s⁻¹ while module X rebounds to the left. How much kinetic energy is dissipated in this rebound collision?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (2)(8) = (2)v_X + (6.8)(2.8) gives v_X = -1.52 m s⁻¹ (1.52 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(2)(1.52)² + ½(6.8)(2.8)² = 29.0 J. Energy lost = 64.0 J − K_f = 35.0 J. Target = 35.0 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 1.52 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 35.0 J (B).

items.stem: In a vertical-plane spinner, a gyroscope test mass of mass 0.6 kg moves in a vertical circle of radius 2.2 m on a light radial tether, which snaps if tension exceeds 24 N. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the maximum speed a gyroscope test mass can have at the bottom without breaking a light radial tether?
items.workedSolution: Tension is greatest at the bottom where T_max − mg = m v_max² / r. Thus v_max = √[((24/0.6) − 9.81) × 2.2] = 8.15 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves T_max − mg = mv²/r to obtain 8.15 m s⁻¹ (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds g instead of subtracting g when rearranging T_max − mg = mv²/r.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats vertical circular motion as horizontal, omitting weight mg at the lowest point.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes minimum top-of-loop critical speed √(gr) instead of maximum safe bottom speed.

items.stem: Dropped from rest at the anchor in a laboratory ceiling mount, a calibration steel ball of mass 10 kg falls freely 3.8 m until a Hookean rubber cord becomes taut at A, then stretches the cord by 0.6 m over 0.12 s to come momentarily to rest at B. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the mean upward force exerted by a Hookean rubber cord between A and B?
items.workedSolution: Speed when taut at A: v_A = √(2 × 9.8 × 3.8) = 8.63 m s⁻¹ downward. Taking upward positive, (F_mean − mg)Δt = 0 − (−mv_A), so F_mean = mv_A / 0.12 + 10(9.8) = 817 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = mv_A with v_A = √(2gL) to obtain 817 N (B).

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, a proving-ground chassis mule of mass 1500 kg accelerates horizontally so a light-string plumb mass hangs at 34° to the vertical, later climbs a 8° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 55 m (static friction coefficient 0.85), and coasts from 17 m s⁻¹ against a 530 N resistive force toward the recovery marker. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the horizontal acceleration during the initial straight-line phase when a light-string plumb mass deflects by 34°?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 34° = ma and T cos 34° = mg => a = g tan 34° = 6.61 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.85 × 9.8 × 55) = 21.4 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1500)(17)² / 530 = 409 m. Target = 6.61 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 6.61 m s⁻² (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses g sin θ as if on an inclined plane rather than resolving T sin θ = ma and T cos θ = mg to obtain g tan θ.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the ratio of horizontal to vertical components, evaluating g / tan θ instead of g tan θ.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies g by cos θ instead of tan θ.

items.stem: In translational equilibrium at constant speed, a turbine casing pallet (weight 320 N) travels 28 m down a powerhouse access incline, dropping 6.7 m vertically. How much gravitational potential energy is lost over the full length of the slope?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed ΔE_k = 0. Potential energy lost = W h = 320 × 6.7 = 2.14 × 10³ J. Parallel equilibrium gives F_res = W sin θ = W h / L = 76.6 N. Target = 2.14 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ = 6.7/28 and zero net force to obtain 2.14 × 10³ J (A).

items.stem: During a range trial on a level demonstration track, a lecture-hall steel ball leaves a floor-mounted spring cannon at 34 m s⁻¹ and 34° above the horizontal. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the total time of flight before returning to a level demonstration track?
items.workedSolution: u_y = 34 sin 34° = 19.0 m s⁻¹ and u_x = 34 cos 34° = 28.2 m s⁻¹. Flight time T = 2u_y / 9.81 = 3.88 s; horizontal range R = u_x T = 109 m. Target = 3.88 s.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves orthogonal components accurately to obtain 3.88 s (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes time to reach the apex u sin θ / g rather than full time of flight.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Swaps sin θ and cos θ when resolving vertical launch speed.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses total speed u instead of vertical component u sin θ.

items.stem: Referring to the launch of an irrigation water packet from a ground-level nozzle at 45 m s⁻¹ and 66° above horizontal farmland: Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². What maximum vertical height above horizontal farmland does it reach?
items.workedSolution: At the apex v_y = 0 while horizontal velocity remains constant at v_apex = u cos 66° = 18.3 m s⁻¹. Maximum height h_max = (u sin 66°)² / (2g) = 86.1 m. Target = 86.1 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_y = 0 and constant v_x = u cos 66° at apex to obtain 86.1 m (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Converts all initial kinetic energy into gravitational potential energy, forgetting non-zero horizontal speed u cos θ at the apex.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses horizontal component u cos θ instead of vertical component u sin θ in h = u_y² / (2g).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of two in the denominator of h_max = u_y² / (2g).

items.stem: In a rebound impact on a smooth marshalling test track, wagon X (mass 1.6 kg, initial speed 13 m s⁻¹ right) hits stationary wagon Y (mass 5.8 kg), which moves right at 4.3 m s⁻¹. What is the total kinetic energy of the two bodies immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (1.6)(13) = (1.6)v_X + (5.8)(4.3) gives v_X = -2.59 m s⁻¹ (2.59 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(1.6)(2.59)² + ½(5.8)(4.3)² = 59.0 J. Energy lost = 135 J − K_f = 76.2 J. Target = 59.0 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 2.59 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 59.0 J (A).

items.stem: During a head-on collision test on a level docking-simulator rail, module X (2.5 kg) moves right at 9 m s⁻¹ while module Y (4.2 kg) moves left at 4.5 m s⁻¹ (arrow omitted), and module Y exits right at 5.5 m s⁻¹. Find the velocity of module X right after collision.
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward as positive: p_before = (2.5)(9) + (4.2)(−4.5) = 3.60 kg m s⁻¹. From p_before = (2.5)v_X + (4.2)(5.5), v_X = -7.80 m s⁻¹, which is 7.80 m s⁻¹ to the left.

markScheme.criterion: Uses signed head-on momentum p_before = 3.60 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 7.80 m s⁻¹ to the left (C).

items.stem: In a laboratory swing frame, a brass impact sphere of mass 1.9 kg hangs on a 0.8 m string, is released from rest with the string horizontal, and collides inelastically at the bottom with stationary a wax capture block of mass 4.18 kg. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the tension in the string immediately before a brass impact sphere strikes a wax capture block?
items.workedSolution: Just before collision u² = 2gL => u = 3.96 m s⁻¹. Radial Newton second law T − mg = mu²/L = 2mg gives T = 3mg = 55.9 N. Momentum conservation gives v = mu/(m+M) = 1.24 m s⁻¹. Target = 55.9 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates quarter-swing dynamics and radial/tangential laws to obtain 55.9 N (D).

items.stem: Attached to an elastic recovery cord of unstretched length 3.4 m in a vertical test bay, an aerospace drop canister of mass 6.5 kg falls from rest at the anchor, passes taut point A, and stretches the cord by 1.15 m in 0.32 s to rest at B. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the peak tension in an elastic recovery cord at the lowest point B?
items.workedSolution: Total vertical drop from release S to lowest point B is L + x = 3.4 + 1.15 = 4.55 m. By energy conservation mg(L + x) = ½kx², giving k = 2mg(L + x)/x² = 438 N m⁻¹ and peak tension T_B = kx = 504 N. Target = 504 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses full vertical drop (3.4 + 1.15) m in mg(L + x) = ½kx² to obtain 504 N (C).

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, a mine-tunnel shuttle vehicle of mass 1000 kg accelerates horizontally so a ceiling pendulum sensor hangs at 22° to the vertical, later climbs a 10° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 75 m (static friction coefficient 0.55), and coasts from 15 m s⁻¹ against a 350 N resistive force toward the shaft station. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the horizontal acceleration during the initial straight-line phase when a ceiling pendulum sensor deflects by 22°?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 22° = ma and T cos 22° = mg => a = g tan 22° = 3.96 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.55 × 9.81 × 75) = 20.1 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1000)(15)² / 350 = 321 m. Target = 3.96 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 3.96 m s⁻² (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses g sin θ as if on an inclined plane rather than resolving T sin θ = ma and T cos θ = mg to obtain g tan θ.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the ratio of horizontal to vertical components, evaluating g / tan θ instead of g tan θ.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies g by cos θ instead of tan θ.

items.stem: The diagram depicts a mining equipment skid weighing 1640 N moving at constant speed down a straight haulage incline of length 10 m and vertical height 4.4 m. What is the magnitude of the resistive force opposing motion along the slope?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed ΔE_k = 0. Potential energy lost = W h = 1640 × 4.4 = 7.22 × 10³ J. Parallel equilibrium gives F_res = W sin θ = W h / L = 722 N. Target = 722 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ = 4.4/10 and zero net force to obtain 722 N (C).

items.stem: The diagram shows a heavy logistics crate of weight 150 N moving at constant speed 6 m s⁻¹ down a rough warehouse ramp of slope length 14 m and height 8.4 m. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 150 × (8.4/14) = 90.0 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 540 W. Target = 90.0 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 90.0 N (C).

items.stem: In a kinematics experiment over a flat proving ground, an acoustic ranging dart is launched at 33 m s⁻¹ and 28° above the horizontal. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the speed of the projectile at the highest point of its trajectory?
items.workedSolution: At the apex v_y = 0 while horizontal velocity remains constant at v_apex = u cos 28° = 29.1 m s⁻¹. Maximum height h_max = (u sin 28°)² / (2g) = 12.2 m. Target = 29.1 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_y = 0 and constant v_x = u cos 28° at apex to obtain 29.1 m s⁻¹ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Assumes the projectile is momentarily stationary at its highest point, forgetting its constant horizontal velocity u cos θ.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses u sin θ instead of u cos θ for the speed at the apex.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Assumes speed remains equal to launch speed u throughout the flight.

items.stem: The diagram shows glider X of mass 2.4 kg moving right at 14 m s⁻¹ toward stationary glider Y of mass 3.2 kg on a horizontal frictionless air track; after collision, glider Y travels right at 7.02 m s⁻¹. What is the speed of glider X immediately after the collision?
items.workedSolution: Momentum conservation: (2.4)(14) = (2.4)v_X + (3.2)(7.02), giving v_X = 4.64 m s⁻¹. K_i = 235 J and K_f = 105 J, so ΔK_lost = K_i − K_f = 131 J. Target = 4.64 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves linear momentum and evaluates kinetic energy budget to obtain 4.64 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: During a head-on collision test on a horizontal magnetic-bearing guideway, shuttle X (2.5 kg) moves right at 11 m s⁻¹ while shuttle Y (3 kg) moves left at 3 m s⁻¹ (arrow omitted), and shuttle Y exits right at 1.5 m s⁻¹. Find the velocity of shuttle X right after collision.
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward as positive: p_before = (2.5)(11) + (3)(−3) = 18.5 kg m s⁻¹. From p_before = (2.5)v_X + (3)(1.5), v_X = 5.60 m s⁻¹, which is 5.60 m s⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: Uses signed head-on momentum p_before = 18.5 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 5.60 m s⁻¹ to the right (A).

items.stem: The diagram shows a telemetry capsule (2.2 kg) at the bottom of a vertical circle of radius 1.4 m in a vertical rotation stand; a high-tensile cord has a maximum safe tension of 113 N. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the maximum allowed speed at this point?
items.workedSolution: Tension is greatest at the bottom where T_max − mg = m v_max² / r. Thus v_max = √[((113/2.2) − 9.81) × 1.4] = 7.63 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves T_max − mg = mv²/r to obtain 7.63 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Adds g instead of subtracting g when rearranging T_max − mg = mv²/r.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Treats vertical circular motion as horizontal, omitting weight mg at the lowest point.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes minimum top-of-loop critical speed √(gr) instead of maximum safe bottom speed.

items.stem: The diagram illustrates a mountaineering test mass of mass 4 kg released at the support of a dynamic climbing rope (natural length 2.8 m), becoming taut at A and decelerating to rest at B (extension 1.3 m) over 0.27 s. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What mean force does a dynamic climbing rope exert between A and B?
items.workedSolution: Speed when taut at A: v_A = √(2 × 9.81 × 2.8) = 7.41 m s⁻¹ downward. Taking upward positive, (F_mean − mg)Δt = 0 − (−mv_A), so F_mean = mv_A / 0.27 + 4(9.81) = 149 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = mv_A with v_A = √(2gL) to obtain 149 N (C).

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, an instrumented test truck of mass 1400 kg accelerates horizontally so a ceiling-suspended plumb bob hangs at 38° to the vertical, later climbs a 10° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 50 m (static friction coefficient 0.8), and coasts from 18 m s⁻¹ against a 500 N resistive force toward the terminal bay. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the horizontal acceleration during the initial straight-line phase when a ceiling-suspended plumb bob deflects by 38°?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 38° = ma and T cos 38° = mg => a = g tan 38° = 7.66 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.8 × 9.8 × 50) = 19.8 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1400)(18)² / 500 = 454 m. Target = 7.66 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 7.66 m s⁻² (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses g sin θ as if on an inclined plane rather than resolving T sin θ = ma and T cos θ = mg to obtain g tan θ.

options.label: C

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses the later grade angle instead of the plumb-bob deflection angle.

items.stem: A steel ballast box (weight 200 N) slides at constant speed 4 m s⁻¹ down a braking test slope, which is 32 m long and drops 14.4 m vertically. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 200 × (14.4/32) = 90.0 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 360 W. Target = 90.0 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 90.0 N (D).

items.stem: Fired from a spring-loaded catapult at 32 m s⁻¹ and 22° above the horizontal, a robotics arena sphere lands back on a level arena floor. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What is the total time of flight before returning to a level arena floor?
items.workedSolution: u_y = 32 sin 22° = 12.0 m s⁻¹ and u_x = 32 cos 22° = 29.7 m s⁻¹. Flight time T = 2u_y / 9.8 = 2.45 s; horizontal range R = u_x T = 72.6 m. Target = 2.45 s.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves orthogonal components accurately to obtain 2.45 s (C).

options.label: D

items.stem: Travelling at 6 m s⁻¹ to the right along a horizontal magnetic-bearing guideway, shuttle X (2.8 kg) strikes stationary shuttle Y (1.2 kg), sending shuttle Y rightward at 5 m s⁻¹. What is the speed of shuttle X immediately after the collision?
items.workedSolution: Momentum conservation: (2.8)(6) = (2.8)v_X + (1.2)(5), giving v_X = 3.86 m s⁻¹. K_i = 50.4 J and K_f = 35.8 J, so ΔK_lost = K_i − K_f = 14.6 J. Target = 3.86 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves linear momentum and evaluates kinetic energy budget to obtain 3.86 m s⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: Moving rightward at 7 m s⁻¹ on a frictionless optical-bench track, carriage X (2 kg) collides head-on with stationary carriage Y (4.4 kg); immediately afterward carriage Y travels right at 3.84 m s⁻¹ and carriage X rebounds backward. What is the total kinetic energy of the two bodies immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (2)(7) = (2)v_X + (4.4)(3.84) gives v_X = -1.45 m s⁻¹ (1.45 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(2)(1.45)² + ½(4.4)(3.84)² = 34.5 J. Energy lost = 49.0 J − K_f = 14.5 J. Target = 34.5 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 1.45 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 34.5 J (B).

items.stem: Held with its 1 m light string horizontal in a pivot suspension rig, a tungsten alloy sphere (2.1 kg) swings down from rest and sticks to stationary a stationary capture cup (4.62 kg) at the lowest point. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What is the speed of the coupled bodies immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Just before collision u² = 2gL => u = 4.43 m s⁻¹. Radial Newton second law T − mg = mu²/L = 2mg gives T = 3mg = 61.8 N. Momentum conservation gives v = mu/(m+M) = 1.38 m s⁻¹. Target = 1.38 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates quarter-swing dynamics and radial/tangential laws to obtain 1.38 m s⁻¹ (C).
