items.stem: Whirled in a vertical circle of radius 1 m on a light inextensible string (breaking tension 22 N) in a circular motion demonstrator, a polymer-coated mass has mass 0.6 kg. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. Determine the greatest safe speed at the lowest point.
items.workedSolution: Tension is greatest at the bottom where T_max − mg = m v_max² / r. Thus v_max = √[((22/0.6) − 9.81) × 1] = 5.18 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves T_max − mg = mv²/r to obtain 5.18 m s⁻¹ (B).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes minimum top-of-loop critical speed √(gr) instead of maximum safe bottom speed.

items.stem: Released from rest at the support in a vertical deceleration shaft, a payload shock capsule (3.5 kg) falls freely through the 3.4 m natural length of a compliant elastomer rope to point A and then extends the Hookean cord by 0.45 m during 0.22 s to instantaneous rest at B. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What is the peak tension in a compliant elastomer rope at the lowest point B?
items.workedSolution: Total vertical drop from release S to lowest point B is L + x = 3.4 + 0.45 = 3.85 m. By energy conservation mg(L + x) = ½kx², giving k = 2mg(L + x)/x² = 1.30 × 10³ N m⁻¹ and peak tension T_B = kx = 587 N. Target = 587 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses full vertical drop (3.4 + 0.45) m in mg(L + x) = ½kx² to obtain 587 N (C).

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, an electric quarry haulage rig of mass 1300 kg accelerates horizontally so a suspended brass bob hangs at 38° to the vertical, later climbs a 8° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 80 m (static friction coefficient 0.7), and coasts from 22 m s⁻¹ against a 350 N resistive force toward the weighbridge. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What is the horizontal acceleration during the initial straight-line phase when a suspended brass bob deflects by 38°?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 38° = ma and T cos 38° = mg => a = g tan 38° = 7.66 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.7 × 9.81 × 80) = 23.4 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1300)(22)² / 350 = 899 m. Target = 7.66 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 7.66 m s⁻² (C).

items.stem: Sliding at constant velocity down a planar ski run of slope length 32 m and vertical drop 14.1 m, a snowcat maintenance sled has weight 840 N. What is the magnitude of the resistive force opposing motion along the slope?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed ΔE_k = 0. Potential energy lost = W h = 840 × 14.1 = 1.18 × 10⁴ J. Parallel equilibrium gives F_res = W sin θ = W h / L = 370 N. Target = 370 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ = 14.1/32 and zero net force to obtain 370 N (B).

items.stem: Projected from a pneumatic pitching machine at 15 m s⁻¹ at an angle of 66° above a level turf pitch, a sports-science test ball follows a parabolic arc. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the speed of the projectile at the highest point of its trajectory?
items.workedSolution: At the apex v_y = 0 while horizontal velocity remains constant at v_apex = u cos 66° = 6.10 m s⁻¹. Maximum height h_max = (u sin 66°)² / (2g) = 9.57 m. Target = 6.10 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_y = 0 and constant v_x = u cos 66° at apex to obtain 6.10 m s⁻¹ (A).

options.label: B

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses u sin θ instead of u cos θ for the speed at the apex.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Assumes speed remains equal to launch speed u throughout the flight.

items.stem: On a level low-friction dynamics rail, lighter cart X of mass 1.6 kg moving right at 6 m s⁻¹ strikes stationary heavier cart Y of mass 4.5 kg, causing cart Y to move right at 2.59 m s⁻¹ while cart X rebounds to the left. How much kinetic energy is dissipated in this rebound collision?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (1.6)(6) = (1.6)v_X + (4.5)(2.59) gives v_X = -1.28 m s⁻¹ (1.28 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(1.6)(1.28)² + ½(4.5)(2.59)² = 16.4 J. Energy lost = 28.8 J − K_f = 12.4 J. Target = 12.4 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 1.28 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 12.4 J (B).

items.stem: Approaching each other along a level docking-simulator rail, module X (4 kg, 10 m s⁻¹ to the right) collides head-on with module Y (3 kg, 2 m s⁻¹ to the left, arrow not shown); afterward module Y travels to the right at 5 m s⁻¹. Determine the final velocity of module X.
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward as positive: p_before = (4)(10) + (3)(−2) = 34.0 kg m s⁻¹. From p_before = (4)v_X + (3)(5), v_X = 4.75 m s⁻¹, which is 4.75 m s⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: Uses signed head-on momentum p_before = 34.0 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 4.75 m s⁻¹ to the right (A).

items.stem: In a light-string pendulum, a physics lecture bob of mass 0.5 kg hangs on a 1.8 m string, is released from rest with the string horizontal, and collides inelastically at the bottom with stationary a stationary putty sphere of mass 0.5 kg. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the tension in the string immediately before a physics lecture bob strikes a stationary putty sphere?
items.workedSolution: Just before collision u² = 2gL => u = 5.94 m s⁻¹. Radial Newton second law T − mg = mu²/L = 2mg gives T = 3mg = 14.7 N. Momentum conservation gives v = mu/(m+M) = 2.97 m s⁻¹. Target = 14.7 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates quarter-swing dynamics and radial/tangential laws to obtain 14.7 N (A).

items.stem: In a dry-test tower, a marine mooring weight of mass 7 kg is released from rest at the anchor of a stretchable nylon hawser of unstretched length 2 m. The cord becomes taut at A and stretches obeying Hooke's law by a maximum extension of 0.85 m over 0.34 s before a marine mooring weight comes momentarily to rest at B. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the spring constant of a stretchable nylon hawser?
items.workedSolution: Total vertical drop from release S to lowest point B is L + x = 2 + 0.85 = 2.85 m. By energy conservation mg(L + x) = ½kx², giving k = 2mg(L + x)/x² = 542 N m⁻¹ and peak tension T_B = kx = 460 N. Target = 542 N m⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses full vertical drop (2 + 0.85) m in mg(L + x) = ½kx² to obtain 542 N m⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: Dropped from rest at the anchor in a drop-test tower, an instrumented drop sphere of mass 2 kg falls freely 4 m until an elastic bungee tether becomes taut at A, then stretches the cord by 1.4 m over 0.18 s to come momentarily to rest at B. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the mean upward force exerted by an elastic bungee tether between A and B?
items.workedSolution: Speed when taut at A: v_A = √(2 × 9.81 × 4) = 8.86 m s⁻¹ downward. Taking upward positive, (F_mean − mg)Δt = 0 − (−mv_A), so F_mean = mv_A / 0.18 + 2(9.81) = 118 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = mv_A with v_A = √(2gL) to obtain 118 N (A).

items.stem: While sliding down a planar test embankment (32 m long, 9.6 m vertical height) at constant speed 5.5 m s⁻¹, a civil-engineering gabion of weight 850 N converts lost potential energy into heat. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 850 × (9.6/32) = 255 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 1.40 × 10³ W. Target = 255 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 255 N (D).

items.stem: During a range trial on a horizontal test paddock, a tracer polymer pellet leaves a ground discharge tube at 40 m s⁻¹ and 30° above the horizontal. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the total time of flight before returning to a horizontal test paddock?
items.workedSolution: u_y = 40 sin 30° = 20.0 m s⁻¹ and u_x = 40 cos 30° = 34.6 m s⁻¹. Flight time T = 2u_y / 9.8 = 4.08 s; horizontal range R = u_x T = 141 m. Target = 4.08 s.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves orthogonal components accurately to obtain 4.08 s (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes time to reach the apex u sin θ / g rather than full time of flight.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Swaps sin θ and cos θ when resolving vertical launch speed.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses total speed u instead of vertical component u sin θ.

items.stem: During an inelastic collision trial on a level docking-simulator rail, module X (mass 5.2 kg, initial rightward speed 14 m s⁻¹) hits stationary module Y (mass 1.2 kg), which moves off to the right at 14.4 m s⁻¹. What is the speed of module X immediately after the collision?
items.workedSolution: Momentum conservation: (5.2)(14) = (5.2)v_X + (1.2)(14.4), giving v_X = 10.7 m s⁻¹. K_i = 510 J and K_f = 421 J, so ΔK_lost = K_i − K_f = 88.8 J. Target = 10.7 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves linear momentum and evaluates kinetic energy budget to obtain 10.7 m s⁻¹ (B).

options.distractorRationale: Assumes both bodies stick together instead of using the measured post-collision speed of Y.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Adds m_Y v_Y instead of subtracting m_Y v_Y when solving momentum conservation.

items.stem: In a rebound impact on a polished ice test channel, sled X (mass 2 kg, initial speed 15 m s⁻¹ right) hits stationary sled Y (mass 5.2 kg), which moves right at 6.67 m s⁻¹. What is the total kinetic energy of the two bodies immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (2)(15) = (2)v_X + (5.2)(6.67) gives v_X = -2.34 m s⁻¹ (2.34 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(2)(2.34)² + ½(5.2)(6.67)² = 121 J. Energy lost = 225 J − K_f = 104 J. Target = 121 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 2.34 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 121 J (B).

options.distractorRationale: Subtracts the kinetic energy of rebounding X from Y as if kinetic energy were a signed vector.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Includes only the kinetic energy of Y and forgets the kinetic energy of rebounding X.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the kinetic energy dissipated rather than the total final kinetic energy.

items.stem: During a tensile limit test in a lecture-hall whirl rig, a calibration ball of mass 1.4 kg swings on a thin braided string of length 1.2 m rated to 33 N maximum tension. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². Calculate the maximum speed at the bottom of the path.
items.workedSolution: Tension is greatest at the bottom where T_max − mg = m v_max² / r. Thus v_max = √[((33/1.4) − 9.81) × 1.2] = 4.06 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves T_max − mg = mv²/r to obtain 4.06 m s⁻¹ (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds g instead of subtracting g when rearranging T_max − mg = mv²/r.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats vertical circular motion as horizontal, omitting weight mg at the lowest point.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes minimum top-of-loop critical speed √(gr) instead of maximum safe bottom speed.

items.stem: During an impulse-arrest test in a vertical deceleration shaft, a payload shock capsule of mass 6 kg drops freely 2.6 m to taut point A and extends a compliant elastomer rope by 0.5 m over 0.33 s until instantaneous rest at B. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.8 m s⁻². Calculate the mean upward cord force during deceleration.
items.workedSolution: Speed when taut at A: v_A = √(2 × 9.8 × 2.6) = 7.14 m s⁻¹ downward. Taking upward positive, (F_mean − mg)Δt = 0 − (−mv_A), so F_mean = mv_A / 0.33 + 6(9.8) = 189 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = mv_A with v_A = √(2gL) to obtain 189 N (D).

options.distractorRationale: Calculates mean resultant upward force mv_A/Δt and forgets to add downward weight mg to find mean cord tension.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts mg from mv_A/Δt instead of adding mg in F_mean − mg = Δp/Δt.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies momentum change mv_A by Δt instead of dividing by Δt.

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, an instrumented test truck of mass 1700 kg accelerates horizontally so a ceiling-suspended plumb bob hangs at 38° to the vertical, later climbs a 8° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 70 m (static friction coefficient 0.8), and coasts from 22 m s⁻¹ against a 620 N resistive force toward the terminal bay. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the maximum speed on the flat semicircular curve of radius 70 m without skidding?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 38° = ma and T cos 38° = mg => a = g tan 38° = 7.66 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.8 × 9.8 × 70) = 23.4 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1700)(22)² / 620 = 664 m. Target = 23.4 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 23.4 m s⁻¹ (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the static friction coefficient μ_s in μ_s mg = mv²/R.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Divides by μ_s instead of multiplying by μ_s.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes v² = μ_s g R without taking the square root.

items.stem: The diagram depicts a transformer housing weighing 280 N moving at constant speed down a substation access slope of length 33 m and vertical height 10.6 m. What is the magnitude of the resistive force opposing motion along the slope?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed ΔE_k = 0. Potential energy lost = W h = 280 × 10.6 = 2.97 × 10³ J. Parallel equilibrium gives F_res = W sin θ = W h / L = 89.9 N. Target = 89.9 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ = 10.6/33 and zero net force to obtain 89.9 N (A).

options.distractorRationale: Resolves perpendicular normal reaction W cos θ instead of parallel equilibrium force W sin θ = Wh/L.

options.label: C

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Equates resistive force along the slope to the full vertical weight W.

items.stem: The diagram shows a volcanic ballistic clast launched at 18 m s⁻¹ inclined at 60° to a flat ash plain. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What horizontal range does it cover before landing on a flat ash plain?
items.workedSolution: u_y = 18 sin 60° = 15.6 m s⁻¹ and u_x = 18 cos 60° = 9.00 m s⁻¹. Flight time T = 2u_y / 9.81 = 3.18 s; horizontal range R = u_x T = 28.6 m. Target = 28.6 m.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves orthogonal components accurately to obtain 28.6 m (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies horizontal speed by ascent time u sin θ / g instead of full flight time 2u sin θ / g.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes cos θ for sin θ in the flight-time expression.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses the 45° maximum-range formula u²/g without the angle factor sin(2θ).

items.stem: In a kinematics experiment over calm water at launch level, a rescue line-throwing bob is launched at 45 m s⁻¹ and 28° above the horizontal. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the speed of the projectile at the highest point of its trajectory?
items.workedSolution: At the apex v_y = 0 while horizontal velocity remains constant at v_apex = u cos 28° = 39.7 m s⁻¹. Maximum height h_max = (u sin 28°)² / (2g) = 22.7 m. Target = 39.7 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_y = 0 and constant v_x = u cos 28° at apex to obtain 39.7 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Assumes the projectile is momentarily stationary at its highest point, forgetting its constant horizontal velocity u cos θ.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses u sin θ instead of u cos θ for the speed at the apex.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Assumes speed remains equal to launch speed u throughout the flight.

items.stem: The diagram shows trolley X of mass 1.6 kg approaching stationary trolley Y of mass 5.8 kg at 6 m s⁻¹ on a smooth glass collision groove. After impact, trolley Y moves right at 2.17 m s⁻¹. How much kinetic energy is dissipated in this rebound collision?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (1.6)(6) = (1.6)v_X + (5.8)(2.17) gives v_X = -1.87 m s⁻¹ (1.87 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(1.6)(1.87)² + ½(5.8)(2.17)² = 16.4 J. Energy lost = 28.8 J − K_f = 12.4 J. Target = 12.4 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 1.87 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 12.4 J (C).

options.label: B

options.label: D

items.stem: On a level cleanroom linear rail, carrier X of mass 4 kg moves right at 7 m s⁻¹ toward carrier Y of mass 2.4 kg approaching head-on to the left at 4.5 m s⁻¹ (initial arrow on Y omitted). Immediately after collision, carrier Y moves right at 3.5 m s⁻¹. What is the velocity of carrier X immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward as positive: p_before = (4)(7) + (2.4)(−4.5) = 17.2 kg m s⁻¹. From p_before = (4)v_X + (2.4)(3.5), v_X = 2.20 m s⁻¹, which is 2.20 m s⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: Uses signed head-on momentum p_before = 17.2 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 2.20 m s⁻¹ to the right (A).

items.stem: The diagram shows a cast-iron hammer bob of mass 0.3 kg released from a horizontal 1.4 m string in a Charpy-style swing rig toward stationary a deformable putty mass of mass 0.54 kg at the bottom. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the tension in the string immediately before a cast-iron hammer bob strikes a deformable putty mass?
items.workedSolution: Just before collision u² = 2gL => u = 5.24 m s⁻¹. Radial Newton second law T − mg = mu²/L = 2mg gives T = 3mg = 8.83 N. Momentum conservation gives v = mu/(m+M) = 1.87 m s⁻¹. Target = 8.83 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates quarter-swing dynamics and radial/tangential laws to obtain 8.83 N (D).

items.stem: The three-stage diagram shows a bridge-jump test sandbag of mass 9.5 kg dropped from rest at the support of an elastic shock cord (natural length 2.8 m), reaching A taut and extending a further 1.05 m over 0.14 s to rest at lowest point B. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the spring constant of an elastic shock cord?
items.workedSolution: Total vertical drop from release S to lowest point B is L + x = 2.8 + 1.05 = 3.85 m. By energy conservation mg(L + x) = ½kx², giving k = 2mg(L + x)/x² = 650 N m⁻¹ and peak tension T_B = kx = 683 N. Target = 650 N m⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses full vertical drop (2.8 + 1.05) m in mg(L + x) = ½kx² to obtain 650 N m⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, a rail-yard test locomotive of mass 1400 kg accelerates horizontally so a roof-hung indicator sphere hangs at 22° to the vertical, later climbs a 8° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 50 m (static friction coefficient 0.7), and coasts from 14 m s⁻¹ against a 560 N resistive force toward the buffer platform. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the horizontal acceleration during the initial straight-line phase when a roof-hung indicator sphere deflects by 22°?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 22° = ma and T cos 22° = mg => a = g tan 22° = 3.96 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.7 × 9.81 × 50) = 18.5 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1400)(14)² / 560 = 245 m. Target = 3.96 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 3.96 m s⁻² (C).

options.label: D

items.stem: Of weight 120 N, a steel cable drum cradle descends a warehouse ramp at steady speed over a slope distance of 31 m through a vertical height change of 14.9 m. How much gravitational potential energy is lost over the full length of the slope?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed ΔE_k = 0. Potential energy lost = W h = 120 × 14.9 = 1.79 × 10³ J. Parallel equilibrium gives F_res = W sin θ = W h / L = 57.7 N. Target = 1.79 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ = 14.9/31 and zero net force to obtain 1.79 × 10³ J (D).

items.stem: A quarry stone skip (weight 650 N) slides at constant speed 2.5 m s⁻¹ down a planar service incline, which is 24 m long and drops 8.4 m vertically. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 650 × (8.4/24) = 228 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 569 W. Target = 228 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 228 N (C).

items.stem: A tracer polymer pellet leaves a ground discharge tube at 27 m s⁻¹ inclined at 55° above the horizontal over a horizontal test paddock. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What maximum vertical height above a horizontal test paddock does it reach?
items.workedSolution: At the apex v_y = 0 while horizontal velocity remains constant at v_apex = u cos 55° = 15.5 m s⁻¹. Maximum height h_max = (u sin 55°)² / (2g) = 25.0 m. Target = 25.0 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_y = 0 and constant v_x = u cos 55° at apex to obtain 25.0 m (A).

options.label: D

items.stem: Travelling at 12 m s⁻¹ to the right along a precision gas-bearing trough, rider X (2.8 kg) strikes stationary rider Y (2.4 kg), sending rider Y rightward at 8.18 m s⁻¹. What is the speed of rider X immediately after the collision?
items.workedSolution: Momentum conservation: (2.8)(12) = (2.8)v_X + (2.4)(8.18), giving v_X = 4.99 m s⁻¹. K_i = 202 J and K_f = 115 J, so ΔK_lost = K_i − K_f = 86.5 J. Target = 4.99 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves linear momentum and evaluates kinetic energy budget to obtain 4.99 m s⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: During a head-on collision test on a level docking-simulator rail, module X (4 kg) moves right at 8 m s⁻¹ while module Y (4.2 kg) moves left at 6 m s⁻¹ (arrow omitted), and module Y exits right at 2.5 m s⁻¹. Find the velocity of module X right after collision.
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward as positive: p_before = (4)(8) + (4.2)(−6) = 6.80 kg m s⁻¹. From p_before = (4)v_X + (4.2)(2.5), v_X = -0.925 m s⁻¹, which is 0.925 m s⁻¹ to the left.

markScheme.criterion: Uses signed head-on momentum p_before = 6.80 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 0.925 m s⁻¹ to the left (A).

items.stem: Whirled in a vertical circle of radius 1.2 m on a light inextensible wire (breaking tension 38 N) in a vertical circular test rig, a steel sensor sphere has mass 0.8 kg. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. Determine the greatest safe speed at the lowest point.
items.workedSolution: Tension is greatest at the bottom where T_max − mg = m v_max² / r. Thus v_max = √[((38/0.8) − 9.81) × 1.2] = 6.73 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves T_max − mg = mv²/r to obtain 6.73 m s⁻¹ (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds g instead of subtracting g when rearranging T_max − mg = mv²/r.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats vertical circular motion as horizontal, omitting weight mg at the lowest point.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes minimum top-of-loop critical speed √(gr) instead of maximum safe bottom speed.

items.stem: In a stage gridiron support, a stunt-rig counterweight (11 kg) falls from rest at the support through the 2.6 m slack length of an elastic arrest cable to point A and is brought momentarily to rest after stretching 0.8 m in a time of 0.15 s to B. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. Determine the time-averaged tension in an elastic arrest cable during this 0.15 s interval.
items.workedSolution: Speed when taut at A: v_A = √(2 × 9.81 × 2.6) = 7.14 m s⁻¹ downward. Taking upward positive, (F_mean − mg)Δt = 0 − (−mv_A), so F_mean = mv_A / 0.15 + 11(9.81) = 632 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = mv_A with v_A = √(2gL) to obtain 632 N (D).

items.stem: Across a level driving range, a tee on flat ground projects a golf launch-monitor ball with initial speed 26 m s⁻¹ at 38° above the horizontal. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What horizontal range does it cover before landing on a level driving range?
items.workedSolution: u_y = 26 sin 38° = 16.0 m s⁻¹ and u_x = 26 cos 38° = 20.5 m s⁻¹. Flight time T = 2u_y / 9.8 = 3.27 s; horizontal range R = u_x T = 66.9 m. Target = 66.9 m.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves orthogonal components accurately to obtain 66.9 m (B).

items.stem: On a frictionless optical-bench track, carriage X of mass 2.4 kg moves right at 5 m s⁻¹ and collides with stationary carriage Y of mass 2.4 kg. Immediately after impact, carriage Y moves right at 3.64 m s⁻¹. What is the speed of carriage X immediately after the collision?
items.workedSolution: Momentum conservation: (2.4)(5) = (2.4)v_X + (2.4)(3.64), giving v_X = 1.36 m s⁻¹. K_i = 30.0 J and K_f = 18.1 J, so ΔK_lost = K_i − K_f = 11.9 J. Target = 1.36 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves linear momentum and evaluates kinetic energy budget to obtain 1.36 m s⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: On a horizontal magnetic-bearing guideway, lighter shuttle X of mass 1.8 kg moving right at 15 m s⁻¹ strikes stationary heavier shuttle Y of mass 4 kg, causing shuttle Y to move right at 8.93 m s⁻¹ while shuttle X rebounds to the left. How much kinetic energy is dissipated in this rebound collision?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (1.8)(15) = (1.8)v_X + (4)(8.93) gives v_X = -4.84 m s⁻¹ (4.84 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(1.8)(4.84)² + ½(4)(8.93)² = 181 J. Energy lost = 203 J − K_f = 21.9 J. Target = 21.9 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 4.84 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 21.9 J (B).

items.stem: In a laboratory swing frame, a brass impact sphere of mass 2.5 kg hangs on a 1.2 m string, is released from rest with the string horizontal, and collides inelastically at the bottom with stationary a wax capture block of mass 5.5 kg. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the tension in the string immediately before a brass impact sphere strikes a wax capture block?
items.workedSolution: Just before collision u² = 2gL => u = 4.85 m s⁻¹. Radial Newton second law T − mg = mu²/L = 2mg gives T = 3mg = 73.6 N. Momentum conservation gives v = mu/(m+M) = 1.52 m s⁻¹. Target = 73.6 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates quarter-swing dynamics and radial/tangential laws to obtain 73.6 N (A).

items.stem: In a vertical loop frame, a compact lead bob of mass 3 kg moves in a vertical circle of radius 2.2 m on a light steel cable, which snaps if tension exceeds 83 N. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the maximum speed a compact lead bob can have at the bottom without breaking a light steel cable?
items.workedSolution: Tension is greatest at the bottom where T_max − mg = m v_max² / r. Thus v_max = √[((83/3) − 9.81) × 2.2] = 6.27 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves T_max − mg = mv²/r to obtain 6.27 m s⁻¹ (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds g instead of subtracting g when rearranging T_max − mg = mv²/r.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats vertical circular motion as horizontal, omitting weight mg at the lowest point.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes minimum top-of-loop critical speed √(gr) instead of maximum safe bottom speed.

items.stem: In a laboratory ceiling mount, a calibration steel ball of mass 7 kg is released from rest at the anchor of a Hookean rubber cord of unstretched length 2 m. The cord becomes taut at A and stretches obeying Hooke's law by a maximum extension of 0.55 m over 0.26 s before a calibration steel ball comes momentarily to rest at B. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the spring constant of a Hookean rubber cord?
items.workedSolution: Total vertical drop from release S to lowest point B is L + x = 2 + 0.55 = 2.55 m. By energy conservation mg(L + x) = ½kx², giving k = 2mg(L + x)/x² = 1.16 × 10³ N m⁻¹ and peak tension T_B = kx = 636 N. Target = 1.16 × 10³ N m⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses full vertical drop (2 + 0.55) m in mg(L + x) = ½kx² to obtain 1.16 × 10³ N m⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, a heavy-duty rescue tender of mass 1600 kg accelerates horizontally so a suspended steel bob hangs at 26° to the vertical, later climbs a 8° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 60 m (static friction coefficient 0.55), and coasts from 14 m s⁻¹ against a 500 N resistive force toward the depot line. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the horizontal acceleration during the initial straight-line phase when a suspended steel bob deflects by 26°?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 26° = ma and T cos 26° = mg => a = g tan 26° = 4.78 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.55 × 9.81 × 60) = 18.0 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1600)(14)² / 500 = 314 m. Target = 4.78 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 4.78 m s⁻² (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses g sin θ as if on an inclined plane rather than resolving T sin θ = ma and T cos θ = mg to obtain g tan θ.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the ratio of horizontal to vertical components, evaluating g / tan θ instead of g tan θ.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies g by cos θ instead of tan θ.

items.stem: In translational equilibrium at constant speed, a freight container sled (weight 720 N) travels 30 m down a dockyard unloading ramp, dropping 7.2 m vertically. How much gravitational potential energy is lost over the full length of the slope?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed ΔE_k = 0. Potential energy lost = W h = 720 × 7.2 = 5.18 × 10³ J. Parallel equilibrium gives F_res = W sin θ = W h / L = 173 N. Target = 5.18 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ = 7.2/30 and zero net force to obtain 5.18 × 10³ J (D).

items.stem: While sliding down a refractory cooling chute (20 m long, 9 m vertical height) at constant speed 6 m s⁻¹, a foundry ingot sled of weight 750 N converts lost potential energy into heat. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 750 × (9/20) = 338 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 2.03 × 10³ W. Target = 338 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 338 N (B).

items.stem: Referring to the launch of a hail-impact test sphere from an angled gas gun at 27 m s⁻¹ and 66° above a horizontal test hall: Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². What maximum vertical height above a horizontal test hall does it reach?
items.workedSolution: At the apex v_y = 0 while horizontal velocity remains constant at v_apex = u cos 66° = 11.0 m s⁻¹. Maximum height h_max = (u sin 66°)² / (2g) = 31.0 m. Target = 31.0 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_y = 0 and constant v_x = u cos 66° at apex to obtain 31.0 m (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Converts all initial kinetic energy into gravitational potential energy, forgetting non-zero horizontal speed u cos θ at the apex.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses horizontal component u cos θ instead of vertical component u sin θ in h = u_y² / (2g).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of two in the denominator of h_max = u_y² / (2g).

items.stem: In a rebound impact on a level cleanroom linear rail, carrier X (mass 1.2 kg, initial speed 10 m s⁻¹ right) hits stationary carrier Y (mass 3.4 kg), which moves right at 4.12 m s⁻¹. What is the total kinetic energy of the two bodies immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (1.2)(10) = (1.2)v_X + (3.4)(4.12) gives v_X = -1.67 m s⁻¹ (1.67 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(1.2)(1.67)² + ½(3.4)(4.12)² = 30.5 J. Energy lost = 60.0 J − K_f = 29.5 J. Target = 30.5 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 1.67 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 30.5 J (B).

options.distractorRationale: Subtracts the kinetic energy of rebounding X from Y as if kinetic energy were a signed vector.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Includes only the kinetic energy of Y and forgets the kinetic energy of rebounding X.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Assumes the collision is perfectly elastic and equates K_f to K_i.

items.stem: During a head-on collision test on a horizontal magnetic-bearing guideway, shuttle X (3 kg) moves right at 10 m s⁻¹ while shuttle Y (2.4 kg) moves left at 5 m s⁻¹ (arrow omitted), and shuttle Y exits right at 3.5 m s⁻¹. Find the velocity of shuttle X right after collision.
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward as positive: p_before = (3)(10) + (2.4)(−5) = 18.0 kg m s⁻¹. From p_before = (3)v_X + (2.4)(3.5), v_X = 3.20 m s⁻¹, which is 3.20 m s⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: Uses signed head-on momentum p_before = 18.0 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 3.20 m s⁻¹ to the right (A).

items.stem: Swinging from rest through a quarter-circle of radius 1.8 m in a suspension test gantry, an instrumented pendulum mass (mass 1.5 kg) couples on impact with stationary a magnetic-latch block (mass 3.3 kg). Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the speed of the coupled bodies immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Just before collision u² = 2gL => u = 5.94 m s⁻¹. Radial Newton second law T − mg = mu²/L = 2mg gives T = 3mg = 44.1 N. Momentum conservation gives v = mu/(m+M) = 1.86 m s⁻¹. Target = 1.86 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates quarter-swing dynamics and radial/tangential laws to obtain 1.86 m s⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: Attached to a braided dynamic lanyard of unstretched length 3.4 m in a fall-arrest gantry, a rescue arrest dummy of mass 6.5 kg falls from rest at the anchor, passes taut point A, and stretches the cord by 1.35 m in 0.16 s to rest at B. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the peak tension in a braided dynamic lanyard at the lowest point B?
items.workedSolution: Total vertical drop from release S to lowest point B is L + x = 3.4 + 1.35 = 4.75 m. By energy conservation mg(L + x) = ½kx², giving k = 2mg(L + x)/x² = 332 N m⁻¹ and peak tension T_B = kx = 449 N. Target = 449 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses full vertical drop (3.4 + 1.35) m in mg(L + x) = ½kx² to obtain 449 N (A).

items.stem: During an impulse-arrest test in an overhead hoist beam, a crane overload test block of mass 13 kg drops freely 3 m to taut point A and extends an elastic snubber line by 1.3 m over 0.36 s until instantaneous rest at B. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². Calculate the mean upward cord force during deceleration.
items.workedSolution: Speed when taut at A: v_A = √(2 × 9.81 × 3) = 7.67 m s⁻¹ downward. Taking upward positive, (F_mean − mg)Δt = 0 − (−mv_A), so F_mean = mv_A / 0.36 + 13(9.81) = 405 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = mv_A with v_A = √(2gL) to obtain 405 N (C).

items.stem: The diagram shows an expedition supply sled of weight 200 N moving at constant speed 4 m s⁻¹ down a crusty glacier slope of slope length 22 m and height 8.8 m. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 200 × (8.8/22) = 80.0 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 320 W. Target = 80.0 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 80.0 N (D).

items.stem: The diagram shows an acoustic ranging dart launched at 42 m s⁻¹ inclined at 34° to a flat proving ground. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.8 m s⁻². What horizontal range does it cover before landing on a flat proving ground?
items.workedSolution: u_y = 42 sin 34° = 23.5 m s⁻¹ and u_x = 42 cos 34° = 34.8 m s⁻¹. Flight time T = 2u_y / 9.8 = 4.79 s; horizontal range R = u_x T = 167 m. Target = 167 m.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves orthogonal components accurately to obtain 167 m (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies horizontal speed by ascent time u sin θ / g instead of full flight time 2u sin θ / g.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes cos θ for sin θ in the flight-time expression.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses the 45° maximum-range formula u²/g without the angle factor sin(2θ).

items.stem: The diagram shows sled X of mass 1.6 kg moving right at 4 m s⁻¹ toward stationary sled Y of mass 1.6 kg on a polished ice test channel; after collision, sled Y travels right at 2.77 m s⁻¹. What is the speed of sled X immediately after the collision?
items.workedSolution: Momentum conservation: (1.6)(4) = (1.6)v_X + (1.6)(2.77), giving v_X = 1.23 m s⁻¹. K_i = 12.8 J and K_f = 7.35 J, so ΔK_lost = K_i − K_f = 5.45 J. Target = 1.23 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves linear momentum and evaluates kinetic energy budget to obtain 1.23 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: B

items.stem: The diagram shows module X of mass 0.8 kg approaching stationary module Y of mass 2.9 kg at 6 m s⁻¹ on a level docking-simulator rail. After impact, module Y moves right at 2.17 m s⁻¹. How much kinetic energy is dissipated in this rebound collision?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (0.8)(6) = (0.8)v_X + (2.9)(2.17) gives v_X = -1.87 m s⁻¹ (1.87 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(0.8)(1.87)² + ½(2.9)(2.17)² = 8.22 J. Energy lost = 14.4 J − K_f = 6.18 J. Target = 6.18 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 1.87 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 6.18 J (B).

options.distractorRationale: Treats the rebounding kinetic energy of X as negative because v_X < 0, subtracting ½m_X v_X² instead of adding scalar kinetic energies.

options.label: C

options.label: D

items.stem: The diagram shows a gyroscope test mass (2.6 kg) at the bottom of a vertical circle of radius 1.2 m in a vertical-plane spinner; a light radial tether has a maximum safe tension of 103 N. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the maximum allowed speed at this point?
items.workedSolution: Tension is greatest at the bottom where T_max − mg = m v_max² / r. Thus v_max = √[((103/2.6) − 9.81) × 1.2] = 5.98 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves T_max − mg = mv²/r to obtain 5.98 m s⁻¹ (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds g instead of subtracting g when rearranging T_max − mg = mv²/r.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats vertical circular motion as horizontal, omitting weight mg at the lowest point.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes minimum top-of-loop critical speed √(gr) instead of maximum safe bottom speed.

items.stem: The diagram illustrates a calibration steel ball of mass 2 kg released at the support of a Hookean rubber cord (natural length 2 m), becoming taut at A and decelerating to rest at B (extension 0.8 m) over 0.18 s. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.8 m s⁻². What mean force does a Hookean rubber cord exert between A and B?
items.workedSolution: Speed when taut at A: v_A = √(2 × 9.8 × 2) = 6.26 m s⁻¹ downward. Taking upward positive, (F_mean − mg)Δt = 0 − (−mv_A), so F_mean = mv_A / 0.18 + 2(9.8) = 89.2 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = mv_A with v_A = √(2gL) to obtain 89.2 N (C).

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, a proving-ground chassis mule of mass 1600 kg accelerates horizontally so a light-string plumb mass hangs at 34° to the vertical, later climbs a 10° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 55 m (static friction coefficient 0.45), and coasts from 15 m s⁻¹ against a 380 N resistive force toward the recovery marker. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the horizontal acceleration during the initial straight-line phase when a light-string plumb mass deflects by 34°?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 34° = ma and T cos 34° = mg => a = g tan 34° = 6.61 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.45 × 9.8 × 55) = 15.6 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1600)(15)² / 380 = 474 m. Target = 6.61 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 6.61 m s⁻² (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses g sin θ as if on an inclined plane rather than resolving T sin θ = ma and T cos θ = mg to obtain g tan θ.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the ratio of horizontal to vertical components, evaluating g / tan θ instead of g tan θ.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies g by cos θ instead of tan θ.

items.stem: Of weight 720 N, a turbine casing pallet descends a powerhouse access incline at steady speed over a slope distance of 27 m through a vertical height change of 9.7 m. How much gravitational potential energy is lost over the full length of the slope?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed ΔE_k = 0. Potential energy lost = W h = 720 × 9.7 = 6.98 × 10³ J. Parallel equilibrium gives F_res = W sin θ = W h / L = 259 N. Target = 6.98 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ = 9.7/27 and zero net force to obtain 6.98 × 10³ J (A).

items.stem: Fired from a floor-mounted spring cannon at 44 m s⁻¹ and 56° above the horizontal, a lecture-hall steel ball lands back on a level demonstration track. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What is the total time of flight before returning to a level demonstration track?
items.workedSolution: u_y = 44 sin 56° = 36.5 m s⁻¹ and u_x = 44 cos 56° = 24.6 m s⁻¹. Flight time T = 2u_y / 9.81 = 7.44 s; horizontal range R = u_x T = 183 m. Target = 7.44 s.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves orthogonal components accurately to obtain 7.44 s (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes time to reach the apex u sin θ / g rather than full time of flight.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Swaps sin θ and cos θ when resolving vertical launch speed.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses total speed u instead of vertical component u sin θ.

items.stem: An irrigation water packet leaves a ground-level nozzle at 30 m s⁻¹ inclined at 55° above the horizontal over horizontal farmland. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What maximum vertical height above horizontal farmland does it reach?
items.workedSolution: At the apex v_y = 0 while horizontal velocity remains constant at v_apex = u cos 55° = 17.2 m s⁻¹. Maximum height h_max = (u sin 55°)² / (2g) = 30.8 m. Target = 30.8 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_y = 0 and constant v_x = u cos 55° at apex to obtain 30.8 m (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Converts all initial kinetic energy into gravitational potential energy, forgetting non-zero horizontal speed u cos θ at the apex.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses horizontal component u cos θ instead of vertical component u sin θ in h = u_y² / (2g).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of two in the denominator of h_max = u_y² / (2g).

items.stem: Moving rightward at 6 m s⁻¹ on a smooth marshalling test track, wagon X (1.4 kg) collides head-on with stationary wagon Y (4.8 kg); immediately afterward wagon Y travels right at 2.28 m s⁻¹ and wagon X rebounds backward. What is the total kinetic energy of the two bodies immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (1.4)(6) = (1.4)v_X + (4.8)(2.28) gives v_X = -1.82 m s⁻¹ (1.82 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(1.4)(1.82)² + ½(4.8)(2.28)² = 14.8 J. Energy lost = 25.2 J − K_f = 10.4 J. Target = 14.8 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 1.82 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 14.8 J (A).

items.stem: Approaching each other along a level docking-simulator rail, module X (4 kg, 7 m s⁻¹ to the right) collides head-on with module Y (3.6 kg, 5.5 m s⁻¹ to the left, arrow not shown); afterward module Y travels to the right at 3 m s⁻¹. Determine the final velocity of module X.
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward as positive: p_before = (4)(7) + (3.6)(−5.5) = 8.20 kg m s⁻¹. From p_before = (4)v_X + (3.6)(3), v_X = -0.650 m s⁻¹, which is 0.650 m s⁻¹ to the left.

markScheme.criterion: Uses signed head-on momentum p_before = 8.20 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 0.650 m s⁻¹ to the left (B).

items.stem: Held with its 2.2 m light string horizontal in a ballistic pendulum rig, a steel pendulum bob (0.3 kg) swings down from rest and sticks to stationary a lump of modelling clay (0.42 kg) at the lowest point. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What is the speed of the coupled bodies immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Just before collision u² = 2gL => u = 6.57 m s⁻¹. Radial Newton second law T − mg = mu²/L = 2mg gives T = 3mg = 8.83 N. Momentum conservation gives v = mu/(m+M) = 2.74 m s⁻¹. Target = 2.74 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates quarter-swing dynamics and radial/tangential laws to obtain 2.74 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: Released from rest at the support in a vertical test bay, an aerospace drop canister (9.5 kg) falls freely through the 1.8 m natural length of an elastic recovery cord to point A and then extends the Hookean cord by 0.95 m during 0.28 s to instantaneous rest at B. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What is the peak tension in an elastic recovery cord at the lowest point B?
items.workedSolution: Total vertical drop from release S to lowest point B is L + x = 1.8 + 0.95 = 2.75 m. By energy conservation mg(L + x) = ½kx², giving k = 2mg(L + x)/x² = 567 N m⁻¹ and peak tension T_B = kx = 539 N. Target = 539 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses full vertical drop (1.8 + 0.95) m in mg(L + x) = ½kx² to obtain 539 N (A).

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, a heavy-duty rescue tender of mass 1500 kg accelerates horizontally so a suspended steel bob hangs at 18° to the vertical, later climbs a 12° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 50 m (static friction coefficient 0.55), and coasts from 20 m s⁻¹ against a 470 N resistive force toward the depot line. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the maximum speed on the flat semicircular curve of radius 50 m without skidding?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 18° = ma and T cos 18° = mg => a = g tan 18° = 3.19 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.55 × 9.81 × 50) = 16.4 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1500)(20)² / 470 = 638 m. Target = 16.4 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 16.4 m s⁻¹ (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the static friction coefficient μ_s in μ_s mg = mv²/R.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides by μ_s instead of multiplying by μ_s.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes v² = μ_s g R without taking the square root.

items.stem: Sliding at constant velocity down a straight haulage incline of slope length 20 m and vertical drop 7.2 m, a mining equipment skid has weight 1360 N. What is the magnitude of the resistive force opposing motion along the slope?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed ΔE_k = 0. Potential energy lost = W h = 1360 × 7.2 = 9.79 × 10³ J. Parallel equilibrium gives F_res = W sin θ = W h / L = 490 N. Target = 490 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ = 7.2/20 and zero net force to obtain 490 N (A).

items.stem: Descending a rough warehouse ramp of length 20 m and vertical drop 11 m at a steady speed of 4.5 m s⁻¹, a heavy logistics crate has weight 450 N. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 450 × (11/20) = 248 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 1.11 × 10³ W. Target = 248 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 248 N (C).

items.stem: Projected from a calibrated ground launcher at 39 m s⁻¹ at an angle of 37° above a flat proving ground, an acoustic ranging dart follows a parabolic arc. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the speed of the projectile at the highest point of its trajectory?
items.workedSolution: At the apex v_y = 0 while horizontal velocity remains constant at v_apex = u cos 37° = 31.1 m s⁻¹. Maximum height h_max = (u sin 37°)² / (2g) = 28.1 m. Target = 31.1 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_y = 0 and constant v_x = u cos 37° at apex to obtain 31.1 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: On a horizontal frictionless air track, glider X of mass 4.8 kg moves right at 6 m s⁻¹ and collides with stationary glider Y of mass 0.8 kg. Immediately after impact, glider Y moves right at 6.12 m s⁻¹. What is the speed of glider X immediately after the collision?
items.workedSolution: Momentum conservation: (4.8)(6) = (4.8)v_X + (0.8)(6.12), giving v_X = 4.98 m s⁻¹. K_i = 86.4 J and K_f = 74.5 J, so ΔK_lost = K_i − K_f = 11.9 J. Target = 4.98 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves linear momentum and evaluates kinetic energy budget to obtain 4.98 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: On a smooth marshalling test track, wagon X of mass 3.5 kg moves right at 10 m s⁻¹ toward wagon Y of mass 1.2 kg approaching head-on to the left at 5.5 m s⁻¹ (initial arrow on Y omitted). Immediately after collision, wagon Y moves right at 4.5 m s⁻¹. What is the velocity of wagon X immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward as positive: p_before = (3.5)(10) + (1.2)(−5.5) = 28.4 kg m s⁻¹. From p_before = (3.5)v_X + (1.2)(4.5), v_X = 6.57 m s⁻¹, which is 6.57 m s⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: Uses signed head-on momentum p_before = 28.4 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 6.57 m s⁻¹ to the right (A).

items.stem: In a vertical rotation stand, a telemetry capsule of mass 0.4 kg moves in a vertical circle of radius 2 m on a high-tensile cord, which snaps if tension exceeds 21 N. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the maximum speed a telemetry capsule can have at the bottom without breaking a high-tensile cord?
items.workedSolution: Tension is greatest at the bottom where T_max − mg = m v_max² / r. Thus v_max = √[((21/0.4) − 9.81) × 2] = 9.24 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves T_max − mg = mv²/r to obtain 9.24 m s⁻¹ (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds g instead of subtracting g when rearranging T_max − mg = mv²/r.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats vertical circular motion as horizontal, omitting weight mg at the lowest point.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes minimum top-of-loop critical speed √(gr) instead of maximum safe bottom speed.

items.stem: In an overhead hoist beam, a crane overload test block (2 kg) falls from rest at the support through the 4.6 m slack length of an elastic snubber line to point A and is brought momentarily to rest after stretching 1.1 m in a time of 0.12 s to B. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. Determine the time-averaged tension in an elastic snubber line during this 0.12 s interval.
items.workedSolution: Speed when taut at A: v_A = √(2 × 9.81 × 4.6) = 9.50 m s⁻¹ downward. Taking upward positive, (F_mean − mg)Δt = 0 − (−mv_A), so F_mean = mv_A / 0.12 + 2(9.81) = 178 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = mv_A with v_A = √(2gL) to obtain 178 N (D).

items.stem: On a smooth marshalling test track, wagon X of mass 4 kg moves right at 13 m s⁻¹ toward wagon Y of mass 3 kg approaching head-on to the left at 2.5 m s⁻¹ (initial arrow on Y omitted). Immediately after collision, wagon Y moves right at 2 m s⁻¹. What is the velocity of wagon X immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward as positive: p_before = (4)(13) + (3)(−2.5) = 44.5 kg m s⁻¹. From p_before = (4)v_X + (3)(2), v_X = 9.63 m s⁻¹, which is 9.63 m s⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: Uses signed head-on momentum p_before = 44.5 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 9.63 m s⁻¹ to the right (D).

items.stem: In a vertical rotation stand, a telemetry capsule of mass 2.6 kg moves in a vertical circle of radius 1 m on a high-tensile cord, which snaps if tension exceeds 62 N. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the maximum speed a telemetry capsule can have at the bottom without breaking a high-tensile cord?
items.workedSolution: Tension is greatest at the bottom where T_max − mg = m v_max² / r. Thus v_max = √[((62/2.6) − 9.81) × 1] = 3.75 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves T_max − mg = mv²/r to obtain 3.75 m s⁻¹ (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds g instead of subtracting g when rearranging T_max − mg = mv²/r.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats vertical circular motion as horizontal, omitting weight mg at the lowest point.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes minimum top-of-loop critical speed √(gr) instead of maximum safe bottom speed.

items.stem: Dropped from rest at the anchor in a cliff-sim drop frame, a mountaineering test mass of mass 2 kg falls freely 3 m until a dynamic climbing rope becomes taut at A, then stretches the cord by 1.2 m over 0.27 s to come momentarily to rest at B. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the mean upward force exerted by a dynamic climbing rope between A and B?
items.workedSolution: Speed when taut at A: v_A = √(2 × 9.81 × 3) = 7.67 m s⁻¹ downward. Taking upward positive, (F_mean − mg)Δt = 0 − (−mv_A), so F_mean = mv_A / 0.27 + 2(9.81) = 76.4 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = mv_A with v_A = √(2gL) to obtain 76.4 N (C).

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, an instrumented test truck of mass 900 kg accelerates horizontally so a ceiling-suspended plumb bob hangs at 30° to the vertical, later climbs a 8° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 90 m (static friction coefficient 0.8), and coasts from 22 m s⁻¹ against a 590 N resistive force toward the terminal bay. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the horizontal acceleration during the initial straight-line phase when a ceiling-suspended plumb bob deflects by 30°?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 30° = ma and T cos 30° = mg => a = g tan 30° = 5.66 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.8 × 9.8 × 90) = 26.6 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(900)(22)² / 590 = 369 m. Target = 5.66 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 5.66 m s⁻² (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses g sin θ as if on an inclined plane rather than resolving T sin θ = ma and T cos θ = mg to obtain g tan θ.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the ratio of horizontal to vertical components, evaluating g / tan θ instead of g tan θ.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies g by cos θ instead of tan θ.

items.stem: While sliding down a braking test slope (10 m long, 4 m vertical height) at constant speed 4.5 m s⁻¹, a steel ballast box of weight 700 N converts lost potential energy into heat. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 700 × (4/10) = 280 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 1.26 × 10³ W. Target = 280 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 280 N (D).

items.stem: During a range trial on a level arena floor, a robotics arena sphere leaves a spring-loaded catapult at 26 m s⁻¹ and 34° above the horizontal. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the total time of flight before returning to a level arena floor?
items.workedSolution: u_y = 26 sin 34° = 14.5 m s⁻¹ and u_x = 26 cos 34° = 21.6 m s⁻¹. Flight time T = 2u_y / 9.8 = 2.97 s; horizontal range R = u_x T = 64.0 m. Target = 2.97 s.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves orthogonal components accurately to obtain 2.97 s (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes time to reach the apex u sin θ / g rather than full time of flight.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Swaps sin θ and cos θ when resolving vertical launch speed.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses total speed u instead of vertical component u sin θ.

items.stem: On a polished ice test channel, sled X of mass 2.4 kg moves right at 8 m s⁻¹ and collides with stationary sled Y of mass 1.6 kg. Immediately after impact, sled Y moves right at 6.81 m s⁻¹. How much kinetic energy is lost in the collision?
items.workedSolution: Momentum conservation: (2.4)(8) = (2.4)v_X + (1.6)(6.81), giving v_X = 3.46 m s⁻¹. K_i = 76.8 J and K_f = 51.5 J, so ΔK_lost = K_i − K_f = 25.3 J. Target = 25.3 J.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves linear momentum and evaluates kinetic energy budget to obtain 25.3 J (A).

items.stem: In a rebound impact on a frictionless optical-bench track, carriage X (mass 0.8 kg, initial speed 7 m s⁻¹ right) hits stationary carriage Y (mass 1.8 kg), which moves right at 3.77 m s⁻¹. What is the total kinetic energy of the two bodies immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (0.8)(7) = (0.8)v_X + (1.8)(3.77) gives v_X = -1.48 m s⁻¹ (1.48 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(0.8)(1.48)² + ½(1.8)(3.77)² = 13.7 J. Energy lost = 19.6 J − K_f = 5.93 J. Target = 13.7 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 1.48 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 13.7 J (D).

items.stem: Swinging from rest through a quarter-circle of radius 1.8 m in a pivot suspension rig, a tungsten alloy sphere (mass 2.3 kg) couples on impact with stationary a stationary capture cup (mass 4.14 kg). Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the speed of the coupled bodies immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Just before collision u² = 2gL => u = 5.94 m s⁻¹. Radial Newton second law T − mg = mu²/L = 2mg gives T = 3mg = 67.7 N. Momentum conservation gives v = mu/(m+M) = 2.12 m s⁻¹. Target = 2.12 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates quarter-swing dynamics and radial/tangential laws to obtain 2.12 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: During a tensile limit test in a circular motion demonstrator, a polymer-coated mass of mass 2.6 kg swings on a light inextensible string of length 0.6 m rated to 92 N maximum tension. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². Calculate the maximum speed at the bottom of the path.
items.workedSolution: Tension is greatest at the bottom where T_max − mg = m v_max² / r. Thus v_max = √[((92/2.6) − 9.81) × 0.6] = 3.92 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves T_max − mg = mv²/r to obtain 3.92 m s⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: Attached to a compliant elastomer rope of unstretched length 2 m in a vertical deceleration shaft, a payload shock capsule of mass 8.5 kg falls from rest at the anchor, passes taut point A, and stretches the cord by 0.95 m in 0.16 s to rest at B. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the peak tension in a compliant elastomer rope at the lowest point B?
items.workedSolution: Total vertical drop from release S to lowest point B is L + x = 2 + 0.95 = 2.95 m. By energy conservation mg(L + x) = ½kx², giving k = 2mg(L + x)/x² = 545 N m⁻¹ and peak tension T_B = kx = 517 N. Target = 517 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses full vertical drop (2 + 0.95) m in mg(L + x) = ½kx² to obtain 517 N (C).

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, an electric quarry haulage rig of mass 1500 kg accelerates horizontally so a suspended brass bob hangs at 30° to the vertical, later climbs a 14° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 95 m (static friction coefficient 0.55), and coasts from 17 m s⁻¹ against a 380 N resistive force toward the weighbridge. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the horizontal acceleration during the initial straight-line phase when a suspended brass bob deflects by 30°?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 30° = ma and T cos 30° = mg => a = g tan 30° = 5.66 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.55 × 9.81 × 95) = 22.6 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1500)(17)² / 380 = 570 m. Target = 5.66 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 5.66 m s⁻² (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses g sin θ as if on an inclined plane rather than resolving T sin θ = ma and T cos θ = mg to obtain g tan θ.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the ratio of horizontal to vertical components, evaluating g / tan θ instead of g tan θ.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies g by cos θ instead of tan θ.

items.stem: The diagram depicts a snowcat maintenance sled weighing 840 N moving at constant speed down a planar ski run of length 10 m and vertical height 3.6 m. What is the magnitude of the resistive force opposing motion along the slope?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed ΔE_k = 0. Potential energy lost = W h = 840 × 3.6 = 3.02 × 10³ J. Parallel equilibrium gives F_res = W sin θ = W h / L = 302 N. Target = 302 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ = 3.6/10 and zero net force to obtain 302 N (B).

items.stem: The diagram shows a shipyard launch block of weight 600 N moving at constant speed 3.5 m s⁻¹ down a greased timber way of slope length 12 m and height 6 m. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 600 × (6/12) = 300 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 1.05 × 10³ W. Target = 300 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 300 N (D).

items.stem: In a kinematics experiment over a level turf pitch, a sports-science test ball is launched at 42 m s⁻¹ and 55° above the horizontal. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the speed of the projectile at the highest point of its trajectory?
items.workedSolution: At the apex v_y = 0 while horizontal velocity remains constant at v_apex = u cos 55° = 24.1 m s⁻¹. Maximum height h_max = (u sin 55°)² / (2g) = 60.3 m. Target = 24.1 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_y = 0 and constant v_x = u cos 55° at apex to obtain 24.1 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Assumes the projectile is momentarily stationary at its highest point, forgetting its constant horizontal velocity u cos θ.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses u sin θ instead of u cos θ for the speed at the apex.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Assumes speed remains equal to launch speed u throughout the flight.

items.stem: The diagram shows cart X of mass 2 kg approaching stationary cart Y of mass 7.2 kg at 14 m s⁻¹ on a level low-friction dynamics rail. After impact, cart Y moves right at 4.66 m s⁻¹. How much kinetic energy is dissipated in this rebound collision?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (2)(14) = (2)v_X + (7.2)(4.66) gives v_X = -2.78 m s⁻¹ (2.78 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(2)(2.78)² + ½(7.2)(4.66)² = 85.9 J. Energy lost = 196 J − K_f = 110 J. Target = 110 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 2.78 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 110 J (D).

options.distractorRationale: Treats the rebounding kinetic energy of X as negative because v_X < 0, subtracting ½m_X v_X² instead of adding scalar kinetic energies.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Ignores the rebound kinetic energy of X completely after impact.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Reports total post-collision kinetic energy instead of kinetic energy lost.

items.stem: Along a frictionless optical-bench track, carriage X of mass 3.5 kg travelling right at 13 m s⁻¹ meets carriage Y of mass 3 kg travelling left at 4.5 m s⁻¹ (not drawn). After impact carriage Y rebounds right at 2.5 m s⁻¹. What is the post-collision velocity of carriage X?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward as positive: p_before = (3.5)(13) + (3)(−4.5) = 32.0 kg m s⁻¹. From p_before = (3.5)v_X + (3)(2.5), v_X = 7.00 m s⁻¹, which is 7.00 m s⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: Uses signed head-on momentum p_before = 32.0 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 7.00 m s⁻¹ to the right (D).

items.stem: The diagram shows a physics lecture bob of mass 1.1 kg released from a horizontal 2 m string in a light-string pendulum toward stationary a stationary putty sphere of mass 2.42 kg at the bottom. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the tension in the string immediately before a physics lecture bob strikes a stationary putty sphere?
items.workedSolution: Just before collision u² = 2gL => u = 6.26 m s⁻¹. Radial Newton second law T − mg = mu²/L = 2mg gives T = 3mg = 32.4 N. Momentum conservation gives v = mu/(m+M) = 1.96 m s⁻¹. Target = 32.4 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates quarter-swing dynamics and radial/tangential laws to obtain 32.4 N (D).

options.distractorRationale: Equates string tension at the bottom to static weight mg, forgetting upward centripetal force mv²/L = 2mg.

items.stem: The three-stage diagram shows a marine mooring weight of mass 8 kg dropped from rest at the support of a stretchable nylon hawser (natural length 1.8 m), reaching A taut and extending a further 0.45 m over 0.32 s to rest at lowest point B. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the spring constant of a stretchable nylon hawser?
items.workedSolution: Total vertical drop from release S to lowest point B is L + x = 1.8 + 0.45 = 2.25 m. By energy conservation mg(L + x) = ½kx², giving k = 2mg(L + x)/x² = 1.74 × 10³ N m⁻¹ and peak tension T_B = kx = 785 N. Target = 1.74 × 10³ N m⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses full vertical drop (1.8 + 0.45) m in mg(L + x) = ½kx² to obtain 1.74 × 10³ N m⁻¹ (B).

options.distractorRationale: Equates ½kx² to mgL instead of mg(L + x), forgetting the extra vertical drop x while the cord stretches.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of ½ in elastic potential energy E_e = ½kx².

items.stem: The diagram illustrates an instrumented drop sphere of mass 6 kg released at the support of an elastic bungee tether (natural length 4.6 m), becoming taut at A and decelerating to rest at B (extension 1.4 m) over 0.18 s. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What mean force does an elastic bungee tether exert between A and B?
items.workedSolution: Speed when taut at A: v_A = √(2 × 9.81 × 4.6) = 9.50 m s⁻¹ downward. Taking upward positive, (F_mean − mg)Δt = 0 − (−mv_A), so F_mean = mv_A / 0.18 + 6(9.81) = 376 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = mv_A with v_A = √(2gL) to obtain 376 N (C).

items.stem: A civil-engineering gabion (weight 700 N) slides at constant speed 4 m s⁻¹ down a planar test embankment, which is 12 m long and drops 6 m vertically. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 700 × (6/12) = 350 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 1.40 × 10³ W. Target = 350 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 350 N (D).

items.stem: Fired from a ground discharge tube at 26 m s⁻¹ and 56° above the horizontal, a tracer polymer pellet lands back on a horizontal test paddock. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What is the total time of flight before returning to a horizontal test paddock?
items.workedSolution: u_y = 26 sin 56° = 21.6 m s⁻¹ and u_x = 26 cos 56° = 14.5 m s⁻¹. Flight time T = 2u_y / 9.8 = 4.40 s; horizontal range R = u_x T = 64.0 m. Target = 4.40 s.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves orthogonal components accurately to obtain 4.40 s (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes time to reach the apex u sin θ / g rather than full time of flight.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Swaps sin θ and cos θ when resolving vertical launch speed.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses total speed u instead of vertical component u sin θ.

items.stem: Travelling at 10 m s⁻¹ to the right along a level docking-simulator rail, module X (3.6 kg) strikes stationary module Y (1.2 kg), sending module Y rightward at 8.93 m s⁻¹. What is the speed of module X immediately after the collision?
items.workedSolution: Momentum conservation: (3.6)(10) = (3.6)v_X + (1.2)(8.93), giving v_X = 7.02 m s⁻¹. K_i = 180 J and K_f = 137 J, so ΔK_lost = K_i − K_f = 43.4 J. Target = 7.02 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves linear momentum and evaluates kinetic energy budget to obtain 7.02 m s⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: Moving rightward at 11 m s⁻¹ on a polished ice test channel, sled X (1.2 kg) collides head-on with stationary sled Y (2.9 kg); immediately afterward sled Y travels right at 5.97 m s⁻¹ and sled X rebounds backward. What is the total kinetic energy of the two bodies immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (1.2)(11) = (1.2)v_X + (2.9)(5.97) gives v_X = -3.43 m s⁻¹ (3.43 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(1.2)(3.43)² + ½(2.9)(5.97)² = 58.7 J. Energy lost = 72.6 J − K_f = 13.9 J. Target = 58.7 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 3.43 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 58.7 J (B).

items.stem: Whirled in a vertical circle of radius 0.6 m on a thin braided string (breaking tension 95 N) in a lecture-hall whirl rig, a calibration ball has mass 2.2 kg. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. Determine the greatest safe speed at the lowest point.
items.workedSolution: Tension is greatest at the bottom where T_max − mg = m v_max² / r. Thus v_max = √[((95/2.2) − 9.81) × 0.6] = 4.47 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves T_max − mg = mv²/r to obtain 4.47 m s⁻¹ (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds g instead of subtracting g when rearranging T_max − mg = mv²/r.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats vertical circular motion as horizontal, omitting weight mg at the lowest point.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes minimum top-of-loop critical speed √(gr) instead of maximum safe bottom speed.

items.stem: In a vertical deceleration shaft, a payload shock capsule (14 kg) falls from rest at the support through the 3.2 m slack length of a compliant elastomer rope to point A and is brought momentarily to rest after stretching 0.6 m in a time of 0.3 s to B. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. Determine the time-averaged tension in a compliant elastomer rope during this 0.3 s interval.
items.workedSolution: Speed when taut at A: v_A = √(2 × 9.8 × 3.2) = 7.92 m s⁻¹ downward. Taking upward positive, (F_mean − mg)Δt = 0 − (−mv_A), so F_mean = mv_A / 0.3 + 14(9.8) = 507 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = mv_A with v_A = √(2gL) to obtain 507 N (D).

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, an articulated test coach of mass 1500 kg accelerates horizontally so a roof-mounted plumb sphere hangs at 18° to the vertical, later climbs a 8° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 50 m (static friction coefficient 0.8), and coasts from 17 m s⁻¹ against a 620 N resistive force toward the timing gate. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What is the horizontal acceleration during the initial straight-line phase when a roof-mounted plumb sphere deflects by 18°?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 18° = ma and T cos 18° = mg => a = g tan 18° = 3.18 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.8 × 9.8 × 50) = 19.8 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1500)(17)² / 620 = 350 m. Target = 3.18 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 3.18 m s⁻² (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses g sin θ as if on an inclined plane rather than resolving T sin θ = ma and T cos θ = mg to obtain g tan θ.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the ratio of horizontal to vertical components, evaluating g / tan θ instead of g tan θ.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies g by cos θ instead of tan θ.

items.stem: Sliding at constant velocity down a substation access slope of slope length 14 m and vertical drop 5.6 m, a transformer housing has weight 760 N. What is the magnitude of the resistive force opposing motion along the slope?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed ΔE_k = 0. Potential energy lost = W h = 760 × 5.6 = 4.26 × 10³ J. Parallel equilibrium gives F_res = W sin θ = W h / L = 304 N. Target = 304 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ = 5.6/14 and zero net force to obtain 304 N (A).

items.stem: Across a flat ash plain, a ground-level vent projects a volcanic ballistic clast with initial speed 34 m s⁻¹ at 38° above the horizontal. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What horizontal range does it cover before landing on a flat ash plain?
items.workedSolution: u_y = 34 sin 38° = 20.9 m s⁻¹ and u_x = 34 cos 38° = 26.8 m s⁻¹. Flight time T = 2u_y / 9.81 = 4.27 s; horizontal range R = u_x T = 114 m. Target = 114 m.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves orthogonal components accurately to obtain 114 m (D).

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes cos θ for sin θ in the flight-time expression.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses the 45° maximum-range formula u²/g without the angle factor sin(2θ).

items.stem: Projected from a deck-level launcher at 42 m s⁻¹ at an angle of 33° above calm water at launch level, a rescue line-throwing bob follows a parabolic arc. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the speed of the projectile at the highest point of its trajectory?
items.workedSolution: At the apex v_y = 0 while horizontal velocity remains constant at v_apex = u cos 33° = 35.2 m s⁻¹. Maximum height h_max = (u sin 33°)² / (2g) = 26.7 m. Target = 35.2 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_y = 0 and constant v_x = u cos 33° at apex to obtain 35.2 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Assumes the projectile is momentarily stationary at its highest point, forgetting its constant horizontal velocity u cos θ.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses u sin θ instead of u cos θ for the speed at the apex.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Assumes speed remains equal to launch speed u throughout the flight.

items.stem: On a smooth glass collision groove, lighter trolley X of mass 1.6 kg moving right at 16 m s⁻¹ strikes stationary heavier trolley Y of mass 3.8 kg, causing trolley Y to move right at 9.07 m s⁻¹ while trolley X rebounds to the left. How much kinetic energy is dissipated in this rebound collision?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (1.6)(16) = (1.6)v_X + (3.8)(9.07) gives v_X = -5.54 m s⁻¹ (5.54 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(1.6)(5.54)² + ½(3.8)(9.07)² = 181 J. Energy lost = 205 J − K_f = 23.9 J. Target = 23.9 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 5.54 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 23.9 J (B).

items.stem: On a polished ice test channel, sled X of mass 4 kg moves right at 8 m s⁻¹ toward sled Y of mass 1.2 kg approaching head-on to the left at 4.5 m s⁻¹ (initial arrow on Y omitted). Immediately after collision, sled Y moves right at 4 m s⁻¹. What is the velocity of sled X immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward as positive: p_before = (4)(8) + (1.2)(−4.5) = 26.6 kg m s⁻¹. From p_before = (4)v_X + (1.2)(4), v_X = 5.45 m s⁻¹, which is 5.45 m s⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: Uses signed head-on momentum p_before = 26.6 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 5.45 m s⁻¹ to the right (D).

items.stem: In a Charpy-style swing rig, a cast-iron hammer bob of mass 0.5 kg hangs on a 1.6 m string, is released from rest with the string horizontal, and collides inelastically at the bottom with stationary a deformable putty mass of mass 0.7 kg. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the tension in the string immediately before a cast-iron hammer bob strikes a deformable putty mass?
items.workedSolution: Just before collision u² = 2gL => u = 5.60 m s⁻¹. Radial Newton second law T − mg = mu²/L = 2mg gives T = 3mg = 14.7 N. Momentum conservation gives v = mu/(m+M) = 2.33 m s⁻¹. Target = 14.7 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates quarter-swing dynamics and radial/tangential laws to obtain 14.7 N (A).

items.stem: In a high-platform test rig, a bridge-jump test sandbag of mass 11 kg is released from rest at the anchor of an elastic shock cord of unstretched length 3.4 m. The cord becomes taut at A and stretches obeying Hooke's law by a maximum extension of 0.75 m over 0.36 s before a bridge-jump test sandbag comes momentarily to rest at B. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the spring constant of an elastic shock cord?
items.workedSolution: Total vertical drop from release S to lowest point B is L + x = 3.4 + 0.75 = 4.15 m. By energy conservation mg(L + x) = ½kx², giving k = 2mg(L + x)/x² = 1.59 × 10³ N m⁻¹ and peak tension T_B = kx = 1.19 × 10³ N. Target = 1.59 × 10³ N m⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses full vertical drop (3.4 + 0.75) m in mg(L + x) = ½kx² to obtain 1.59 × 10³ N m⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, a rail-yard test locomotive of mass 1000 kg accelerates horizontally so a roof-hung indicator sphere hangs at 26° to the vertical, later climbs a 12° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 95 m (static friction coefficient 0.45), and coasts from 19 m s⁻¹ against a 350 N resistive force toward the buffer platform. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the horizontal acceleration during the initial straight-line phase when a roof-hung indicator sphere deflects by 26°?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 26° = ma and T cos 26° = mg => a = g tan 26° = 4.78 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.45 × 9.81 × 95) = 20.5 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1000)(19)² / 350 = 516 m. Target = 4.78 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 4.78 m s⁻² (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses g sin θ as if on an inclined plane rather than resolving T sin θ = ma and T cos θ = mg to obtain g tan θ.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the ratio of horizontal to vertical components, evaluating g / tan θ instead of g tan θ.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies g by cos θ instead of tan θ.

items.stem: In translational equilibrium at constant speed, a steel cable drum cradle (weight 1520 N) travels 25 m down a warehouse ramp, dropping 12 m vertically. How much gravitational potential energy is lost over the full length of the slope?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed ΔE_k = 0. Potential energy lost = W h = 1520 × 12 = 1.82 × 10⁴ J. Parallel equilibrium gives F_res = W sin θ = W h / L = 730 N. Target = 1.82 × 10⁴ J.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ = 12/25 and zero net force to obtain 1.82 × 10⁴ J (A).

items.stem: While sliding down a planar service incline (22 m long, 7.7 m vertical height) at constant speed 6 m s⁻¹, a quarry stone skip of weight 200 N converts lost potential energy into heat. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 200 × (7.7/22) = 70.0 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 420 W. Target = 70.0 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 70.0 N (C).

items.stem: Referring to the launch of a tracer polymer pellet from a ground discharge tube at 42 m s⁻¹ and 24° above a horizontal test paddock: Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.8 m s⁻². What maximum vertical height above a horizontal test paddock does it reach?
items.workedSolution: At the apex v_y = 0 while horizontal velocity remains constant at v_apex = u cos 24° = 38.4 m s⁻¹. Maximum height h_max = (u sin 24°)² / (2g) = 14.9 m. Target = 14.9 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_y = 0 and constant v_x = u cos 24° at apex to obtain 14.9 m (B).

options.label: C

options.label: D
