items.stem: During an inelastic collision trial on a precision gas-bearing trough, rider X (mass 4 kg, initial rightward speed 6 m s⁻¹) hits stationary rider Y (mass 2 kg), which moves off to the right at 5.67 m s⁻¹. What is the speed of rider X immediately after the collision?
items.workedSolution: Momentum conservation: (4)(6) = (4)v_X + (2)(5.67), giving v_X = 3.17 m s⁻¹. K_i = 72.0 J and K_f = 52.2 J, so ΔK_lost = K_i − K_f = 19.8 J. Target = 3.17 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves linear momentum and evaluates kinetic energy budget to obtain 3.17 m s⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: During a head-on collision test on a smooth glass collision groove, trolley X (2.5 kg) moves right at 13 m s⁻¹ while trolley Y (3 kg) moves left at 6 m s⁻¹ (arrow omitted), and trolley Y exits right at 2 m s⁻¹. Find the velocity of trolley X right after collision.
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward as positive: p_before = (2.5)(13) + (3)(−6) = 14.5 kg m s⁻¹. From p_before = (2.5)v_X + (3)(2), v_X = 3.40 m s⁻¹, which is 3.40 m s⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: Uses signed head-on momentum p_before = 14.5 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 3.40 m s⁻¹ to the right (A).

items.stem: During a tensile limit test in a vertical circular test rig, a steel sensor sphere of mass 1 kg swings on a light inextensible wire of length 1.8 m rated to 40 N maximum tension. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². Calculate the maximum speed at the bottom of the path.
items.workedSolution: Tension is greatest at the bottom where T_max − mg = m v_max² / r. Thus v_max = √[((40/1) − 9.81) × 1.8] = 7.37 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves T_max − mg = mv²/r to obtain 7.37 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Adds g instead of subtracting g when rearranging T_max − mg = mv²/r.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Treats vertical circular motion as horizontal, omitting weight mg at the lowest point.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes minimum top-of-loop critical speed √(gr) instead of maximum safe bottom speed.

items.stem: During an impulse-arrest test in a stage gridiron support, a stunt-rig counterweight of mass 3 kg drops freely 2.8 m to taut point A and extends an elastic arrest cable by 0.6 m over 0.24 s until instantaneous rest at B. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². Calculate the mean upward cord force during deceleration.
items.workedSolution: Speed when taut at A: v_A = √(2 × 9.81 × 2.8) = 7.41 m s⁻¹ downward. Taking upward positive, (F_mean − mg)Δt = 0 − (−mv_A), so F_mean = mv_A / 0.24 + 3(9.81) = 122 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = mv_A with v_A = √(2gL) to obtain 122 N (A).

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, an airport baggage tractor of mass 1700 kg accelerates horizontally so a cab-mounted pendulum bob hangs at 18° to the vertical, later climbs a 10° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 70 m (static friction coefficient 0.45), and coasts from 19 m s⁻¹ against a 560 N resistive force toward the concourse stop. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the horizontal acceleration during the initial straight-line phase when a cab-mounted pendulum bob deflects by 18°?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 18° = ma and T cos 18° = mg => a = g tan 18° = 3.18 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.45 × 9.8 × 70) = 17.6 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1700)(19)² / 560 = 548 m. Target = 3.18 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 3.18 m s⁻² (D).

items.stem: The diagram shows a warehouse pallet box of weight 150 N moving at constant speed 3.5 m s⁻¹ down a gravity-brake ramp of slope length 28 m and height 8.4 m. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 150 × (8.4/28) = 45.0 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 158 W. Target = 45.0 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 45.0 N (A).

items.stem: The diagram shows a golf launch-monitor ball launched at 14 m s⁻¹ inclined at 26° to a level driving range. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.8 m s⁻². What horizontal range does it cover before landing on a level driving range?
items.workedSolution: u_y = 14 sin 26° = 6.14 m s⁻¹ and u_x = 14 cos 26° = 12.6 m s⁻¹. Flight time T = 2u_y / 9.8 = 1.25 s; horizontal range R = u_x T = 15.8 m. Target = 15.8 m.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves orthogonal components accurately to obtain 15.8 m (B).

items.stem: The diagram shows carriage X of mass 4.4 kg moving right at 6 m s⁻¹ toward stationary carriage Y of mass 1.6 kg on a frictionless optical-bench track; after collision, carriage Y travels right at 6.91 m s⁻¹. What is the speed of carriage X immediately after the collision?
items.workedSolution: Momentum conservation: (4.4)(6) = (4.4)v_X + (1.6)(6.91), giving v_X = 3.49 m s⁻¹. K_i = 79.2 J and K_f = 65.0 J, so ΔK_lost = K_i − K_f = 14.2 J. Target = 3.49 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves linear momentum and evaluates kinetic energy budget to obtain 3.49 m s⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: The diagram shows shuttle X of mass 0.8 kg approaching stationary shuttle Y of mass 2.4 kg at 8 m s⁻¹ on a horizontal magnetic-bearing guideway. After impact, shuttle Y moves right at 3.67 m s⁻¹. How much kinetic energy is dissipated in this rebound collision?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (0.8)(8) = (0.8)v_X + (2.4)(3.67) gives v_X = -3.01 m s⁻¹ (3.01 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(0.8)(3.01)² + ½(2.4)(3.67)² = 19.8 J. Energy lost = 25.6 J − K_f = 5.81 J. Target = 5.81 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 3.01 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 5.81 J (A).

items.stem: The diagram shows a brass impact sphere of mass 2.3 kg released from a horizontal 0.8 m string in a laboratory swing frame toward stationary a wax capture block of mass 5.06 kg at the bottom. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the tension in the string immediately before a brass impact sphere strikes a wax capture block?
items.workedSolution: Just before collision u² = 2gL => u = 3.96 m s⁻¹. Radial Newton second law T − mg = mu²/L = 2mg gives T = 3mg = 67.7 N. Momentum conservation gives v = mu/(m+M) = 1.24 m s⁻¹. Target = 67.7 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates quarter-swing dynamics and radial/tangential laws to obtain 67.7 N (B).

items.stem: The diagram shows a compact lead bob (0.8 kg) at the bottom of a vertical circle of radius 1.4 m in a vertical loop frame; a light steel cable has a maximum safe tension of 41 N. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the maximum allowed speed at this point?
items.workedSolution: Tension is greatest at the bottom where T_max − mg = m v_max² / r. Thus v_max = √[((41/0.8) − 9.81) × 1.4] = 7.62 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves T_max − mg = mv²/r to obtain 7.62 m s⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: The three-stage diagram shows a calibration steel ball of mass 10 kg dropped from rest at the support of a Hookean rubber cord (natural length 2.4 m), reaching A taut and extending a further 0.85 m over 0.24 s to rest at lowest point B. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the spring constant of a Hookean rubber cord?
items.workedSolution: Total vertical drop from release S to lowest point B is L + x = 2.4 + 0.85 = 3.25 m. By energy conservation mg(L + x) = ½kx², giving k = 2mg(L + x)/x² = 882 N m⁻¹ and peak tension T_B = kx = 749 N. Target = 882 N m⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses full vertical drop (2.4 + 0.85) m in mg(L + x) = ½kx² to obtain 882 N m⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, a heavy-duty rescue tender of mass 1700 kg accelerates horizontally so a suspended steel bob hangs at 34° to the vertical, later climbs a 10° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 95 m (static friction coefficient 0.55), and coasts from 14 m s⁻¹ against a 440 N resistive force toward the depot line. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the horizontal acceleration during the initial straight-line phase when a suspended steel bob deflects by 34°?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 34° = ma and T cos 34° = mg => a = g tan 34° = 6.62 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.55 × 9.81 × 95) = 22.6 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1700)(14)² / 440 = 379 m. Target = 6.62 m s⁻².

items.stem: Of weight 600 N, a freight container sled descends a dockyard unloading ramp at steady speed over a slope distance of 12 m through a vertical height change of 6.7 m. How much gravitational potential energy is lost over the full length of the slope?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed ΔE_k = 0. Potential energy lost = W h = 600 × 6.7 = 4.02 × 10³ J. Parallel equilibrium gives F_res = W sin θ = W h / L = 335 N. Target = 4.02 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ = 6.7/12 and zero net force to obtain 4.02 × 10³ J (D).

items.stem: A foundry ingot sled (weight 700 N) slides at constant speed 2 m s⁻¹ down a refractory cooling chute, which is 12 m long and drops 5.4 m vertically. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 700 × (5.4/12) = 315 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 630 W. Target = 315 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 315 N (B).

items.stem: A hail-impact test sphere leaves an angled gas gun at 42 m s⁻¹ inclined at 55° above the horizontal over a horizontal test hall. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What maximum vertical height above a horizontal test hall does it reach?
items.workedSolution: At the apex v_y = 0 while horizontal velocity remains constant at v_apex = u cos 55° = 24.1 m s⁻¹. Maximum height h_max = (u sin 55°)² / (2g) = 60.3 m. Target = 60.3 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_y = 0 and constant v_x = u cos 55° at apex to obtain 60.3 m (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Converts all initial kinetic energy into gravitational potential energy, forgetting non-zero horizontal speed u cos θ at the apex.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses horizontal component u cos θ instead of vertical component u sin θ in h = u_y² / (2g).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of two in the denominator of h_max = u_y² / (2g).

items.stem: Moving rightward at 13 m s⁻¹ on a level cleanroom linear rail, carrier X (0.8 kg) collides head-on with stationary carrier Y (2.2 kg); immediately afterward carrier Y travels right at 6.38 m s⁻¹ and carrier X rebounds backward. What is the total kinetic energy of the two bodies immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (0.8)(13) = (0.8)v_X + (2.2)(6.38) gives v_X = -4.55 m s⁻¹ (4.55 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(0.8)(4.55)² + ½(2.2)(6.38)² = 53.0 J. Energy lost = 67.6 J − K_f = 14.6 J. Target = 53.0 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 4.55 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 53.0 J (C).

items.stem: Along a polished ice test channel, sled X of mass 2.5 kg travelling right at 13 m s⁻¹ meets sled Y of mass 3.6 kg travelling left at 2 m s⁻¹ (not drawn). After impact sled Y rebounds right at 2.5 m s⁻¹. What is the post-collision velocity of sled X?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward as positive: p_before = (2.5)(13) + (3.6)(−2) = 25.3 kg m s⁻¹. From p_before = (2.5)v_X + (3.6)(2.5), v_X = 6.52 m s⁻¹, which is 6.52 m s⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: Uses signed head-on momentum p_before = 25.3 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 6.52 m s⁻¹ to the right (A).

items.stem: Held with its 1 m light string horizontal in a suspension test gantry, an instrumented pendulum mass (0.3 kg) swings down from rest and sticks to stationary a magnetic-latch block (0.66 kg) at the lowest point. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What is the speed of the coupled bodies immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Just before collision u² = 2gL => u = 4.43 m s⁻¹. Radial Newton second law T − mg = mu²/L = 2mg gives T = 3mg = 8.83 N. Momentum conservation gives v = mu/(m+M) = 1.38 m s⁻¹. Target = 1.38 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates quarter-swing dynamics and radial/tangential laws to obtain 1.38 m s⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: Released from rest at the support in a fall-arrest gantry, a rescue arrest dummy (11.5 kg) falls freely through the 3.4 m natural length of a braided dynamic lanyard to point A and then extends the Hookean cord by 1.15 m during 0.26 s to instantaneous rest at B. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What is the peak tension in a braided dynamic lanyard at the lowest point B?
items.workedSolution: Total vertical drop from release S to lowest point B is L + x = 3.4 + 1.15 = 4.55 m. By energy conservation mg(L + x) = ½kx², giving k = 2mg(L + x)/x² = 776 N m⁻¹ and peak tension T_B = kx = 893 N. Target = 893 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses full vertical drop (3.4 + 1.15) m in mg(L + x) = ½kx² to obtain 893 N (A).

items.stem: In an overhead hoist beam, a crane overload test block (13 kg) falls from rest at the support through the 3.4 m slack length of an elastic snubber line to point A and is brought momentarily to rest after stretching 1 m in a time of 0.24 s to B. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. Determine the time-averaged tension in an elastic snubber line during this 0.24 s interval.
items.workedSolution: Speed when taut at A: v_A = √(2 × 9.81 × 3.4) = 8.17 m s⁻¹ downward. Taking upward positive, (F_mean − mg)Δt = 0 − (−mv_A), so F_mean = mv_A / 0.24 + 13(9.81) = 570 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = mv_A with v_A = √(2gL) to obtain 570 N (D).

items.stem: Descending a crusty glacier slope of length 32 m and vertical drop 16 m at a steady speed of 2.5 m s⁻¹, an expedition supply sled has weight 1100 N. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 1100 × (16/32) = 550 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 1.38 × 10³ W. Target = 550 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 550 N (D).

items.stem: Across a flat proving ground, a calibrated ground launcher projects an acoustic ranging dart with initial speed 36 m s⁻¹ at 38° above the horizontal. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What horizontal range does it cover before landing on a flat proving ground?
items.workedSolution: u_y = 36 sin 38° = 22.2 m s⁻¹ and u_x = 36 cos 38° = 28.4 m s⁻¹. Flight time T = 2u_y / 9.8 = 4.52 s; horizontal range R = u_x T = 128 m. Target = 128 m.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves orthogonal components accurately to obtain 128 m (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies horizontal speed by ascent time u sin θ / g instead of full flight time 2u sin θ / g.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes cos θ for sin θ in the flight-time expression.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses the 45° maximum-range formula u²/g without the angle factor sin(2θ).

items.stem: On a polished ice test channel, sled X of mass 3.6 kg moves right at 13 m s⁻¹ and collides with stationary sled Y of mass 2.4 kg. Immediately after impact, sled Y moves right at 9.28 m s⁻¹. What is the speed of sled X immediately after the collision?
items.workedSolution: Momentum conservation: (3.6)(13) = (3.6)v_X + (2.4)(9.28), giving v_X = 6.81 m s⁻¹. K_i = 304 J and K_f = 187 J, so ΔK_lost = K_i − K_f = 117 J. Target = 6.81 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves linear momentum and evaluates kinetic energy budget to obtain 6.81 m s⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: On a level docking-simulator rail, lighter module X of mass 1 kg moving right at 12 m s⁻¹ strikes stationary heavier module Y of mass 2.8 kg, causing module Y to move right at 5.61 m s⁻¹ while module X rebounds to the left. How much kinetic energy is dissipated in this rebound collision?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (1)(12) = (1)v_X + (2.8)(5.61) gives v_X = -3.71 m s⁻¹ (3.71 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(1)(3.71)² + ½(2.8)(5.61)² = 50.9 J. Energy lost = 72.0 J − K_f = 21.1 J. Target = 21.1 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 3.71 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 21.1 J (A).

items.stem: In a vertical-plane spinner, a gyroscope test mass of mass 0.8 kg moves in a vertical circle of radius 1.6 m on a light radial tether, which snaps if tension exceeds 29 N. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the maximum speed a gyroscope test mass can have at the bottom without breaking a light radial tether?
items.workedSolution: Tension is greatest at the bottom where T_max − mg = m v_max² / r. Thus v_max = √[((29/0.8) − 9.81) × 1.6] = 6.50 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves T_max − mg = mv²/r to obtain 6.50 m s⁻¹ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Adds g instead of subtracting g when rearranging T_max − mg = mv²/r.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats vertical circular motion as horizontal, omitting weight mg at the lowest point.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes minimum top-of-loop critical speed √(gr) instead of maximum safe bottom speed.

items.stem: Dropped from rest at the anchor in a laboratory ceiling mount, a calibration steel ball of mass 11 kg falls freely 3.8 m until a Hookean rubber cord becomes taut at A, then stretches the cord by 0.6 m over 0.24 s to come momentarily to rest at B. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the mean upward force exerted by a Hookean rubber cord between A and B?
items.workedSolution: Speed when taut at A: v_A = √(2 × 9.8 × 3.8) = 8.63 m s⁻¹ downward. Taking upward positive, (F_mean − mg)Δt = 0 − (−mv_A), so F_mean = mv_A / 0.24 + 11(9.8) = 503 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = mv_A with v_A = √(2gL) to obtain 503 N (B).

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, an airport baggage tractor of mass 1300 kg accelerates horizontally so a cab-mounted pendulum bob hangs at 18° to the vertical, later climbs a 10° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 60 m (static friction coefficient 0.6), and coasts from 21 m s⁻¹ against a 620 N resistive force toward the concourse stop. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What is the maximum speed on the flat semicircular curve of radius 60 m without skidding?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 18° = ma and T cos 18° = mg => a = g tan 18° = 3.18 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.6 × 9.8 × 60) = 18.8 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1300)(21)² / 620 = 462 m. Target = 18.8 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 18.8 m s⁻¹ (B).

options.label: A

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Divides by μ_s instead of multiplying by μ_s.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes v² = μ_s g R without taking the square root.

items.stem: In translational equilibrium at constant speed, a turbine casing pallet (weight 1560 N) travels 21 m down a powerhouse access incline, dropping 10.1 m vertically. How much gravitational potential energy is lost over the full length of the slope?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed ΔE_k = 0. Potential energy lost = W h = 1560 × 10.1 = 1.58 × 10⁴ J. Parallel equilibrium gives F_res = W sin θ = W h / L = 750 N. Target = 1.58 × 10⁴ J.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ = 10.1/21 and zero net force to obtain 1.58 × 10⁴ J (D).

items.stem: During a range trial on a level demonstration track, a lecture-hall steel ball leaves a floor-mounted spring cannon at 38 m s⁻¹ and 60° above the horizontal. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the total time of flight before returning to a level demonstration track?
items.workedSolution: u_y = 38 sin 60° = 32.9 m s⁻¹ and u_x = 38 cos 60° = 19.0 m s⁻¹. Flight time T = 2u_y / 9.81 = 6.71 s; horizontal range R = u_x T = 127 m. Target = 6.71 s.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves orthogonal components accurately to obtain 6.71 s (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes time to reach the apex u sin θ / g rather than full time of flight.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Swaps sin θ and cos θ when resolving vertical launch speed.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses total speed u instead of vertical component u sin θ.

items.stem: Referring to the launch of an irrigation water packet from a ground-level nozzle at 15 m s⁻¹ and 37° above horizontal farmland: Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². What maximum vertical height above horizontal farmland does it reach?
items.workedSolution: At the apex v_y = 0 while horizontal velocity remains constant at v_apex = u cos 37° = 12.0 m s⁻¹. Maximum height h_max = (u sin 37°)² / (2g) = 4.15 m. Target = 4.15 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_y = 0 and constant v_x = u cos 37° at apex to obtain 4.15 m (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Converts all initial kinetic energy into gravitational potential energy, forgetting non-zero horizontal speed u cos θ at the apex.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses horizontal component u cos θ instead of vertical component u sin θ in h = u_y² / (2g).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of two in the denominator of h_max = u_y² / (2g).

items.stem: In a rebound impact on a smooth marshalling test track, wagon X (mass 1.8 kg, initial speed 9 m s⁻¹ right) hits stationary wagon Y (mass 6.1 kg), which moves right at 3.88 m s⁻¹. What is the total kinetic energy of the two bodies immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (1.8)(9) = (1.8)v_X + (6.1)(3.88) gives v_X = -4.15 m s⁻¹ (4.15 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(1.8)(4.15)² + ½(6.1)(3.88)² = 61.4 J. Energy lost = 72.9 J − K_f = 11.5 J. Target = 61.4 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 4.15 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 61.4 J (C).

items.stem: During a head-on collision test on a level docking-simulator rail, module X (1 kg) moves right at 10 m s⁻¹ while module Y (1.8 kg) moves left at 3.5 m s⁻¹ (arrow omitted), and module Y exits right at 2.5 m s⁻¹. Find the velocity of module X right after collision.
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward as positive: p_before = (1)(10) + (1.8)(−3.5) = 3.70 kg m s⁻¹. From p_before = (1)v_X + (1.8)(2.5), v_X = -0.800 m s⁻¹, which is 0.800 m s⁻¹ to the left.

markScheme.criterion: Uses signed head-on momentum p_before = 3.70 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 0.800 m s⁻¹ to the left (B).

items.stem: Swinging from rest through a quarter-circle of radius 1.4 m in a ballistic pendulum rig, a steel pendulum bob (mass 1.5 kg) couples on impact with stationary a lump of modelling clay (mass 2.1 kg). Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the speed of the coupled bodies immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Just before collision u² = 2gL => u = 5.24 m s⁻¹. Radial Newton second law T − mg = mu²/L = 2mg gives T = 3mg = 44.1 N. Momentum conservation gives v = mu/(m+M) = 2.18 m s⁻¹. Target = 2.18 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates quarter-swing dynamics and radial/tangential laws to obtain 2.18 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: Attached to an elastic recovery cord of unstretched length 3.4 m in a vertical test bay, an aerospace drop canister of mass 4 kg falls from rest at the anchor, passes taut point A, and stretches the cord by 0.75 m in 0.18 s to rest at B. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the peak tension in an elastic recovery cord at the lowest point B?
items.workedSolution: Total vertical drop from release S to lowest point B is L + x = 3.4 + 0.75 = 4.15 m. By energy conservation mg(L + x) = ½kx², giving k = 2mg(L + x)/x² = 578 N m⁻¹ and peak tension T_B = kx = 434 N. Target = 434 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses full vertical drop (3.4 + 0.75) m in mg(L + x) = ½kx² to obtain 434 N (B).

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, a mine-tunnel shuttle vehicle of mass 1300 kg accelerates horizontally so a ceiling pendulum sensor hangs at 22° to the vertical, later climbs a 12° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 75 m (static friction coefficient 0.6), and coasts from 15 m s⁻¹ against a 470 N resistive force toward the shaft station. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the horizontal acceleration during the initial straight-line phase when a ceiling pendulum sensor deflects by 22°?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 22° = ma and T cos 22° = mg => a = g tan 22° = 3.96 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.6 × 9.81 × 75) = 21.0 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1300)(15)² / 470 = 311 m. Target = 3.96 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 3.96 m s⁻² (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses g sin θ as if on an inclined plane rather than resolving T sin θ = ma and T cos θ = mg to obtain g tan θ.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the ratio of horizontal to vertical components, evaluating g / tan θ instead of g tan θ.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies g by cos θ instead of tan θ.

items.stem: The diagram depicts a mining equipment skid weighing 1720 N moving at constant speed down a straight haulage incline of length 18 m and vertical height 9.4 m. What is the magnitude of the resistive force opposing motion along the slope?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed ΔE_k = 0. Potential energy lost = W h = 1720 × 9.4 = 1.62 × 10⁴ J. Parallel equilibrium gives F_res = W sin θ = W h / L = 898 N. Target = 898 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ = 9.4/18 and zero net force to obtain 898 N (D).

items.stem: The diagram shows a heavy logistics crate of weight 950 N moving at constant speed 5.5 m s⁻¹ down a rough warehouse ramp of slope length 18 m and height 8.1 m. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 950 × (8.1/18) = 428 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 2.35 × 10³ W. Target = 428 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 428 N (C).

items.stem: In a kinematics experiment over a flat proving ground, an acoustic ranging dart is launched at 33 m s⁻¹ and 62° above the horizontal. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the speed of the projectile at the highest point of its trajectory?
items.workedSolution: At the apex v_y = 0 while horizontal velocity remains constant at v_apex = u cos 62° = 15.5 m s⁻¹. Maximum height h_max = (u sin 62°)² / (2g) = 43.3 m. Target = 15.5 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_y = 0 and constant v_x = u cos 62° at apex to obtain 15.5 m s⁻¹ (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Assumes the projectile is momentarily stationary at its highest point, forgetting its constant horizontal velocity u cos θ.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses u sin θ instead of u cos θ for the speed at the apex.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Assumes speed remains equal to launch speed u throughout the flight.

items.stem: The diagram shows glider X of mass 4.8 kg moving right at 8 m s⁻¹ toward stationary glider Y of mass 1.6 kg on a horizontal frictionless air track; after collision, glider Y travels right at 8.05 m s⁻¹. What is the speed of glider X immediately after the collision?
items.workedSolution: Momentum conservation: (4.8)(8) = (4.8)v_X + (1.6)(8.05), giving v_X = 5.32 m s⁻¹. K_i = 154 J and K_f = 120 J, so ΔK_lost = K_i − K_f = 33.9 J. Target = 5.32 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves linear momentum and evaluates kinetic energy budget to obtain 5.32 m s⁻¹ (B).

options.distractorRationale: Assumes both bodies stick together instead of using the measured post-collision speed of Y.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Adds m_Y v_Y instead of subtracting m_Y v_Y when solving momentum conservation.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Assumes kinetic energy is conserved in an inelastic collision.

items.stem: Along a smooth marshalling test track, wagon X of mass 3.5 kg travelling right at 8 m s⁻¹ meets wagon Y of mass 3.6 kg travelling left at 2.5 m s⁻¹ (not drawn). After impact wagon Y rebounds right at 1.5 m s⁻¹. What is the post-collision velocity of wagon X?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward as positive: p_before = (3.5)(8) + (3.6)(−2.5) = 19.0 kg m s⁻¹. From p_before = (3.5)v_X + (3.6)(1.5), v_X = 3.89 m s⁻¹, which is 3.89 m s⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: Uses signed head-on momentum p_before = 19.0 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 3.89 m s⁻¹ to the right (A).

items.stem: The diagram shows a telemetry capsule (3 kg) at the bottom of a vertical circle of radius 2.2 m in a vertical rotation stand; a high-tensile cord has a maximum safe tension of 130 N. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the maximum allowed speed at this point?
items.workedSolution: Tension is greatest at the bottom where T_max − mg = m v_max² / r. Thus v_max = √[((130/3) − 9.81) × 2.2] = 8.59 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves T_max − mg = mv²/r to obtain 8.59 m s⁻¹ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Adds g instead of subtracting g when rearranging T_max − mg = mv²/r.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats vertical circular motion as horizontal, omitting weight mg at the lowest point.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes minimum top-of-loop critical speed √(gr) instead of maximum safe bottom speed.

items.stem: The diagram illustrates a mountaineering test mass of mass 10 kg released at the support of a dynamic climbing rope (natural length 1.8 m), becoming taut at A and decelerating to rest at B (extension 0.8 m) over 0.21 s. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What mean force does a dynamic climbing rope exert between A and B?
items.workedSolution: Speed when taut at A: v_A = √(2 × 9.81 × 1.8) = 5.94 m s⁻¹ downward. Taking upward positive, (F_mean − mg)Δt = 0 − (−mv_A), so F_mean = mv_A / 0.21 + 10(9.81) = 381 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = mv_A with v_A = √(2gL) to obtain 381 N (A).

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, an instrumented test truck of mass 1200 kg accelerates horizontally so a ceiling-suspended plumb bob hangs at 30° to the vertical, later climbs a 14° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 75 m (static friction coefficient 0.75), and coasts from 20 m s⁻¹ against a 500 N resistive force toward the terminal bay. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the horizontal acceleration during the initial straight-line phase when a ceiling-suspended plumb bob deflects by 30°?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 30° = ma and T cos 30° = mg => a = g tan 30° = 5.66 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.75 × 9.8 × 75) = 23.5 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1200)(20)² / 500 = 480 m. Target = 5.66 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 5.66 m s⁻² (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses g sin θ as if on an inclined plane rather than resolving T sin θ = ma and T cos θ = mg to obtain g tan θ.

options.label: B

options.label: C

items.stem: A steel ballast box (weight 1350 N) slides at constant speed 4 m s⁻¹ down a braking test slope, which is 12 m long and drops 7.2 m vertically. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 1350 × (7.2/12) = 810 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 3.24 × 10³ W. Target = 810 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 810 N (A).

items.stem: Fired from a spring-loaded catapult at 34 m s⁻¹ and 26° above the horizontal, a robotics arena sphere lands back on a level arena floor. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What is the total time of flight before returning to a level arena floor?
items.workedSolution: u_y = 34 sin 26° = 14.9 m s⁻¹ and u_x = 34 cos 26° = 30.6 m s⁻¹. Flight time T = 2u_y / 9.8 = 3.04 s; horizontal range R = u_x T = 93.0 m. Target = 3.04 s.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves orthogonal components accurately to obtain 3.04 s (B).

options.label: A

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Swaps sin θ and cos θ when resolving vertical launch speed.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses total speed u instead of vertical component u sin θ.

items.stem: Travelling at 12 m s⁻¹ to the right along a horizontal magnetic-bearing guideway, shuttle X (3.6 kg) strikes stationary shuttle Y (2.8 kg), sending shuttle Y rightward at 10.08 m s⁻¹. What is the speed of shuttle X immediately after the collision?
items.workedSolution: Momentum conservation: (3.6)(12) = (3.6)v_X + (2.8)(10.08), giving v_X = 4.16 m s⁻¹. K_i = 259 J and K_f = 173 J, so ΔK_lost = K_i − K_f = 85.8 J. Target = 4.16 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves linear momentum and evaluates kinetic energy budget to obtain 4.16 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: Moving rightward at 10 m s⁻¹ on a frictionless optical-bench track, carriage X (1.2 kg) collides head-on with stationary carriage Y (3.1 kg); immediately afterward carriage Y travels right at 5.32 m s⁻¹ and carriage X rebounds backward. What is the total kinetic energy of the two bodies immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (1.2)(10) = (1.2)v_X + (3.1)(5.32) gives v_X = -3.74 m s⁻¹ (3.74 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(1.2)(3.74)² + ½(3.1)(5.32)² = 52.3 J. Energy lost = 60.0 J − K_f = 7.72 J. Target = 52.3 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 3.74 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 52.3 J (A).

items.stem: Held with its 0.6 m light string horizontal in a pivot suspension rig, a tungsten alloy sphere (1.7 kg) swings down from rest and sticks to stationary a stationary capture cup (3.06 kg) at the lowest point. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What is the speed of the coupled bodies immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Just before collision u² = 2gL => u = 3.43 m s⁻¹. Radial Newton second law T − mg = mu²/L = 2mg gives T = 3mg = 50.0 N. Momentum conservation gives v = mu/(m+M) = 1.23 m s⁻¹. Target = 1.23 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates quarter-swing dynamics and radial/tangential laws to obtain 1.23 m s⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: Whirled in a vertical circle of radius 1.2 m on a light inextensible string (breaking tension 33 N) in a circular motion demonstrator, a polymer-coated mass has mass 1.4 kg. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. Determine the greatest safe speed at the lowest point.
items.workedSolution: Tension is greatest at the bottom where T_max − mg = m v_max² / r. Thus v_max = √[((33/1.4) − 9.81) × 1.2] = 4.06 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves T_max − mg = mv²/r to obtain 4.06 m s⁻¹ (A).

options.label: B

options.label: C

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes minimum top-of-loop critical speed √(gr) instead of maximum safe bottom speed.

items.stem: Released from rest at the support in a vertical deceleration shaft, a payload shock capsule (5.5 kg) falls freely through the 2.4 m natural length of a compliant elastomer rope to point A and then extends the Hookean cord by 1.35 m during 0.16 s to instantaneous rest at B. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What is the peak tension in a compliant elastomer rope at the lowest point B?
items.workedSolution: Total vertical drop from release S to lowest point B is L + x = 2.4 + 1.35 = 3.75 m. By energy conservation mg(L + x) = ½kx², giving k = 2mg(L + x)/x² = 222 N m⁻¹ and peak tension T_B = kx = 299 N. Target = 299 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses full vertical drop (2.4 + 1.35) m in mg(L + x) = ½kx² to obtain 299 N (C).

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, an electric quarry haulage rig of mass 1500 kg accelerates horizontally so a suspended brass bob hangs at 26° to the vertical, later climbs a 8° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 75 m (static friction coefficient 0.65), and coasts from 15 m s⁻¹ against a 590 N resistive force toward the weighbridge. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What is the horizontal acceleration during the initial straight-line phase when a suspended brass bob deflects by 26°?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 26° = ma and T cos 26° = mg => a = g tan 26° = 4.78 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.65 × 9.81 × 75) = 21.9 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1500)(15)² / 590 = 286 m. Target = 4.78 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 4.78 m s⁻² (A).

items.stem: Sliding at constant velocity down a planar ski run of slope length 16 m and vertical drop 4.5 m, a snowcat maintenance sled has weight 520 N. What is the magnitude of the resistive force opposing motion along the slope?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed ΔE_k = 0. Potential energy lost = W h = 520 × 4.5 = 2.34 × 10³ J. Parallel equilibrium gives F_res = W sin θ = W h / L = 146 N. Target = 146 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ = 4.5/16 and zero net force to obtain 146 N (C).

items.stem: Projected from a pneumatic pitching machine at 27 m s⁻¹ at an angle of 28° above a level turf pitch, a sports-science test ball follows a parabolic arc. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the speed of the projectile at the highest point of its trajectory?
items.workedSolution: At the apex v_y = 0 while horizontal velocity remains constant at v_apex = u cos 28° = 23.8 m s⁻¹. Maximum height h_max = (u sin 28°)² / (2g) = 8.19 m. Target = 23.8 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_y = 0 and constant v_x = u cos 28° at apex to obtain 23.8 m s⁻¹ (A).

options.label: B

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses u sin θ instead of u cos θ for the speed at the apex.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Assumes speed remains equal to launch speed u throughout the flight.

items.stem: On a level low-friction dynamics rail, lighter cart X of mass 0.8 kg moving right at 10 m s⁻¹ strikes stationary heavier cart Y of mass 2.1 kg, causing cart Y to move right at 5.09 m s⁻¹ while cart X rebounds to the left. How much kinetic energy is dissipated in this rebound collision?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (0.8)(10) = (0.8)v_X + (2.1)(5.09) gives v_X = -3.36 m s⁻¹ (3.36 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(0.8)(3.36)² + ½(2.1)(5.09)² = 31.7 J. Energy lost = 40.0 J − K_f = 8.28 J. Target = 8.28 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 3.36 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 8.28 J (A).

items.stem: On a frictionless optical-bench track, carriage X of mass 4 kg moves right at 10 m s⁻¹ toward carriage Y of mass 3.6 kg approaching head-on to the left at 4.5 m s⁻¹ (initial arrow on Y omitted). Immediately after collision, carriage Y moves right at 2.5 m s⁻¹. What is the velocity of carriage X immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward as positive: p_before = (4)(10) + (3.6)(−4.5) = 23.8 kg m s⁻¹. From p_before = (4)v_X + (3.6)(2.5), v_X = 3.70 m s⁻¹, which is 3.70 m s⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: Uses signed head-on momentum p_before = 23.8 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 3.70 m s⁻¹ to the right (C).

items.stem: In a light-string pendulum, a physics lecture bob of mass 1.9 kg hangs on a 1.8 m string, is released from rest with the string horizontal, and collides inelastically at the bottom with stationary a stationary putty sphere of mass 2.66 kg. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the tension in the string immediately before a physics lecture bob strikes a stationary putty sphere?
items.workedSolution: Just before collision u² = 2gL => u = 5.94 m s⁻¹. Radial Newton second law T − mg = mu²/L = 2mg gives T = 3mg = 55.9 N. Momentum conservation gives v = mu/(m+M) = 2.48 m s⁻¹. Target = 55.9 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates quarter-swing dynamics and radial/tangential laws to obtain 55.9 N (C).

items.stem: In a dry-test tower, a marine mooring weight of mass 12 kg is released from rest at the anchor of a stretchable nylon hawser of unstretched length 2.2 m. The cord becomes taut at A and stretches obeying Hooke's law by a maximum extension of 1.35 m over 0.32 s before a marine mooring weight comes momentarily to rest at B. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the spring constant of a stretchable nylon hawser?
items.workedSolution: Total vertical drop from release S to lowest point B is L + x = 2.2 + 1.35 = 3.55 m. By energy conservation mg(L + x) = ½kx², giving k = 2mg(L + x)/x² = 459 N m⁻¹ and peak tension T_B = kx = 619 N. Target = 459 N m⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses full vertical drop (2.2 + 1.35) m in mg(L + x) = ½kx² to obtain 459 N m⁻¹ (B).

options.distractorRationale: Equates ½kx² to mgL instead of mg(L + x), forgetting the extra vertical drop x while the cord stretches.

options.label: C

options.label: D

items.stem: Dropped from rest at the anchor in a drop-test tower, an instrumented drop sphere of mass 7 kg falls freely 2 m until an elastic bungee tether becomes taut at A, then stretches the cord by 1.3 m over 0.27 s to come momentarily to rest at B. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the mean upward force exerted by an elastic bungee tether between A and B?
items.workedSolution: Speed when taut at A: v_A = √(2 × 9.81 × 2) = 6.26 m s⁻¹ downward. Taking upward positive, (F_mean − mg)Δt = 0 − (−mv_A), so F_mean = mv_A / 0.27 + 7(9.81) = 231 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = mv_A with v_A = √(2gL) to obtain 231 N (D).

items.stem: While sliding down a planar test embankment (28 m long, 9.8 m vertical height) at constant speed 4.5 m s⁻¹, a civil-engineering gabion of weight 1500 N converts lost potential energy into heat. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 1500 × (9.8/28) = 525 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 2.36 × 10³ W. Target = 525 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 525 N (D).

options.label: B

items.stem: During a range trial on a horizontal test paddock, a tracer polymer pellet leaves a ground discharge tube at 30 m s⁻¹ and 30° above the horizontal. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the total time of flight before returning to a horizontal test paddock?
items.workedSolution: u_y = 30 sin 30° = 15.0 m s⁻¹ and u_x = 30 cos 30° = 26.0 m s⁻¹. Flight time T = 2u_y / 9.8 = 3.06 s; horizontal range R = u_x T = 79.5 m. Target = 3.06 s.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves orthogonal components accurately to obtain 3.06 s (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes time to reach the apex u sin θ / g rather than full time of flight.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Swaps sin θ and cos θ when resolving vertical launch speed.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses total speed u instead of vertical component u sin θ.

items.stem: During an inelastic collision trial on a level docking-simulator rail, module X (mass 2.8 kg, initial rightward speed 6 m s⁻¹) hits stationary module Y (mass 2.8 kg), which moves off to the right at 4.57 m s⁻¹. What is the speed of module X immediately after the collision?
items.workedSolution: Momentum conservation: (2.8)(6) = (2.8)v_X + (2.8)(4.57), giving v_X = 1.43 m s⁻¹. K_i = 50.4 J and K_f = 32.1 J, so ΔK_lost = K_i − K_f = 18.3 J. Target = 1.43 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves linear momentum and evaluates kinetic energy budget to obtain 1.43 m s⁻¹ (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Assumes both bodies stick together instead of using the measured post-collision speed of Y.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds m_Y v_Y instead of subtracting m_Y v_Y when solving momentum conservation.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Assumes kinetic energy is conserved in an inelastic collision.

items.stem: In a rebound impact on a polished ice test channel, sled X (mass 2 kg, initial speed 13 m s⁻¹ right) hits stationary sled Y (mass 7.2 kg), which moves right at 4.33 m s⁻¹. What is the total kinetic energy of the two bodies immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (2)(13) = (2)v_X + (7.2)(4.33) gives v_X = -2.59 m s⁻¹ (2.59 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(2)(2.59)² + ½(7.2)(4.33)² = 74.2 J. Energy lost = 169 J − K_f = 94.8 J. Target = 74.2 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 2.59 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 74.2 J (D).

items.stem: During a tensile limit test in a lecture-hall whirl rig, a calibration ball of mass 2.8 kg swings on a thin braided string of length 1 m rated to 99 N maximum tension. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². Calculate the maximum speed at the bottom of the path.
items.workedSolution: Tension is greatest at the bottom where T_max − mg = m v_max² / r. Thus v_max = √[((99/2.8) − 9.81) × 1] = 5.05 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves T_max − mg = mv²/r to obtain 5.05 m s⁻¹ (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds g instead of subtracting g when rearranging T_max − mg = mv²/r.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats vertical circular motion as horizontal, omitting weight mg at the lowest point.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes minimum top-of-loop critical speed √(gr) instead of maximum safe bottom speed.

items.stem: During an impulse-arrest test in a vertical deceleration shaft, a payload shock capsule of mass 12 kg drops freely 1.8 m to taut point A and extends a compliant elastomer rope by 1.3 m over 0.18 s until instantaneous rest at B. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.8 m s⁻². Calculate the mean upward cord force during deceleration.
items.workedSolution: Speed when taut at A: v_A = √(2 × 9.8 × 1.8) = 5.94 m s⁻¹ downward. Taking upward positive, (F_mean − mg)Δt = 0 − (−mv_A), so F_mean = mv_A / 0.18 + 12(9.8) = 514 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = mv_A with v_A = √(2gL) to obtain 514 N (A).

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, an articulated test coach of mass 1800 kg accelerates horizontally so a roof-mounted plumb sphere hangs at 30° to the vertical, later climbs a 12° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 95 m (static friction coefficient 0.65), and coasts from 15 m s⁻¹ against a 470 N resistive force toward the timing gate. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the horizontal acceleration during the initial straight-line phase when a roof-mounted plumb sphere deflects by 30°?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 30° = ma and T cos 30° = mg => a = g tan 30° = 5.66 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.65 × 9.8 × 95) = 24.6 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1800)(15)² / 470 = 431 m. Target = 5.66 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 5.66 m s⁻² (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses g sin θ as if on an inclined plane rather than resolving T sin θ = ma and T cos θ = mg to obtain g tan θ.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the ratio of horizontal to vertical components, evaluating g / tan θ instead of g tan θ.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies g by cos θ instead of tan θ.

items.stem: The diagram depicts a transformer housing weighing 560 N moving at constant speed down a substation access slope of length 34 m and vertical height 20.4 m. What is the magnitude of the resistive force opposing motion along the slope?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed ΔE_k = 0. Potential energy lost = W h = 560 × 20.4 = 1.14 × 10⁴ J. Parallel equilibrium gives F_res = W sin θ = W h / L = 336 N. Target = 336 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ = 20.4/34 and zero net force to obtain 336 N (A).

items.stem: On a horizontal frictionless air track, glider X of mass 4 kg moves to the right at 12 m s⁻¹ and collides head-on with glider Y of mass 1.2 kg moving to the left at 2.5 m s⁻¹ (arrow on Y not shown). Immediately after impact, glider Y moves to the right at 5 m s⁻¹. Take motion to the right as positive.
items.workedSolution: (a) p_before = 4 × 12 + 1.2 × (−2.5) = 45.0 kg m s⁻¹. Answer: 45.0 kg m s⁻¹ to the right. (b) v_X = (45.0 − 1.2 × 5) / 4 = 9.75 m s⁻¹. Answer: 9.75 m s⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates m_X u_X − m_Y |u_Y| with correct signs.
Obtains 45.0 kg m s⁻¹ to the right.

items.workedSolution: (a) v_apex = 36 × cos 33°. Answer: 30.2 m s⁻¹. (b) u_y = 36 × sin 33° = 19.6 m s⁻¹. h_max = u_y² / (2 × 9.81). Answer: 19.6 m. (c) T = 2u_y / 9.81 = 4.00 s. R = 30.2 × T. Answer: 121 m.

items.workedSolution: (a) p_before = 2.5 × 7 + 3 × (−2.5) = 10.0 kg m s⁻¹. Answer: 10.0 kg m s⁻¹ to the right. (b) v_X = (10.0 − 3 × 2) / 2.5 = 1.60 m s⁻¹. Answer: 1.60 m s⁻¹ to the right.

items.workedSolution: (a) v_apex = 27 × cos 55°. Answer: 15.5 m s⁻¹. (b) u_y = 27 × sin 55° = 22.1 m s⁻¹. h_max = u_y² / (2 × 9.8). Answer: 25.0 m. (c) T = 2u_y / 9.8 = 4.51 s. R = 15.5 × T. Answer: 69.9 m.

markScheme.criterion: Recognizes v_y = 0 at apex so v_apex = u cos θ.

items.stem: On a level low-friction dynamics rail, cart X of mass 3.5 kg moves to the right at 11 m s⁻¹ and collides head-on with cart Y of mass 1.8 kg moving to the left at 5.5 m s⁻¹ (arrow on Y not shown). Immediately after impact, cart Y moves to the right at 5.5 m s⁻¹. Take motion to the right as positive.
items.workedSolution: (a) p_before = 3.5 × 11 + 1.8 × (−5.5) = 28.6 kg m s⁻¹. Answer: 28.6 kg m s⁻¹ to the right. (b) v_X = (28.6 − 1.8 × 5.5) / 3.5 = 5.34 m s⁻¹. Answer: 5.34 m s⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates m_X u_X − m_Y |u_Y| with correct signs.
Obtains 28.6 kg m s⁻¹ to the right.
Solves p_before = m_X v_X + m_Y v_Y for v_X.
Obtains 5.34 m s⁻¹ to the right.

items.workedSolution: (a) p_before = 3.5 × 8 + 3 × (−2.5) = 20.5 kg m s⁻¹. Answer: 20.5 kg m s⁻¹ to the right. (b) v_X = (20.5 − 3 × 1.5) / 3.5 = 4.57 m s⁻¹. Answer: 4.57 m s⁻¹ to the right.

items.stem: Released from rest at the anchor of an elastic shock cord (natural length 3 m) in a high-platform test rig, a bridge-jump test sandbag of mass 11 kg falls freely to point A where the cord becomes taut, then stretches the cord by 1 m over 0.3 s before reaching instantaneous rest at B. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) v_A = √(2 × 9.8 × 3). Answer: 7.67 m s⁻¹. (b) Mean resultant upward force = (11 × 7.67) / 0.3 = 281 N. F_mean = 281 + 11 × 9.8. Answer: 389 N. (c) T_B = 2 × 11 × 9.8 × (3 + 1) / 1. Answer: 862 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = m v_A, including weight mg.
Uses mg(L + x) = ½kx² and T_B = kx.

items.stem: Released from rest at the anchor of a braided dynamic lanyard (natural length 3.6 m) in a fall-arrest gantry, a rescue arrest dummy of mass 13 kg falls freely to point A where the cord becomes taut, then stretches the cord by 1.3 m over 0.24 s before reaching instantaneous rest at B. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = m v_A, including weight mg.
Uses mg(L + x) = ½kx² and T_B = kx.

items.stem: On a precision gas-bearing trough, rider X of mass 2.5 kg moves to the right at 13 m s⁻¹ and collides head-on with rider Y of mass 1.8 kg moving to the left at 4.5 m s⁻¹ (arrow on Y not shown). Immediately after impact, rider Y moves to the right at 3 m s⁻¹. Take motion to the right as positive.
items.workedSolution: (a) p_before = 2.5 × 13 + 1.8 × (−4.5) = 24.4 kg m s⁻¹. Answer: 24.4 kg m s⁻¹ to the right. (b) v_X = (24.4 − 1.8 × 3) / 2.5 = 7.60 m s⁻¹. Answer: 7.60 m s⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates m_X u_X − m_Y |u_Y| with correct signs.
Obtains 24.4 kg m s⁻¹ to the right.
Solves p_before = m_X v_X + m_Y v_Y for v_X.
Obtains 7.60 m s⁻¹ to the right.

items.stem: During proving-ground tests, a harbour container carrier of mass 1300 kg accelerates along a level straight so a suspended mass indicator deflects by 22° from the vertical, climbs a straight 8° incline at constant speed, negotiates a flat semicircular curve of radius 40 m (coefficient of static friction 0.55), and finally coasts along the semicircle from 14 m s⁻¹ against a constant 470 N resistance toward the berth checkpoint. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Uses T sin θ = ma and T cos θ = mg => a = g tan θ.
Applies μ_s mg = m v_max² / R.
Subtracts resistive work F_res(πR) from initial kinetic energy ½mu².

parts.prompt: By resolving forces on a suspended mass indicator, calculate the horizontal acceleration when the string deflects by 22°.

items.stem: Launched from a spring-loaded catapult across a level arena floor, a robotics arena sphere has an initial speed of 36 m s⁻¹ at 28° above the horizontal. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance.
items.workedSolution: (a) v_apex = 36 × cos 28°. Answer: 31.8 m s⁻¹. (b) u_y = 36 × sin 28° = 16.9 m s⁻¹. h_max = u_y² / (2 × 9.8). Answer: 14.6 m. (c) T = 2u_y / 9.8 = 3.45 s. R = 31.8 × T. Answer: 110 m.

markScheme.criterion: Recognizes v_y = 0 at apex so v_apex = u cos θ.

items.workedSolution: (a) p_before = 3 × 11 + 4.2 × (−5.5) = 9.90 kg m s⁻¹. Answer: 9.90 kg m s⁻¹ to the right. (b) v_X = (9.90 − 4.2 × 3.5) / 3 = -1.60 m s⁻¹. Answer: 1.60 m s⁻¹ to the left.

items.stem: On a horizontal frictionless air track, glider X of mass 4 kg moves to the right at 10 m s⁻¹ and collides head-on with glider Y of mass 3.6 kg moving to the left at 4 m s⁻¹ (arrow on Y not shown). Immediately after impact, glider Y moves to the right at 5 m s⁻¹. Take motion to the right as positive.
items.workedSolution: (a) p_before = 4 × 10 + 3.6 × (−4) = 25.6 kg m s⁻¹. Answer: 25.6 kg m s⁻¹ to the right. (b) v_X = (25.6 − 3.6 × 5) / 4 = 1.90 m s⁻¹. Answer: 1.90 m s⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates m_X u_X − m_Y |u_Y| with correct signs.
Obtains 25.6 kg m s⁻¹ to the right.
Solves p_before = m_X v_X + m_Y v_Y for v_X.
Obtains 1.90 m s⁻¹ to the right.

items.stem: During proving-ground tests, a rail-yard test locomotive of mass 1400 kg accelerates along a level straight so a roof-hung indicator sphere deflects by 26° from the vertical, climbs a straight 10° incline at constant speed, negotiates a flat semicircular curve of radius 40 m (coefficient of static friction 0.6), and finally coasts along the semicircle from 20 m s⁻¹ against a constant 380 N resistance toward the buffer platform. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Uses T sin θ = ma and T cos θ = mg => a = g tan θ.
Applies μ_s mg = m v_max² / R.
Subtracts resistive work F_res(πR) from initial kinetic energy ½mu².

items.stem: Launched from a tee on flat ground across a level driving range, a golf launch-monitor ball has an initial speed of 36 m s⁻¹ at 24° above the horizontal. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) v_apex = 36 × cos 24°. Answer: 32.9 m s⁻¹. (b) u_y = 36 × sin 24° = 14.6 m s⁻¹. h_max = u_y² / (2 × 9.8). Answer: 10.9 m. (c) T = 2u_y / 9.8 = 2.99 s. R = 32.9 × T. Answer: 98.3 m.

markScheme.criterion: Recognizes v_y = 0 at apex so v_apex = u cos θ.

items.stem: On a smooth glass collision groove, trolley X of mass 3.5 kg moves to the right at 13 m s⁻¹ and collides head-on with trolley Y of mass 1.2 kg moving to the left at 6 m s⁻¹ (arrow on Y not shown). Immediately after impact, trolley Y moves to the right at 4.5 m s⁻¹. Take motion to the right as positive.
items.workedSolution: (a) p_before = 3.5 × 13 + 1.2 × (−6) = 38.3 kg m s⁻¹. Answer: 38.3 kg m s⁻¹ to the right. (b) v_X = (38.3 − 1.2 × 4.5) / 3.5 = 9.40 m s⁻¹. Answer: 9.40 m s⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates m_X u_X − m_Y |u_Y| with correct signs.
Obtains 38.3 kg m s⁻¹ to the right.
Solves p_before = m_X v_X + m_Y v_Y for v_X.
Obtains 9.40 m s⁻¹ to the right.
